findings.suggestion: Catch the order-verify failure and show 'Could not verify this listing right now — refresh or check OpenSea' with the raw detail behind a collapsible.

findings.title: The identical 5-step tour re-fires for every collection
findings.evidence: After completing the Nakamigos tour, entering Jungle Bay immediately showed the same 'Gallery / Floor / Wallet / Cart / Keyboard Shortcuts' tour with only the collection name swapped (junglebay_onboarded, gnssart_onboarded are separate localStorage keys). Three identical tours in one session.
findings.suggestion: Key onboarding once per marketplace, not per collection; per-collection tours only if a step is actually collection-specific.

findings.title: Tour steps 1, 2, 4, 5 are centered modals that don't point at the feature they describe
findings.evidence: Step 3 'Wallet' correctly anchors beside the Connect button with a focus ring, but 'Gallery', 'Floor/Listings', 'Cart' and 'Keyboard Shortcuts' float dead-center with no spotlight on the Gallery tab / cart icon / Keys button.
findings.suggestion: Anchor every step to its control like step 3 already does.

findings.title: Disconnected chat is a dead room: no seeded content, no recent-activity fallback, tiny fixed-height message area
findings.evidence: 'Welcome to Nakamigos Chat / Be the first to start a conversation' with '1 online' (just me). The message panel is ~300px tall on a 1308px viewport with ~60% of the page empty dark space below; Alpha/Discussion filters also empty. Nothing pulls a visitor in.
findings.suggestion: Additively inject live marketplace events (sales/listings from the ticker) as system messages, show total members not just online, and let the message panel flex to fill the viewport.

findings.title: No watchlist feature anywhere (assignment expected one; competitors all have it)
findings.evidence: Searched More menu (P2P Trades, Favorites, Chat, History, Whales, About), header icons (theme/notifications/cart/connect) and the NFT detail modal — no watch/star control. localStorage has nakamigos_price_alerts:[] but no UI was found to add a per-token price alert either (NotificationCenter only has collection-level floor alerts).
findings.suggestion: Add a per-token watch + price-alert entry point on cards and in the detail modal, feeding the existing smart-alerts engine.

findings.title: Inconsistent owner counts between tabs (5,238 vs 5,212) and the All-time-vol stat card appears/disappears
findings.evidence: First gallery load: floor 0.1048, owners 5,238, '52.2K ETH all-time vol' card present. Re-visit minutes later: floor 0.1045, owners 5,212, vol card GONE (3 stat cards instead of 4). Floor tab consistently says 5,212.
findings.suggestion: Use one cached stats source per session; don't drop the vol card when the fetch fails.

findings.title: Rug-to-Riches timeline out of chronological order
findings.evidence: 'May 2022 — Otherside Land Acquired' renders above 'Nov 2021 — Sandbox Land Secured' in an otherwise ascending timeline (Nov 2021 → Jan 2022 → ... → 2023 → 2024 → Present).
findings.suggestion: Sort timeline entries by date.

findings.title: Share card watermark points to 'nakamigos.gallery' — not this app's domain
findings.evidence: The PNG share card footer reads 'nakamigos.gallery' (zoomed capture); the app lives at tegridyfarms.vercel.app/nakamigos. Anyone receiving the shared card has no path back to your marketplace (or lands on a domain you may not own).
findings.suggestion: Watermark with the real marketplace URL.

findings.title: eth.llamarpc.com is down (521) and is retried on every page
findings.evidence: OPTIONS https://eth.llamarpc.com/ → 521 captured repeatedly across chat, gallery, hub. No user-visible breakage observed (failover works) but it adds dead requests on every load.
findings.suggestion: Drop or demote llamarpc in the transport list / use the existing provider-failover ranking.

findings.title: 404 works but costs a full splash and offers only 'Back to Home'
findings.evidence: /nakamigos/nakamigos/not-a-real-tab → splash (~12s + click) → clean '404 Page Not Found' with Back to Home (goes to /nakamigos hub, verified). /nakamigos/fakecollection/gallery → same generic 404 with title 'Not Found | Tradermigos' — it doesn't say the collection doesn't exist nor list the 3 valid collections.
findings.suggestion: Skip splash on 404, and on bad-collection URLs show 'Collection not found' plus the three valid collection cards.

findings.title: Theme cycler is a mystery-meat button (cycles default → midnight → gold silently)
findings.evidence: The diamond icon cycles themes on click with only a hover title ('Theme: midnight') as feedback; clicking it first looked like a bug (a starfield suddenly appeared page-wide). No menu/toast names the active theme.
findings.suggestion: Small dropdown or toast ('Theme: Midnight') on change; keep the cycle behavior as the fast path.

findings.title: Card images pop in 5-10s late with no shimmer — first card sometimes never loads
findings.evidence: On first floor load all 12 cards showed dark voids with only the OpenSea badge for ~10s before images appeared; during the dev pass and the onboarding pass, card #10219 stayed an 'N' placeholder while its 11 siblings loaded.
findings.suggestion: Add skeleton shimmer to the image area and retry failed thumbnails.

findings.title: About pages and chat strand 50-60% of the ultrawide viewport
findings.evidence: JB/GNSS About hero text is a ~600px column pinned left with the right two-thirds of the screen empty; chat is a short full-width strip with the bottom half of the page bare background; the hub centers 3 cards with very wide dark gutters. Grids (6 cards/row) use the width well by contrast.
findings.suggestion: On >2000px viewports, let About pull its stats/timeline beside the hero text (two-column) and let chat fill vertical space; no content removal needed.

findings.title: Dotted separator line above the footer reads as a debug border
findings.evidence: A full-width dashed/dotted bright line renders above the footer on every tab (visible in every screenshot at varying y positions). It looks like an unfinished CSS border rather than a designed divider.
findings.suggestion: Soften to a low-opacity solid hairline or themed gradient.

findings.title: Empty-state microcopy 'No notifications in price' / 'in whale' is awkward
findings.evidence: Switching the Price and Whale tabs shows literal 'No notifications in price' / 'No notifications in whale'.
findings.suggestion: 'No price alerts yet — set thresholds in settings' per tab.

findings.title: Rank badge '#17/20,000' on favorite cards reads like a token number
findings.evidence: Card 'Nakamigos #5' wears a top-left badge '#17/20,000' (title='Rank 17 of 20,000') — two different #numbers on one card confuses; in the modal the same badge is correctly labeled 'RANK #17'.
findings.suggestion: Use the 'RANK #17' label style on cards too.

findings.title: Good guidance copy but no CTA button
findings.evidence: 'No Nakamigos favorites yet — Click the heart on any Nakamigos NFT to save it here.' has no 'Browse Gallery' button, and the broken Gallery nav makes acting on the tip harder.
findings.suggestion: Add a Browse Gallery CTA button to the empty state.

findings.title: Several species show 'Supply TBD'
findings.evidence: Cipr, Duqe, Genj, Naion, Que, Soco, Yami, Zuur cards all read 'Supply TBD' while others have exact 'beings' counts.
findings.suggestion: Backfill the counts (collection is fully minted, so they're knowable).

findings.title: Biggest gaps vs best-in-class on these page types
findings.evidence: Observed across the session: no per-token activity feed in the modal beyond the tiny price-history sparkline; no collection-level volume chart; offers section loads 20s+ with unlabeled skeleton rows; no 'sweep' in Lite mode (exists in Pro on dev); no notification delivery channel hint (alerts are local-only while the tab is open); nav buttons are <button> not <a> so middle-click/open-in-new-tab fails everywhere.
findings.suggestion: Highest-leverage additions: real <a> hrefs on nav tabs, owner/activity tab in the modal, and a 'where do alerts arrive' note in Alert Settings.

good: Document titles are excellent and per-page once inside ('Nakamigos - Chat | Tradermigos', 'Jungle Bay Ape Club - About | Tradermigos', 'Nakamigos - 404 | Tradermigos').

Alert Settings is a real feature: floor drop/rise %, underpriced, whale (buy count + window), volume spike, listing-rate surge, cooldown, quiet hours — all persisting per-collection to localStorage with no server round-trips.

About pages are best-in-class content: Jungle Bay's rug-to-riches expandable timeline, 20 legendary 1/1 cards with working Find-in-Gallery, skin tier pyramid, ecosystem map, Did-You-Know; GNSS's species encyclopedia with inline-expanding species cards.

live:naka-social.splashAndTransitions: Splash: visually impressive card-collage with TRADERMIGOS branding, but it plays on EVERY full page load (including reloads seconds apart and 404 routes), takes ~9-14s before 'CLICK TO ENTER' becomes actionable, requires a manual click every time, and its '20,000 WORKS / ERC-721' stats are Nakamigos-specific even when deep-linking into Jungle Bay (5,555) or GNSS (9,697) — cross-collection bleed at the splash level. After the click there's a further ~5-8s of near-black skeleton before content paints, so a cold deep-link to chat costs ~20s. In-app transitions by contrast are excellent: tab-to-tab swaps are instant with no spinner jank, header/ticker persist, and back-to-hub does not replay the splash. Skeletons: listing grids show flat dark voids (no shimmer) and images pop in 5-10s late; offer rows are anonymous gray bars for 20s+. Sound: toggle bottom-left + 'm' shortcut, state persists (nakamigos_sound_muted); icon swaps on toggle (audio output itself not verifiable from this harness). Page transition feel overall: the PageTransition layer is fine — the splash gate is the single biggest UX tax in the marketplace.
live:naka-social.consoleAndNetwork: Console: zero errors or exceptions captured across the full prod session (chat, gallery, favorites, hub, junglebay, gnssart, 404s) and the dev check. Network: https://eth.llamarpc.com/ OPTIONS → 521 recurring on every page (endpoint down; app survives via failover); https://nft2-cdn.alchemy.com/eth-mainnet/4c08e2...89d → 503 (broken NFT image CDN asset, correlates with the detail-modal placeholder bug); /api/alchemy?endpoint=getNFTMetadata&contractAddress=0xd774...c367&tokenId=20 observed stuck 'pending' for the gallery spotlight. Offers data in detail modals takes ~20s+ to resolve (unlabeled skeleton rows until then). No 4xx/5xx from the app's own /api/ routes were observed. Note: the extension's network log clears on navigation, so per-page coverage is best-effort.

Connect Wallet modal (opened + closed, no wallet selected)
Keyboard-shortcuts overlay + sound toggle + theme cycler
localhost:5173 dev cross-check (floor, gallery button, NFT detail modal)

findings.title: Detail view shows no image and no traits for most tokens (un-enriched cache, no per-token fetch)
findings.evidence: Modal for #18156, #0 and #777 shows the 'N #' placeholder permanently; JS inspection: '.modal-image-side .modal-image-wrap' contains NO element at all. #777 (opened via hub search and via fresh /nft/777 deep link) also shows 'No traits available for this token' while the SAME token's grid card renders its image fine. Traits header elsewhere admits '(based on 40/20,000 loaded)'. The single-NFT evaluation page objective (see the art, see the traits) fails for any token outside the lazily-enriched subset.
findings.suggestion: On modal open, fire an on-demand per-token metadata fetch (Alchemy getNFTMetadata) and, as an instant fallback, reuse the already-loaded grid thumbnail URL. Reproduced at HEAD on dev for un-enriched tokens, so not fixed.

findings.title: Gallery navigation is dead: nav button AND 'G' hotkey route to Listings instead of /gallery
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Gallery' (twice, including via accessibility ref) leaves URL at /nakamigos/nakamigos/ with title 'Nakamigos - Listings'; pressing the documented 'G — Go to Gallery' shortcut does the same. Direct URL /nakamigos/nakamigos/gallery loads a fully working Gallery page. Reproduced identically on localhost:5173 (HEAD) — the gallery route handler navigates to the wrong path.
findings.suggestion: Fix the shared goToGallery navigation function to push /gallery; both entry points clearly share it.

findings.title: ?token= deep links are stripped during splash click-through — shared token links never open the token
findings.evidence: Fresh load of https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app/nakamigos/nakamigos?token=18156 → splash → after CLICK TO ENTER the URL becomes /nakamigos/nakamigos with modalOpen=false (verified via JS on prod AND dev). In-session browsing generates exactly this ?token= URL format (e.g. /gallery?token=0), so copied browser URLs break for recipients. Path-based /nakamigos/nakamigos/nft/777 DOES survive the splash and opens the modal (normalized to /nft/777?token=777).
findings.suggestion: Preserve the query string through the splash-enter transition, or canonicalize all in-app token URLs to the /nft/:id path form that already survives.

findings.title: Order book bid side is nonsense data and the copy contradicts itself ('-4071.3%' spread called 'narrow'/'Healthy')
findings.evidence: Panel shows BEST BID 4.2800 ETH vs BEST ASK 0.1026 ETH, 'Spread -4.1774 (-4071.5%)', bid ladder 4.2350 → 3.6050 ETH on a 0.10-floor collection, and the verdict line 'SPREAD -4.1774 ETH (-4071.3%) ● Healthy — Strong buying interest near floor. Price gap is narrow (-4071.3%), suggesting healthy trading.' Meanwhile every listing card on the same page says 'Best offer: 0.0994'. A 4.28 ETH bid against a 0.10 ask would be instant-arb; the bid feed is mis-parsed or demo data mixed with live asks.
findings.suggestion: Validate the offers source (criteria/qty-scaled WETH offers being read as unit price?), and gate the 'Healthy' verdict on spread sanity (negative spread should read as data error, never 'narrow').

findings.title: 'Rank: Best First' and 'Rank: Highest #' sorts are silent no-ops
findings.evidence: Selecting rank-asc returns the exact same first six tokens in the same order and prices as price-asc (#17129 0.1026, #10219 0.1045, #16971 0.1046, #14540 0.1050, #14388 0.1052, #17885 0.1055); no rank badges on cards. Rank data exists — the #0 detail modal shows a 'RANK #791' badge.
findings.suggestion: Wire the sort to the rank field that the modal already displays, or show a 'rank data loading' state instead of silently falling back.

findings.title: Three skeleton bars in OFFERS never resolve (latched loading state)
findings.evidence: On prod, modals for #18156, #0 and #777 all show 3 grey rows with class="skeleton" and empty innerHTML below BEST OFFER, still pulsing after 60+ seconds. On dev (#16971) skeletons=0, so it may be fixed at HEAD or data-dependent — worth verifying before closing.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the offers query to either rows or an explicit 'No other offers' empty state.

findings.title: 'Make Offer' button beside the Buy CTA is clipped to 34px ('Mak' / 'Ma')
findings.evidence: Button with textContent 'Make Offer' measures width:34px next to 'Connect Wallet to Buy'/'Buy for 0.1046 ETH'; visually renders as 'Mak'. Reproduced on prod and dev (HEAD), every token tested. A second '+ Make Offer' button lower in OFFERS works, so the clipped one is redundant AND broken-looking.
findings.suggestion: Give the secondary button flex-shrink:0 / min-width, or an icon-only variant with a tooltip.

findings.title: Intermittent 429s on /api/opensea best-offer calls and 400s on the collections/<slug>/stats path
findings.evidence: Observed live: /api/opensea?path=offers%2Fcollection%2Fnakamigos%2Fnfts%2F14854%2Fbest → 429 (sibling call 200). Performance API across the session: 27 /api/ calls — 2× 429, 2× 400 on /api/opensea?path=collections%2Fnakamigos%2Fstats, rest 200 at 150–1441ms. No total data blackout (prior incident's failure mode not reproduced), but per-NFT offer calls are getting rate-limited and the stats call is malformed/rejected.
findings.suggestion: Batch/cache per-NFT best-offer lookups server-side; fix the stats path (the 400 is the likely cause of the missing volume — next finding).

findings.title: VOLUME shows an em dash on all three collection cards
findings.evidence: Nakamigos, GNSS Art, and Jungle Bay cards all render 'VOLUME —' while FLOOR/OWNERS/SUPPLY are real (0.1026 ETH / 5,212 / 20,000 etc.). Correlates with the repeated 400 on /api/opensea?path=collections/nakamigos/stats. The stats bar is the landing page's main trust signal.
findings.suggestion: Fix the stats endpoint call; fallback to indexer/Alchemy volume if OpenSea rejects the path.

findings.title: Mandatory click-gate splash replays on EVERY page load and costs 10–20s per visit
findings.evidence: Timed: dark first paint ~1s → collage builds → 'CLICK TO ENTER' appears at ~5s on first load but took 12–15s on several later loads (clicks before that are swallowed); after the click there is a further 4–6s near-black fade before content. Reload without clearing storage replays it identically (no sessionStorage gate, no 'don't show again'), including on deep links to /listings, /collection, /nft/777. The art itself (floating card collage, glitch effects) is genuinely beautiful.
findings.suggestion: Keep the art but: auto-enter after the build animation (make the click optional), gate replays per session, and start data-fetching/preloading the app behind the splash so the post-click black fade disappears.

findings.title: Escape closes the UNDERLYING modal first, orphaning the fullscreen viewer
findings.evidence: From fullscreen view of #18156: first Escape removed ?token from the URL and closed the detail modal while the fullscreen overlay (bottom bar, TRAITS panel, dark backdrop) stayed up over the grid; a second Escape was needed to dismiss the viewer.
findings.suggestion: Close the topmost overlay first (standard layered-dialog stack).

findings.title: Trait counts/percentages computed from the partial loaded sample read as wrong rarity data
findings.evidence: Gallery sidebar trait values show '0%' (e.g. 'Backwards Cap Blue 0% 7'); filtering by it yields '17 results of 20,000 items' (true count is likely hundreds — only ~1,680 tokens were loaded); modal traits show 'Flat 32 (80.0%)' based on 40/20,000 loaded next to a spotlight card saying the true '1,076 exist (5.38%)'. The honest '(based on N/20,000 loaded)' disclosure exists but the numbers still mislead.
findings.suggestion: Use the full-collection trait counts (the Traits page type-cards and spotlight cards already have real totals) for percentages, and label filtered results 'X of loaded sample' explicitly.

findings.title: Gallery 'Search by name or token ID' fails for any token not yet loaded, with a message-less empty state
findings.evidence: Typing 5000 → '0 results of 20,000 items' and a grid of ghost skeleton cards, no 'no results' text or CTA — even though token 5000 exists and the hub search finds #1234 in all three collections instantly.
findings.suggestion: Fall back to direct token-ID lookup (the hub search already does this) and add a real empty state ('No match in loaded items — press Enter to open token #5000').

findings.page: Floor vs Gallery vs loading states
findings.title: Floor price and owners differ across surfaces within minutes
findings.evidence: Floor tab: 0.1026 ETH / 5,212 owners; Gallery hero same session: 0.1045 ETH; /listings loading state briefly: 0.1048 / 5,238 owners before settling back to 0.1026 / 5,212. Two different sources (OpenSea listings vs Alchemy floor) are shown without reconciliation.
findings.suggestion: Pick one canonical floor source per screen or label the source (the listings page already has the 'via OpenSea' badge pattern).

findings.title: Stats bar shows '—' for floor/owners/supply for ~10s while the sweep panel already has floor data
findings.evidence: On switching to Jungle Bay: FLOOR PRICE/OWNERS/SUPPLY all '—' with LISTED 152 and MEDIAN/AVG filled; sweep panel simultaneously showed 'FLOOR IMPACT 0.0887 → 0.0899'. Stats populated ~11s later (0.0886/1,990/5,555).
findings.suggestion: Hydrate the stats bar from the listings payload immediately and reconcile when Alchemy responds; or show skeleton shimmer instead of em dashes (dash reads as 'no data exists').

findings.title: Inconsistent image sourcing: raw ipfs.io full-res for some cards causes slow loads and black re-flashes
findings.evidence: Most cards use res.cloudinary.com/alchemyapi 250px thumbs (fast); some (e.g. #10219) use https://ipfs.io/ipfs/Qm... at 2000px — that card went black again on every grid re-render (sort change, filter). 2 of 120 cards (#17129, #434) sat on the 'N' placeholder for minutes until background enrichment found their image.
findings.suggestion: Normalize all grid images through the Alchemy thumbnail CDN; keep IPFS only as last-resort fallback.

findings.title: Ultrawide (1912px CSS viewport) leaves large dead zones
findings.evidence: Listings: 4-column grid + sweep panel ends ~1200px, right ~700px is dimmed background art; Gallery hero has a near-empty band between hero and the marquee rows; About is a ~600px left-aligned text column against an empty right half. The Traits page (3-column category board) is the one surface that uses the width well.
findings.suggestion: Additive: allow 6–8 grid columns at >1600px, dock the order-book panel open by default on ultrawide, add a right-rail module (recent sales / rarity spotlight) on About and Gallery hero. Keep all existing art/sections.

findings.title: Images pop in with no fade and skeleton card geometry doesn't match loaded cards
findings.evidence: Lazy-loaded images swap from black to full art in one frame; the /listings loading state renders 7 narrow skeleton columns that become 4 wide columns + sweep panel on load (layout jump).
findings.suggestion: 120ms opacity fade on image load; make skeleton grid mirror the real grid template.

findings.title: Bottom bar duplicates the token id
findings.evidence: Reads 'Nakamigos #18156   #18156' (name already contains the id, then the id repeats in grey).
findings.suggestion: Drop the duplicate, or replace with the trait-count/rank.

findings.title: Theme-cycle button aria-label never updates and hub search ignores Escape
findings.evidence: After two cycles (midnight starfield → royal gold) the button still reports 'Current theme: default. Click to cycle.'; in the hub search, Escape leaves the suggestion dropdown open (the X button works).
findings.suggestion: Update the label with the active theme name; close dropdown on Escape.

findings.title: Notifications popover anchors far left of the bell
findings.evidence: Bell sits at x≈628 (screenshot px); the popover renders at x≈370–670, hovering over the sales ticker rather than under the bell.
findings.suggestion: Anchor to the trigger with right-alignment.

findings.title: Listed-Only results don't show prices on cards
findings.evidence: With 'Listed Only' + trait filter active ('4 results of 20,000 items'), cards #429/#547/#595/#1159 show trait subtitles but no ETH price — you must switch to the Floor tab to see what they cost.
findings.suggestion: Surface the listing price badge on gallery cards when Listed Only is on.

findings.title: DEMO badge appears in the hub header with no explanation
findings.evidence: Header shows '* DEMO' on the hub and on early collection loads, later replaced by '● LIVE' + sales ticker; no tooltip or copy explains what is demo vs live (relevant given the demo-looking order-book bids).
findings.suggestion: Tooltip stating exactly which data is simulated, or remove the badge once all surfaces are live.

findings.title: No comparable-sales / similar-tokens module on the detail view
findings.evidence: The modal has price history, offers, traits, and chain info, but nothing like Blur/OpenSea's 'more from this collection' or trait-floor comparables ('cheapest other Human Coffee'), even though the trait spotlight card already knows '1,076 exist (5.38%)'.
findings.suggestion: Add a small comparables strip (same rarest trait, sorted by price) — data already exists in the trait drill-down views.

good: Zero console errors across the entire session (hub, 3 collections, gallery, traits, about, modals, theme switching) — exceptionally clean runtime.

Failures observed: (1) HTTP 429 on /api/opensea?path=offers/collection/nakamigos/nfts/14854/best (sibling 12293 call returned 200) plus 2 more 429s in the performance log — per-NFT best-offer calls are being rate-limited intermittently (~7% of sampled calls), echoing the prior rate-limiter incident in milder form; (2) HTTP 400 twice on /api/opensea?path=collections/nakamigos/stats — consistent, likely the cause of 'VOLUME —' on all hub cards. No 5xx seen. Image CDNs: Alchemy Cloudinary thumbs fast; raw ipfs.io fetches slow (2000px, re-fetch on re-render).

findings.title: Infinite scroll yanks the user back to the top on every page append
findings.evidence: VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:115-122 — `const tokensKey = tokens.length + "-" + (tokens[0]?.id ?? ""); useEffect(() => { if (prevKeyRef.current && prevKeyRef.current !== tokensKey) { if (parentRef.current) parentRef.current.scrollTop = 0; } ... }, [tokensKey]);`. The key includes tokens.length, so a loadMore append (40→80 tokens, same first id) changes the key exactly like a filter change and resets scrollTop to 0. The load-more effect (lines 139-148) fires 5 rows from the bottom, so every page-2+ load while scrolling jumps the viewport to the top. Reachable on Nakamigos/gnssart/junglebay (all >1000 supply, so useNfts.js:84-98 auto-load is disabled and pagination is scroll-driven).
findings.suggestion: Reset scroll only when the change is a filter/sort (e.g. compare first AND last token id, or have Gallery pass an explicit `resetKey` derived from activeFilters/sortBy/search instead of inferring from tokens.length).

findings.title: Column count frozen at the default 4 — ResizeObserver never attaches because first render is the skeleton branch
findings.evidence: VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:41-46 — `useEffect(() => { recalc(); const ro = new ResizeObserver(recalc); if (containerRef.current) ro.observe(containerRef.current); ... }, [recalc, containerRef]);` with recalc=useCallback([containerRef, viewMode]). On mount, loading=true/tokens=[] (useNfts.js:7-8) so the component returns the SkeletonGrid branch (lines 150-162) which never attaches `ref={parentRef}` — observe() is skipped and recalc() no-ops. When data arrives the ref attaches but the effect deps haven't changed, so columns stays at `useState(4)` (line 30) until the user toggles view mode or remounts the tab. On a 390px iPhone that renders `repeat(4, 1fr)` (~85px-wide cards at 340px row height); inline style, no CSS override (App.css only collapses .gallery-layout, not the inner row grid).
findings.suggestion: Use a ref-callback that (re)attaches the ResizeObserver when the node appears, or add `loading`/`tokens.length>0` to the effect deps so it re-runs once the scroll container exists.

findings.title: Gallery price sort and price-range filter operate on a price field that is always null — price filter returns zero results, price sort is a no-op
findings.evidence: api.js normalizeToken:123 sets `price: null` and nothing ever merges listing prices into useNfts tokens (useNfts.js takes no listings input; App.jsx:580 passes `tokens={nfts.tokens}` raw). Yet constants.js:86-87 exposes `{ value: "price", label: "Price: High → Low" }` / `price-asc` in the gallery sort dropdown (sorted at useNfts.js:153-154 via `(b.price || 0) - (a.price || 0)` — all zeros), and FilterSidebar's Min/Max ETH inputs feed Gallery.jsx:52-59 `if (p === 0 || p === null || p === undefined) return false;` — with every p null, ANY price range filters out the entire collection and shows the "No NFTs Match These Filters" empty state. Listed-prices exist in the `listings` prop (used for listedOnly at Gallery.jsx:47-50) but are never joined onto tokens.
findings.suggestion: Merge listings prices into tokens (a Map join in Gallery or useNfts using the already-available `listings` prop) so price sort/filter work, and gallery cards gain price display for free (Card/VirtualCard already render nft.price when non-null).

findings.title: Filter sidebar accordion + trait-search state wiped every time a new token page loads
findings.evidence: FilterSidebar.jsx:403-407 — `useEffect(() => { setExpanded(new Set()); setTraitSearch({}); setHoveredRow(null); }, [traitFilters]);` with the comment "(i.e., new collection loaded)". But useNfts.js:49 calls `setTraitFilters(extractTraitFilters(all))` with a brand-new array on EVERY appended page, so during scroll pagination the user's expanded accordions and in-trait searches collapse repeatedly. Collection switches already remount the whole tree (App.jsx:184 `key={collectionSlug}`), so this reset effect only ever fires spuriously.
findings.suggestion: Drop the effect (remount already handles collection changes) or key it on collection.slug instead of the traitFilters array identity.

findings.title: Trait rarity percentages divide loaded-sample counts by full supply — every trait reads <5% and shows the gold 'rare' color until the whole collection loads
findings.evidence: FilterSidebar.jsx:571 `const pct = totalTokens > 0 ? parseFloat((v.count / totalTokens * 100).toFixed(1)) : 0;` where totalTokens = totalSupply (Gallery.jsx:68 `totalSupply || allTokens?.length`, App.jsx:597 passes stats.supply) but v.count comes only from loaded tokens (extractTraitFilters over loaded pages). With 40-80 of 20,000 Nakamigos loaded, every value computes ~0.1-0.4% → rarityColor(pct<5)="var(--gold)" (lines 4-8) paints ALL traits as ultra-rare. TraitExplorer.jsx:397-402 explicitly fixed this same bug ("dividing by full supply would understate every trait's incidence... Sample incidence is the unbiased estimate") — FilterSidebar was not given the fix.
findings.suggestion: Divide by the loaded-token count like TraitExplorer does (with its "~" sampled marker), keeping supply only for the absolute count column.

findings.title: "View in Gallery" species deep-link navigates with a ?species= param that nothing reads — button silently does nothing useful
findings.evidence: SpeciesEncyclopedia.jsx:327-329 `navigate(`/nakamigos/gnssart/gallery?species=${encodeURIComponent(speciesName)}`)`. A repo-wide grep for `species` shows no consumer: App.jsx only reads the `token` search param (App.jsx:282,293) and parseRoute ignores the query string entirely. The user lands on the unfiltered gallery. Compare JungleBayShowcase/CharacterTypeExplorer which correctly use the onFilterGallery callback (App.jsx:647).
findings.suggestion: Pass an onFilterGallery prop through About.jsx (it already exists for JungleBay at About.jsx) and call nfts.changeFilter with the species trait key, or implement reading ?species= in the gallery.

findings.title: Nakamigos metadataBase/<id>.png fallback URL verifiably 404s, yet three code paths still emit it — broken-image flash plus per-card metadata fetch burst on the sales grid
findings.evidence: Verified live: `curl -I https://alchemy.mypinata.cloud/ipfs/QmaN1jRPtmzeqhp6s3mR1SRK4q1xWPvFvwqW1jyN6trir9/1.png` → 404 (gnss assets.mgxs.co/1.png → 200 image/png, junglebay ipfs path → 206 image/png). Listings.jsx:167-172's own comment says "No deterministic image URL exists (Nakamigos metadata points at per-token IPFS CIDs)" and leaves listing images null — but recentSales (Listings.jsx:239-246) still sets `image: token?.image || fallbackImg` with `fallbackImg = `${collection.metadataBase}/${a.token.id}.png``, listedNfts imageLarge uses the same fullResImg (lines 161-163,175), and api.js normalizeToken:105-108 uses it as last-resort `fallbackImage`. Sales cards aren't flagged imagePending (Listings.jsx:784 `noSelfFetch={nft.imagePending}` — undefined for sales objects), so each 404 fires NftImage.handleError's per-card /api/alchemy fetch (NftImage.jsx:100-127) — up to 24 parallel calls, the exact pattern the 2026-06-11 fix was eliminating.
findings.suggestion: For Nakamigos set the sales-path fallback to null + imagePending like the listings path (the batch enrichment at Listings.jsx:124-145 already covers saleIds), and gate normalizeToken's fallbackImage per collection.

findings.title: Token-metadata enrichment refetches the same IDs on every activities/tokens update — periodic batch-fetch storm
findings.evidence: Listings.jsx:124-145 — `const knownIds = new Set(tokens.map(t => String(t.id)));` then `missingIds = allNeededIds.filter(id => !knownIds.has(id))`. Already-fetched `extraTokens` are never added to knownIds, and the effect deps include `activities` and `tokens`. useCollection polls activities every 60s (fallback) producing a new array each cycle (useCollection.js:68,81), and gallery pagination grows `tokens` — each change re-runs the effect and re-issues fetchTokensByIds for ALL non-gallery listed+sale IDs (up to ~787 listings = 8 batch POSTs of 100, api.js:809-829) even though nothing is missing.
findings.suggestion: Include extraTokens ids in knownIds (or keep a fetched-ids ref) so only genuinely new ids are requested.

findings.title: On API failure while scrolled near the bottom, load-more retries in an unthrottled loop
findings.evidence: VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:134-136 resets the guard on every loading flip (`useEffect(() => { loadMoreCalledRef.current = false; }, [rowCount, loading])`), and the trigger effect (lines 139-148) re-runs because `onLoadMore` (useNfts.js:77-80, useCallback deps [loading, hasMore, load]) gets a new identity each load cycle. On error, useNfts.js:54-56 sets the error message but leaves hasMore=true, so the cycle load→error→loading false→guard reset→effect re-fires→load repeats continuously with no backoff while the user sits near the bottom — hammering the proxy that has already rate-limited once in prod.
findings.suggestion: On error, suppress auto-retrigger (e.g. set hasMore false until the user clicks the error banner's Retry, or add exponential backoff in useNfts).

findings.title: Batch-selection bar (fixed bottom, z-index 100) is covered by the mobile bottom nav (fixed bottom, z-index 9999)
findings.evidence: Listings.jsx:900-907 — sticky bar `position: "fixed", bottom: 0, left: 0, right: 0, zIndex: 100`. MobileNav.jsx:117-128 — `.mobile-bottom-nav { position: "fixed", bottom: 0, zIndex: 9999, padding: "6px 0 max(6px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom))" }`. Both occupy the same strip; on phones the "N selected / Add All to Cart" bar renders underneath the nav, hiding the action buttons. (Stacking math verified from code; not screen-verified.)
findings.suggestion: On <768px offset the selection bar above the nav (e.g. bottom: calc(nav height + safe-area)) or raise its z-index above 9999 while keeping it below modals.

findings.title: Visiting the Traits tab silently kicks off loading ALL 20,000 Nakamigos tokens — ~500 sequential API pages with O(n²) trait re-extraction
findings.evidence: TraitExplorer.jsx:379-381 `useEffect(() => { if (loadAll && hasMore) loadAll(); }, [loadAll, hasMore]);` drives useNfts.js:107-121 (one 40-token page per 200ms). For 20k supply that's ~500 proxy calls over ~100s, and every page re-runs extractTraitFilters over the full accumulated array (useNfts.js:49) plus computeRarity/filter/sort useMemos over a growing 20k array — sustained jank and exactly the API pressure profile that previously tripped the Upstash limiter. Leaving the tab doesn't stop it (loadingAll state lives in useNfts at App level).
findings.suggestion: Add a server/precomputed trait-summary path for Nakamigos (rarity.json already exists per api.js:744), or cap auto-loadAll and show an explicit "Load all 20,000 (may take a minute)" progress affordance with a cancel.

findings.title: "Rarest First" category sort compares each category's MOST COMMON value, not its rarest
findings.evidence: TraitExplorer.jsx:490-495 — `const aMin = a.values[0]?.pct ?? 100;` but values are sorted by count DESC (line 421 `.sort((a, b) => b.count - a.count)`), so values[0] is the most common value. The variable named aMin is actually the max pct; the resulting order is "most evenly distributed categories first", not rarest-first.
findings.suggestion: Use the minimum pct (`a.values[a.values.length - 1]?.pct` or Math.min over values) for the rarest-first comparator.

findings.title: Search only matches the loaded pages — searching a valid token ID that isn't loaded yields 'No Results Found'
findings.evidence: Gallery.jsx:40-44 filters `tokens` (loaded pages only) by name/id; for Nakamigos only ~80 of 20,000 tokens are loaded before scrolling. Searching "15000" shows the empty state even though the token exists. The codebase already has the fix pattern: the ?token= deep link falls back to fetchTokensByIds for unloaded ids (App.jsx:301-308).
findings.suggestion: When a numeric search has zero loaded matches and is within supply, fetch that token by id (fetchTokensByIds) and surface it as a result.

findings.title: Failure-sentinel cache never actually suppresses refetches — failed entries are indistinguishable from cache misses
findings.evidence: NftImage.jsx:36-45 — for a failed entry within TTL, getCachedUrl skips the eviction branch and `return entry.url;` which is null (setCachedFailed stores `{ url: null, ... failed: true }`). Callers treat null as "no cache" (line 80 `if (!cached && !primarySrc ...)` re-fires the metadata fetch; handleError never consults the cache), so the 5-minute failure TTL and the failed flag are dead code — every remount of a known-bad token re-hits /api/alchemy.
findings.suggestion: Return a sentinel (e.g. {failed:true}) from getCachedUrl and short-circuit straight to the placeholder (failCount=3) for cached failures.

findings.title: Search placeholder renders the literal text '…' to users
findings.evidence: TraitExplorer.jsx:716 — `placeholder="Search traits or values…"`. JSX attribute string literals do not process JS unicode escapes, so the input shows `Search traits or values…`. Every other escape in the file correctly uses a JS expression (e.g. line 713 `{"⌕"}`).
findings.suggestion: Change to placeholder={"Search traits or values…"} or just use the … character.

findings.title: Floor prices ≥1 ETH are rounded to whole numbers — a 1.5 ETH floor displays as '2 ETH'
findings.evidence: CollectionLanding.jsx:334-340 — `if (typeof val === "number" && suffix === " ETH" && val < 1) return val.toFixed(4) + suffix; if (... suffix === " ETH") return val.toLocaleString(undefined, { maximumFractionDigits: 0 }) + suffix;` — used for the FLOOR stat (line 578). Fine for volume, wrong for floors between 1 and ~100 ETH.
findings.suggestion: Use the shared lib/formatPrice.js (4 decimals < 1000) for the Floor stat.

findings.title: Token-ID search assumes ids are 1..supply — wrong for burn/sparse collections per the project's own config notes
findings.evidence: CollectionLanding.jsx:98-105 — `if (id > 0 && id <= col.supply)` builds a deep link. constants.js:33 says gnssart "supply 9696 // On-chain totalSupply (token IDs go up to 9000+)" and constants.js:49 junglebay "supply 5555 ... (reflects burns)" — so ids above supply can exist (excluded from search) and ids below supply can be burned (search links to a dead token). Also `id > 0` excludes a token #0 if the collection is 0-indexed.
findings.suggestion: Treat the bound as a heuristic hint in the UI copy, or validate by fetching the token before navigating.

findings.title: Two stacked empty states: full-height 'No items found' from the grid plus the styled empty-state card below it
findings.evidence: Gallery.jsx:197-208 always renders VirtualGalleryGrid; with tokens=[] and !loading it returns its own `calc(100vh - 200px)` centered "No items found" div (VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:164-179). Gallery.jsx:211-231 then ALSO renders its `.empty-state` block for the same condition — the user sees a plain viewport-height message and must scroll past it to reach the real empty state (which itself duplicates EmptyState.jsx copy by hand instead of using the shared component).
findings.suggestion: Skip rendering VirtualGalleryGrid when displayed.length===0 && !loading, and use the shared <EmptyState> component for the copy.

findings.title: Timeline is out of chronological order and embeds a hardcoded market stat as 'Present'
findings.evidence: JungleBayShowcase.jsx:29-39 — TIMELINE_EVENTS places "Nov 2021 — Sandbox Land Secured" (index 5) after "May 2022 — Otherside Land Acquired" (index 4); the rendered timeline is positional, so the dates appear shuffled. The final event hardcodes "Only 0.98% of supply listed." — a point-in-time stat that will silently rot under a 'Present' label.
findings.suggestion: Reorder the array chronologically; compute listed % live from listings/supply (both already in props upstream) or drop the number.

findings.title: queryKeys.traitOffers does not exist but is called in two mutation callbacks — a TypeError landmine in a currently-dead module
findings.evidence: queryConfig.js:56-62 defines only listings/collectionOffers/collectionStats/ownedNfts/nftMetadata, but useTradingMutations.js:55 and :101 call `queryKeys.traitOffers(slug)` in onSettled — would throw `queryKeys.traitOffers is not a function` and skip the subsequent ['offers'] invalidation. Grep confirms no component currently imports any useTradingMutations hook, so it is unreachable today — but it is the designated mutation layer and will detonate the first time someone wires it up.
findings.suggestion: Add `traitOffers: (slug) => ["trait-offers", slug]` to queryKeys (or remove the dead module if the inline mutation paths are canonical).

findings.title: Hardcoded FALLBACK_STATS (floor 0.1048 ETH, 5,238 owners) render as live data on first paint and on API failure with no staleness marker in the Hero
findings.evidence: useCollection.js:17-19 initializes Nakamigos stats to FALLBACK_STATS (constants.js:169-174 `floor: 0.1048, volume: 52200, owners: 5238`), and api.js:218 returns `{ ...FALLBACK_STATS, fallback: true }` on double failure. Hero.jsx:146-153 renders stats.floor as "FLOOR" with no fallback/stale indicator (the isLive flag exists but only feeds the header dot). A wrong floor on a trading surface misleads buyers.
findings.suggestion: Show a subtle 'cached' / 'approx' marker on Hero stat cards when stats.fallback (additive badge, no removal).

findings.title: /:collection/nft/:id deep link opens a bare placeholder modal (no image/attributes) for unloaded tokens, unlike the ?token= path which fetches
findings.evidence: App.jsx:330-338 — `else if (nfts.allTokens.length > 0) { setSelected({ id: deepLinkTokenId, name: `#${deepLinkTokenId}`, attributes: [], image: null }); }` with no fetchTokensByIds call, while the ?token= handler (App.jsx:301-308) does fetch the token. For Nakamigos (no auto-load) most shared /nft/:id links hit the placeholder. Caveat: Modal.jsx may self-enrich — not verified (Modal outside this audit's scope).
findings.suggestion: Reuse the ?token= fetch-by-id fallback for the /nft/:id path.

findings.title: Dead isMobile state with a resize listener that re-renders the sidebar on every window resize
findings.evidence: FilterSidebar.jsx:400 `const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false);` and 410-415 attach a resize listener calling setIsMobile — but isMobile is never read (line 459 `const renderAsMobile = !!isMobileOverlay;` uses only the prop). Pure re-render churn during resize/orientation changes.
findings.suggestion: Delete the state and listener.

findings.title: Card.jsx ignores rankApproximate — approximate ranks display as authoritative, inconsistent with VirtualCard and Hero
findings.evidence: Card.jsx:44 `{nft.rank && (` shows the badge unconditionally, while VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:316 gates with `!nft.rankApproximate` and Hero.jsx:43 with `!cur.rankApproximate`. computeRarity (api.js:795-797) marks ranks approximate when <80% of a non-Nakamigos collection is loaded; Favorites/MyCollection render Card via AnimatedCard (Favorites.jsx:58, MyCollection.jsx:396), so gnssart/junglebay favorites show unreliable ranks as real.
findings.suggestion: Add the same !nft.rankApproximate gate (or an '~' prefix) in Card.jsx.

findings.title: Interactive rows and cards in TraitExplorer, SpeciesEncyclopedia, CharacterTypeExplorer and the JungleBay timeline are mouse-only (no role/tabIndex/keydown), inconsistent with the rest of the app
findings.evidence: TraitExplorer.jsx:777-785 trait value rows are plain divs with onClick only; same for detail-grid items (575-582), SpeciesEncyclopedia.jsx:352-361 species cards, CharacterTypeExplorer.jsx:359-371 type cards, JungleBayShowcase.jsx:264-271 timeline items. Contrast: FilterSidebar rows have role=checkbox/tabIndex/onKeyDown (FilterSidebar.jsx:579-590) and Card/VirtualCard/MarqueeItem all implement role=button + Enter/Space.
findings.suggestion: Apply the existing role+tabIndex+onKeyDown pattern from FilterSidebar to these click targets.

findings.title: Cross-collection search dropdown lacks keyboard navigation and combobox semantics
findings.evidence:
CollectionLanding.jsx:149-265 — input has no onKeyDown (no ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Enter selection, Escape only closes via outside-click handler at 111-119), no role=combobox/aria-expanded/aria-activedescendant, results are plain buttons. Also

/

nested inside the CollectionCard
findings.suggestion: Add arrow-key/Enter handling + combobox ARIA; swap inner headings for styled divs.

findings.title: Add-to-cart on gallery cards is hover-gated — unreachable on touch devices
findings.evidence: VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:358 — `{onAddToCart && !inCart && hovered && (<button ...>` with hovered set only by onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave (296-297). iPhone/iPad users cannot add to cart from the gallery grid (only via modal/listings).
findings.suggestion: On coarse pointers always render the button (media (hover: none) check or a persistent compact button).

findings.title: No 'loading more' indicator during scroll pagination; mobile filter count can also double-count
findings.evidence: VirtualGalleryGrid renders nothing at the bottom while a next page loads (loading=true with tokens present has no UI; Gallery.jsx:119-128 only swaps the toolbar counter). Minor: Gallery.jsx:75 badge `Object.values(activeFilters).reduce((c, v) => c + v.length, 0) + (listedOnly ? 1 : 0)` omits the price filter while FilterSidebar.jsx:417-423 includes it — the two counters can disagree.
findings.suggestion: Add a small spinner row/skeleton row when loading && tokens.length>0; unify the active-count computation.

findings.title: Four of six tuned query configs are dead exports — stats and metadata fetching hand-rolled with useState instead, so the documented cache policy doesn't apply
findings.evidence: Grep shows nftMetadataQuery, floorPriceQuery, collectionStatsQuery, ownedNftsQuery (queryConfig.js:5,13,30,39) have zero importers. useCollection.js implements its own setInterval polling (lines 80-85) and useNfts its own pagination state, so the "centralized so every hook uses consistent, tuned settings" goal (queryConfig.js:1-2) only holds for listings/offers. CollectionLanding also refetches all 3 collections' stats (4 API calls each) on every landing visit with no cache (CollectionLanding.jsx:618-653).
findings.suggestion: Migrate useCollection stats (and landing-page stats) onto useQuery with collectionStatsQuery — instant cross-page cache sharing with the existing config.

findings.title: Featured-NFT rotation swaps src abruptly; volume formatter caps at 'K'
findings.evidence: Hero.jsx:41 puts `transition: "opacity 0.6s, transform 0.6s"` on the img style but nothing changes opacity on swap — the 4s rotation (lines 18-24) is a hard cut. formatVolume (lines 85-89) renders 1,234,567 as "1234.6K" (no M tier). The interval also keeps firing while the tab is hidden.
findings.suggestion: Crossfade via a keyed wrapper (framer-motion AnimatePresence is already in the bundle); add an M tier; pause on document.hidden.

findings.title: Minor consistency nits: raw price in aria-label, unstable list keys in Listings, dead imports/props
findings.evidence: VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:295 aria-label interpolates raw `${nft.price} ETH` (e.g. 0.123456789) while visible UI uses formatPrice; Listings.jsx:782 `key={`${nft.id}-${idx}`}` makes keys order-dependent so re-sorting remounts all cards; Gallery.jsx:2 imports Skeleton but never renders it; Skeleton.jsx:1 accepts a `view` prop it never uses; NftImage.handleError (NftImage.jsx:100) ignores noSelfFetch so a broken batch-supplied URL still triggers a per-card fetch.
findings.suggestion: formatPrice in aria-labels, key by nft.id alone, drop dead imports/props, early-return in handleError when noSelfFetch.

findings.title: fetchCollectionOffers and the bestOffers loop have no abort wiring (cancelled-flag only) and bestOffers fetches 20 offers strictly sequentially
findings.evidence: Listings.jsx:110-115 fetchCollectionOffers has no signal/cleanup (component remount on collection switch makes cross-collection bleed a non-issue — verified App.jsx:184 key={collectionSlug} — but the network work still completes pointlessly); lines 205-221 await fetchBestOffer one-at-a-time for up to 20 ids (~20 sequential round-trips; rate-limit friendly but slow to populate).
findings.suggestion: Thread AbortSignals through; batch best-offer fetches 3-4 at a time.

good: proxy.js is genuinely solid: ApiError preserving HTTP status + Retry-After parsing (seconds AND http-date), isRetryable classification, network-error normalization to status 0, and safe JSON parsing guarding against Vercel edge-case non-JSON responses (proxy.js:9-32,66-72).

fulfillSeaportOrder (api.js:982-1106) is exchange-grade hardened: wrong-chain refusal before broadcast, Seaport 1.5/1.6 address allowlist, fulfillment-function-name allowlist (anti-tampered-API), ABI-parameter-name-based argument mapping instead of Object.values order, BigInt value validation, on-chain receipt status check, and clean rejected/insufficient error taxonomy — it never throws, so Listings.handleBuy's no-try/catch style is safe.

The 2026-06-11 listings image-pipeline fix is real and correct on its primary path: listedNfts leaves image null + imagePending (Listings.jsx:166-175), NftImage honors noSelfFetch with a pulsing 'loading not missing' placeholder (NftImage.jsx:57-62,129-143), and fetchTokensByIds batches 100/request with per-chunk failure tolerance (api.js:809-834). Only the recent-sales side path was missed (flagged).

Rarity engineering: precomputed Nakamigos ranks from a build script (api.js:744-761), runtime fallback that uses real supply as denominator and marks rankApproximate below 80% coverage, and VirtualCard/Hero both honor the flag — honest UX about partial data.

TraitExplorer's sampling honesty is best-in-class: percentages computed from the loaded sample with an explicit written rationale (TraitExplorer.jsx:397-402), '~' prefixes and 'of N supply (trait % from loaded sample)' labels throughout.

Listings UX details: chunked 60-card reveal with 'Show N more (x of y)' (documented against the real 787-listing case), median-led MEDIAN/AVG stat with a comment explaining whale skew (6.9 avg vs 0.45 median in prod), self-buy guarded both in UI ('Your Listing') and in handleBuy, batch-select with running ETH total, listed % of supply, marketplace badges, USD subprices, and an OpenSea escape hatch in every fallback/empty state.

The iOS Safari flex-order bug fix is documented in-place (Listings.jsx:457-465) and backed by real CSS (.listings-main-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr !important } at App.css:1859) — inline-style responsiveness is correctly overridden.

useNfts cancellation discipline: AbortController per collection switch and refresh, abort checks after every await, dedup on page merge, and throttled auto-load gated to <1000-supply collections (useNfts.js:62-98).

useListings is a clean TanStack Query adoption: tuned staleTime/refetchInterval/gcTime from a central config, placeholderData:undefined to avoid cross-collection stale flash, and a memoized stable return shape for consumers.

Accessibility groundwork is broad (if uneven): skip-nav link, role=switch/checkbox with aria-checked in FilterSidebar, aria-pressed favorite buttons, keyboard Enter/Space on cards and marquee items with tabIndex -1 on aria-hidden marquee clones, focus-visible outlines on landing cards, and a full power-user keyboard layer (j/k/Enter/f/c/1-6/?) with input-field guards.

Motion/perf hygiene: hoisted framer-motion hover configs to avoid memo-busting object churn (VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:20-27), prefers-reduced-motion respected at three levels (component checks, marquee-specific CSS disable, and a global animation kill-switch in App.css:3545), contain:strict on the virtualized scroller, CSS-transform marquee with hover/focus pause, and aspect-ratio reservations preventing image CLS.

EmptyState.jsx is a well-designed centralized copy registry (typed registry + {collection} interpolation + compact variant + action wiring) and SkeletonFallback provides page-shaped Suspense skeletons rather than generic spinners.

fetchListings merges OpenSea + native orderbook with per-source failure isolation, dedupes by tokenId keeping the cheapest, and reports a truthful source label (api.js:677-740); fetchCollectionStats takes min(OpenSea floor, native floor) and prefers on-chain totalSupply for burn accuracy.

The ?token= shareable deep link is thoughtfully done: history.replaceState sync both directions, regex-validated id, fetch-by-id fallback for unloaded tokens, and edge-middleware OG cards noted for unfurls (App.jsx:277-309).

CollectionView remount-by-key on collection switch (App.jsx:184) is a clean state-isolation strategy that eliminates whole classes of cross-collection bleed (verified it covers Listings' bestOffers/purchasedIds, which initially looked leaky).
missingVsBestInClass: URL-synced, shareable gallery state: active trait filters, sort, search, listed-only and price range are all in-memory only (useNfts/Gallery state) — OpenSea/Blur encode these in the URL so views are linkable and survive refresh.

Listed-price/listed-status badges on gallery cards: the data exists in the listings prop but is never merged onto tokens, so the main browse grid shows no prices at all (Blur/OpenSea grids lead with price; this also blocks the dead price sort/filter, see findings).

USD values outside the listings grid: Hero floor, gallery, sweep totals and the batch-selection ETH total have no fiat equivalent; priceUsd is only shown when OpenSea happens to supply it on a listing.

Jump-to-token / scroll restoration: the virtualizer has scrollToIndex available but there is no 'go to token #' affordance, and returning from the detail modal or another tab loses grid scroll position.

Pre-trade transparency: Buy Now goes straight to wallet signing with no tx simulation/gas estimate preview, no fee breakdown (1% platform + 1% OpenSea are in constants but not surfaced at point of sale), and no price-vs-floor delta warning for overpriced listings.
Listing metadata depth: no expiry countdown on listing cards (expiry exists on native orders), no 'listed X ago', no maker ENS/short-address display in the grid, no per-listing floor-difference %.

Marketplace/trait filters on the buy grid: Listings offers only sort + max-price; best-in-class buy surfaces (Blur, OpenSea Pro) offer trait filtering and source (OpenSea vs native) toggles on the same grid where the filter data already exists (traitCategories is computed at Listings.jsx:356-371 but only used for the trait-offer dropdown).
Landing-page market context: collection cards show static floor/volume/owners with no 24h deltas, sparklines, or last-updated stamp (Dexscreener/OpenSea category pages lead with change indicators).

Recent-sales analytics affordance: sales cards show price+time but no sale-vs-floor delta or buyer/seller links, and there is no export/share of the sales list (CSV lib exists at lib/csv.js but is not wired here).

Responsive images: NftImage uses a single fixed src with width/height 300 — no srcset/sizes or DPR variants, so retina grids upscale thumbnails and large screens over-fetch nothing/under-resolve (Alchemy provides multiple cached sizes that the code already knows about: thumbnailUrl/pngUrl/originalUrl).
Offline/connection awareness: no navigator.onLine detection or 'you're offline' banner; API failures surface as generic 'check your connection' text with manual Retry only.

Search depth: gallery search matches name/id of loaded tokens only — no trait-value search, no fuzzy matching, no fetch-by-id fallback for valid unloaded ids (the ?token= deep-link path already implements the fetch pattern).

findings.title: Tab-pane entrance animation freezes permanently mid-fade — forms render ghosted/unreadable
findings.evidence: The .glass-card pane wrapper gets stuck mid-tween: computed opacity 0.636536 with transform matrix(1,0,0,1,0,-0.34459) unchanged after 5+ s (prod, click-switch to Liquidity); 0.506454 unchanged across two samples 3 s apart (prod, DIRECT load of /swap?tab=liquidity); 0.721235 (dev localhost:5173 at HEAD — NOT fixed). Result: 'Grow the Crop'/'Pull Crop Out', labels, and even the Connect Wallet button sit at ~50-70% opacity over high-detail artwork — fails contrast, looks disabled/broken. DCA pane completed its fade only on one direct load; froze when reached via tab click.
findings.suggestion: Find the interrupted tween (likely AnimatePresence/entrance animation racing the tab-switch height/layout change) and make panes settle to opacity:1 deterministically (e.g. animation fill-forwards or onAnimationComplete fallback that force-sets final style). Also give the Liquidity gate card the same solid backdrop the Swap pane has.

findings.title: Prod /api/opensea rejects the stats path the frontend sends → 3x 400, volume shows '–', hub drops to DEMO fallback
findings.evidence: GET https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app/api/opensea?path=collections%2Fjunglebay%2Fstats → 400 {"error":"Invalid or missing path"} (3 occurrences on hub load, one per collection). Header shows status badge 'DEMO' with accessible label 'Using demo/fallback data — some features may be limited'; collection cards show Volume '–'. The SAME request on localhost:5173 (HEAD) returns 200 with real OpenSea stats (volume 1034.43, floor 0.08875) — the prod serverless function's path allowlist is stale relative to HEAD.
findings.suggestion: Redeploy prod from HEAD (CLI deploy from repo root per the documented procedure). The fix already exists at HEAD — this is a stale-deployment issue, matching the 06-09 'stale prod build' diagnosis.

findings.title: Swap protocol fee contradicts itself across legal pages: 0.30% (Terms) vs 0.5% (Risks)
findings.evidence: Terms §7: 'a 0.30% fee on token swaps routed through the SwapFeeRouter (SWAP_FEE_BPS = 30; capped at 1.00% / MAX_FEE_BPS = 100 by contract)'. Risks 'Protocol limits & parameters' table: 'Swap — Protocol fee: 0.5% (1% hard cap) — Revenue to stakers; fee routing being finalized'.
findings.suggestion: Read the live SWAP_FEE_BPS on-chain and make both pages quote the same number (or render it from constants the way /contracts does).

findings.title: Treasury described as 'an EOA / multisig, not a smart contract' on Risks, but listed as a deployed contract (Treasury.sol) on Contracts
findings.evidence: Risks card: 'Treasury is an EOA / multisig, not a smart contract … There is no on-chain treasury policy.' Contracts page Core section lists 'Treasury — contracts/src/Treasury.sol — 0x7D2620...A4Bd7d — Etherscan' with a #code link; /treasury page links the same 0x7D2620243EdAd69Ec81A53c4A063B07995A4Bd7d as 'source ↗'.
findings.suggestion: One of the two is stale. If the receive address is genuinely a Safe/EOA, drop it from the contract index (or label it 'external'); if Treasury.sol is deployed at that address, update the Risks card.

findings.title: 'Recent Treasury Transactions' permanently shows 'momentarily unavailable' (prod AND dev HEAD)
findings.evidence: Every load of /treasury (multiple reloads, prod + localhost:5173) renders 'Treasury activity is momentarily unavailable. All activity remains auditable on the block explorer ↗.' No /api/ call for a ledger is even attempted in the network log — the feature appears hard-disabled, while the copy claims a transient outage. Dev additionally shows a 'Price oracle is stale' banner.
findings.suggestion: Either wire the ledger (it presumably needs the rotated Etherscan key) or change the copy to an honest 'coming soon — view on Etherscan' state. 'Momentarily' that never ends erodes the page's transparency promise.

findings.title: First-visit splash is ~15-25 s, not skippable, ends in a mandatory CLICK TO ENTER, and replays every new browser session — including on deep links to /terms and /privacy
findings.evidence: Deep link to /terms played the full sequence (art reveal → particle field → ring → kaleidoscope burst) before showing content (~16 s). On dev a mid-splash click did NOT skip; the sequence ended at 'TEGRIDY FARMS — CLICK TO ENTER', then a further multi-second shatter transition. Gating is per-session (replayed on the fresh localhost session despite tegridy_first_visit existing in localStorage; prod reloads within the session skip it).
findings.suggestion: Keep the art (constraint respected) but: add a visible Skip button from second 1, make any click/keypress fast-forward, auto-enter without the click gate, and remember entry once-ever in localStorage. Consider bypassing entirely for legal/info deep links — a user sent to /terms from a wallet prompt should not sit through 20 s of cinema.

findings.title: Tradermigos has a second entry gate: CLICK TO ENTER splash + ~4 s black transition on EVERY full page load
findings.evidence: Both visits (fresh + reload) showed the 'TRADERMIGOS / THE DIGITAL ART GALLERY / CLICK TO ENTER' screen with progress bar; after clicking, ~4 s of near-black (single light line) before the hub renders. No remembered-entry flag — repeat visitors pay the full cost each time.
findings.suggestion: Remember entry (localStorage) and auto-enter on repeat visits with a quick 300-500 ms fade; keep the full cinematic for first-timers.

findings.title: Logged-out Swap tab shows zero market data — entire form replaced by a connect gate
findings.evidence: Swap pane shows only 'Connect your wallet to swap' + Connect Wallet button. No token pair selector, no price, no quote preview, no chart, no pool stats. Uniswap/Cow/1inch all render the full quote flow logged-out and only gate the final action. Ironically the DCA tab DOES render its full form logged-out (amount input accepted '0.05', computed 'Total cost 1.5000 ETH'), proving the pattern works.
findings.suggestion: Render the swap form with live quoting while disconnected; make the action button the connect CTA (RainbowKit standard). Also fixes the gate-card layout: the Connect Wallet button sits left-aligned against the card edge while the message above is centered.

findings.title: Dead RPC (eth.llamarpc.com) is retried on every page — 503/OPTIONS 521 noise on each navigation
findings.evidence: Every page load logged eth.llamarpc.com POST 503 or OPTIONS 521 (often 2-4 attempts); failover to ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com / rpc.ankr.com (both 200) works, so data loads, but each page pays failed-preflight latency and console/network noise.
findings.suggestion: Health-check and demote a failing RPC for the session (circuit breaker) instead of re-trying it first on every page; or reorder the fallback list since llamarpc has been 5xx all session.

findings.title: 'All contracts are verified on Etherscan' claim could not be confirmed for the Wave-0 redeploys — risk of overstating
findings.evidence: Page header asserts: 'All contracts are verified on Etherscan.' Blockscout (proxy check; Etherscan API requires a key) has source for TOWELI ('Towelie', partial match) but returns NO name/source for TegridyStaking (0xcaDc93...), LP Farming Wave-0 redeploy (0x117126...), and SwapFeeRouter (0x6d5791...). The 06-06 deploy record states Etherscan source-verify was pending because the API key was invalid at deploy time.
findings.suggestion: Spot-check each address on Etherscan after rotating the API key; until then soften to 'Source for every contract is linked below' (the GitHub links already provide this).

findings.title: Jump-scroll (End key) leaves the viewport completely blank — in-view fade-ins only fire on wheel scroll
findings.evidence: Pressing End on /terms scrolled to scrollY 2650 and the screenshot was 100% empty navy; footer (top:3225, h:732) and last content section existed in DOM but were invisible. One wheel tick later everything faded in.
findings.suggestion: Trigger reveal animations from IntersectionObserver (fires on any scroll type) or force-complete animations for elements already in view on scroll-end; also matters for find-in-page and anchor links.

findings.title: Light theme is incomplete: only the header restyles; page content stays dark over a light body
findings.evidence: After toggling, localStorage tegridy-theme='light' and body background became rgb(245,243,255), but every content section still painted dark backgrounds — net effect is an orange header bolted onto the dark site. Nav links (purple on orange) have weak contrast.
findings.suggestion: Either finish light-theme coverage for the info pages or hide the toggle on pages that don't support it; current state reads as a bug.

findings.title: Mascot avatar overlaps the 'Protocol Active' price status chip
findings.evidence: Zoomed screenshot on /admin and / shows the floating Towelie avatar covering the right end of the 'Protocol Active $0.0000...' chip — the price value is partially hidden behind the mascot at default position.
findings.suggestion: Offset the status chip left of the mascot or stack them; both elements are pinned to the same corner.

findings.title: Stat cards mix em-dash and zero for the same meaning
findings.evidence: LIFETIME FEES shows '–' as the headline but '0.0000 ETH routed' as the subtitle; TREASURY BALANCE shows '0 ETH' with '–' beneath; POL HOLDINGS '–' with '0.00% of LP supply'. Dash conventionally signals 'failed to load', which undermines the 'live on-chain view' framing when the real value is just zero.
findings.suggestion: Show explicit zeros ('0 ETH', '$0.00') when the read succeeded and reserve '–' for read failures.

findings.title: Doc links point at /blob/main/ while the repo default branch is mvp-launch
findings.evidence: FIX_STATUS.md, AUDITS.md, CONTRACTS.md, docs/WAVE_0_TODO.md etc. all link to github.com/fomotsar-commits/tegridy-farms/blob/main/...; gh API confirms repo is public, the files exist on main, but default branch is mvp-launch — main can drift stale and silently serve outdated audit/status info.
findings.suggestion: Point doc links at the default branch (or pin to a commit SHA regenerated at build time, matching the 'Last regenerated from constants.ts' pattern).

findings.title: 21,434% APR displayed raw as the headline number
findings.evidence: Home ticker 'Base APR 21,434%' (with small 'early-stage' tag) and /farm stat card 'STAKING APR 21,434%' with sub-caption 'early-TVL bootstrap rate — normalizes as TVL grows'. The caption is honest, but a 5-digit APR is the classic rug-signal heuristic for experienced DeFi users.
findings.suggestion: Additionally show the projected APR at a reference TVL (e.g. 'at $100k TVL: ~X%') or cap the headline with a '>999%' style treatment plus the explainer tooltip.

findings.title: Revenue-destination copy conflicts: 'every fee funds the treasury' vs '100% of protocol revenue goes to stakers'
findings.evidence: Tradermigos hub subtitle: 'Native listings: one flat 1% fee, every fee funds the treasury'. Site footer (every page): '100% of protocol revenue goes to stakers.' Treasury page shows Revenue Distribution = Stakers 100% (10000 bps), Treasury 0% (inactive).
findings.suggestion: Align the Tradermigos line with the actual split ('1% fee — routed to stakers via the revenue distributor') or qualify which fees differ.

findings.title: Hub fires 9 sequential /api/alchemy calls and /api/orderbook takes ~2.4 s
findings.evidence: Resource timing: 9x /api/alchemy (200, 0.8-1.3 s each), 3x /api/orderbook (200, ~2.38 s each), total page ~250 requests / ~6.8 MB compressed — the heaviest page audited.
findings.suggestion: Batch the alchemy reads (multicall or one serverless fan-out) and cache orderbook stats server-side; would cut hub time-to-data roughly in half.

findings.title: Connect gate hides all pool/tier data from prospective stakers
findings.evidence: Logged-out /farm shows 5 stat chips + 'Connect to farm with tegridy' card; no lock-tier table (7d-4yr multipliers exist — the home calculator proves the data is client-side), no current pool TVL breakdown, no reward schedule.
findings.suggestion: Render the tier/boost table and live pool stats read-only below the gate; gate only the position widgets. (Additive — keeps the existing art and card.)

findings.title: No historical dimension on a transparency page
findings.evidence: Page is a snapshot only ('as of block #25299228'): no fees-over-time chart, no TVL history, no distribution history, and the tx ledger is down (see separate finding).
findings.suggestion: Add a small fees/TVL sparkline once the indexer is live; even 7-day history materially strengthens the 'public transparency' framing.

findings.title: Tab naming mismatch: 'Alerts' tab → URL ?tab=limit → page title 'Price Alert'
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Alerts' tab navigates to /swap?tab=limit and sets document.title 'Price Alert | Tegridy Farms'; heading says 'Price Alert'.
findings.suggestion: Pick one name (Alerts or Limit) across tab label, URL param, and title for shareable-URL clarity.

findings.title: Contract-address copy chip gives minimal feedback
findings.evidence: Clicking the copy icon next to 0x420698...278F9D swaps the glyph briefly; no toast/checkmark color change was clearly visible in zoom — at a glance the user cannot tell the copy happened.
findings.suggestion: Brief green check + 'Copied' tooltip (the pattern already common in DeFi UIs).

findings.title: Repo file paths cited inline in user-facing legal text without links
findings.evidence: 'see frontend/src/lib/errorReporting.ts for the exact scrub regex', 'preserved in the frontend/src/pages/PrivacyPage.tsx git history', 'docs/SECRET_ROTATION.md', plus a stray 'Basescan' mention though the app is Ethereum-mainnet only.
findings.suggestion: Hyperlink the file references to GitHub (the transparency is great — make it one click) and drop/justify the Basescan mention.

findings.title: Data-dense pages keep a narrow center column; ultrawide width is mostly art/empty margin
findings.evidence: Terms/Privacy/Risks use a comfortable reading column (good line length — correct call). But /contracts (31 address rows) and /treasury also confine to the same ~half-width column, leaving very large side margins on a 3432px display; the contracts list scrolls long while the sides sit empty.
findings.suggestion: At >2000px, let /contracts go two-column per section (name+source left, address+links right already exist — two cards side by side) and widen /treasury stat row. Additive; background art untouched.

findings.title: Gate card has no inline connect action
findings.evidence: 'Admin Panel — Connect your wallet to access this page.' renders with no button; the user must find the header Connect. (Gate itself is clean: 693 chars in DOM, zero admin controls leaked, no console errors, no spinner.)
findings.suggestion: Add a Connect Wallet button inside the card, mirroring /farm's gate.

good: Risk Disclosure page is genuinely best-in-class: protocol-specific 'What can actually go wrong — as of today' cards with ACTIVE/MITIGATED badges (single-operator key, EOA treasury, no paid audit, IP/parody exposure, single maintainer), a full 'Protocol limits & parameters' table with the WHY for every cap, and 'Last updated: June 11, 2026 (post-relaunch honesty pass)'. Do not let any redesign water this down.

Privacy policy is plain-English and unusually concrete: names the exact Supabase tables, retention behavior, SIWE/JWT revocation, Upstash hashed sliding-window keys, GDPR/CCPA articles with a 30-day response promise — far above DeFi norm.

Contract Index is exemplary: grouped by role, per-contract status badges (PENDING DEPLOY / REDEPLOY QUEUED / AWAITING MULTISIG) with a Wave-0 closure legend, GitHub source links per contract, Etherscan #code links, zeroed addresses honestly shown as 0x000000...000000 with em-dash, and external deps all byte-correct canonical addresses (UniV2 Router02 0x7a250d..., Factory 0x5C69bE..., WETH9 0xC02aaA..., Chainlink ETH/USD 0x5f4eC3...). Footer chip address matches the Etherscan token link.

InfoPage tab architecture works flawlessly: deep links (/terms, /privacy, /risks, /contracts, /treasury) each select the correct pill; in-page tab clicks update URL + document.title + scroll-to-top; every page has a unique, correct title.
/admin gate is clean: zero admin UI in the DOM while disconnected, no console spew, no infinite spinner; 'Skip to main content' a11y link present site-wide.
RPC provider failover works in production: llamarpc 503s were absorbed by publicnode/ankr (both 200) with data rendering fine — the recent infra work demonstrably functions.
Zero console errors observed across every page audited (prod).

Performance is solid for an art-heavy app: DCL 406-946 ms, load <1.1 s on all four perf pages; no single asset over 500 KB compressed; vendor code split (wagmi 311 KB gz / viem 180 KB gz / metamask-sdk 161 KB gz); ~3.8 MB total for home, no visible layout shift between consecutive screenshots, no web-font flash (4 font files, headlines render stable).

Treasury page shows 'as of block #' live-read indicator and an honest Revenue Distribution bar (Stakers 100% / POL 0% inactive / Treasury 0% inactive) matching the empty-treasury reality; tiny $67 TVL is shown rather than faked.
DEMO fallback badge on Tradermigos is honest UX (labeled fallback data instead of silently fake numbers) — the right pattern, even though the underlying 400 should be fixed.

Contextual mascot bubbles adapt per page ('Legal stuff. Required by grown-ups.' on /terms, 'We don't track much' on /privacy, 'Read this. Seriously.' on /risks) with Ask me / Don't show again controls — charming, additive personality.

DCA tab is honest about its keeper-less design: 'Browser-only feature: DCA schedules only run while this tab is open... keeper-based on-chain DCA planned for v2', and its form works fully logged-out with live total-cost math.
CSP blocks arbitrary cross-origin fetch from the page (api.github.com fetch failed) — tight connect-src.

Footer is complete and correct: 26 links, all internal routes exist (incl. /security), externals (app.uniswap.org/swap, etherscan.io token page, GeckoTerminal pool, x.com/junglebayac, discord.gg/junglebay, t.me/tegridyfarms) all carry target=_blank + rel='noopener noreferrer'.
live:info-admin-perf.splashAndTransitions: Site splash: ~15-25 s multi-act animation (art reveal → particles → ring → kaleidoscope) ending in a mandatory CLICK TO ENTER, not skippable by mid-click; gated per browser SESSION so it replays every new session and fires even on deep links to /terms//privacy; within a session, reloads skip it (good). Tradermigos adds a second CLICK TO ENTER splash on EVERY /nakamigos load plus ~4 s of near-black transition after the click. Page-level entrance fades run 2-4 s, leaving pages (notably /security over the white skull art) looking broken/unreadable until they settle. Two real defects in this system: (1) /swap tab panes freeze permanently mid-fade at opacity ~0.5-0.72 (reproduced 3/3, prod + dev HEAD); (2) jump-scrolls (End key) don't trigger in-view reveals — viewport stays fully blank until a wheel event. SPA tab switches and client navigations are otherwise smooth with correct scroll-to-top; no skeletons used on info pages (content fades in instead); first-paint after cache is fast (DCL <1 s).
live:info-admin-perf.consoleAndNetwork: No console errors on any audited page (prod or dev). Network failures: eth.llamarpc.com POST 503 / OPTIONS 521 on essentially every page load, retried 2-4x before failover to ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com and rpc.ankr.com (both 200) — dead provider still first in rotation. /api/opensea?path=collections%2F{slug}%2Fstats → 400 {"error":"Invalid or missing path"} x3 on /nakamigos (same call returns 200 on localhost:5173 — prod serverless stale vs HEAD). Slow calls: /api/orderbook ~2.38 s x3; 9 sequential /api/alchemy calls at 0.8-1.3 s each on /nakamigos. No 429s observed this session. Treasury tx-ledger makes no API call at all (feature dark, copy says 'momentarily unavailable').

findings.evidence:
pass9/iphone14_theater_mode.png and pass9/iphone14_modal_after_wait.png show a solid black area above 'Nakamigos #3' after 24+ seconds; DOM probe confirms .modal-image-side contains only
N #3

findings.title: 'Make Offer' button clipped off the right edge of the 390px viewport in the modal buy row
findings.evidence: pass9/iphone14_theater_mode.png and pass9/iphone14_modal_after_wait.png both show the gold 'Buy on OpenSea' button spanning nearly the full width with the secondary button cut mid-label ('Make (') at the right viewport edge; page scrollWidth stayed 390 so the rest of the button is unreachable. findings.evidence: pass6/iphone14_nakamigos-nakamigos-listings_2.png: 8 of 9 visible cards show the 'N + #tokenId' placeholder (e.g. #1643, #2349, #6296, #7499, #11915) instead of artwork, ~6s after page load; first-viewport rows (pass6 deals_2) do render. findings.evidence: Playwright network log on /nakamigos/nakamigos/nft/3: '502 https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app/api/opensea?path=orders%2Fethereum%2Fseaport%2Foffers&asset_contract_address=0xd774557b6...' and '400 .../api/opensea?path=collections%2Fnakamigos%2Fstats'. findings.title: Deep links to 9 tabs silently dump Lite-mode users (the default) on Floor & Listings with zero explanation

Source: frontend/src/nakamigos/App.jsx:316 `if (isLite && LITE_HIDDEN_ALL.has(tab)) navigate('/nakamigos/'+collectionSlug, {replace:true})` with LITE_HIDDEN sets in src/nakamigos/contexts/TradingModeContext.jsx:15-23. A shared /sniper or /portfolio link looks broken to a new user.
findings.suggestion: On redirect, show a toast ('Pro feature — switch to Pro in the header') or render the tab with a Pro-upsell gate instead of a silent replace.

findings.title: Two stacked interstitials before content on mobile deep links: click-gated splash on EVERY entry + first-visit 5-step tour
findings.evidence: All 23 routes showed the 'CLICK TO ENTER' splash on every full page load (pass1/pass2/pass3 screenshots, e.g. iphone14_nakamigos-nakamigos-chat_1.png); per src/nakamigos/App.jsx:138-143 splash persistence is deliberately per-mount ('the user asked that every entry... plays the splash'). On first collection visit the '1 OF 5 Gallery' tour modal then also blocks content (pass4/iphone14_nakamigos-nakamigos-deals_1.png). A shared listing link on iPhone = wait ~4-6s, tap splash, skip tour, then content.
findings.suggestion: Keep the splash per standing decision, but consider: shorter ready-time on mobile, auto-advance after ready, and not stacking the tour on the same visit a deep link is resolving (defer tour one navigation).
