findings.title: CSP/CORS noise on every page: eth.merkle.io blocked by connect-src, eth.llamarpc.com CORS-fails, Press Start 2P font stylesheet blocked by style-src
findings.evidence: Console on all 23 routes (results JSON): 'Fetch API cannot load https://eth.merkle.io/... violates Content Security Policy' x4 per page, 'Access to fetch at https://eth.llamarpc.com/ ... blocked by CORS' x3-4 per page, and 'Loading the stylesheet https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Press+Start+2P... violates style-src'. viewport:mobile-naka.splashAndTransitions: Splash: lays out well at 390px (title, loading bar, stats plaque all fit; subtitle is tiny/low-contrast — polish finding). It plays on EVERY full page load by deliberate design (App.jsx:138-143 per-mount, user-requested) and is click-gated with no auto-advance: a deep-linked mobile user waits ~4-6s then must tap 'CLICK TO ENTER' (wording says CLICK on a touch device), then on first collection visit the 5-step tour modal stacks on top — two interstitials before content. In-app tab navigation does NOT replay the splash (per-mount only) and bottom-nav transitions are instant with no jank observed. Skeletons: gallery/listings use pulsing letter-placeholders that read as 'missing' rather than 'loading' (and sometimes never resolve — see high finding); modal OFFERS skeletons never resolve due to the 502. Tour modal and Filters drawer animate cleanly at 390px.
viewport:mobile-naka.consoleAndNetwork: Console (identical pattern on all 23 routes, ~10-15 errors/page): (1) CSP connect-src blocks https://eth.merkle.io/ — 4x per page ('Fetch API cannot load... violates Content Security Policy'); (2) https://eth.llamarpc.com/ CORS preflight failure 3-4x per page + matching net::ERR_FAILED — both are wagmi/RPC fallback endpoints that can never succeed, wasting retries on mobile; (3) CSP style-src blocks https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Press+Start+2P — the pixel font stylesheet never loads. Network: /api/opensea?path=orders/ethereum/seaport/offers returns 502 and /api/opensea?path=collections/nakamigos/stats returns 400 on prod — these explain the永-skeleton OFFERS section in the NFT modal, 'VOLUME —' on hub collection cards, and junglebay's FLOOR/OWNERS/SUPPLY all showing '—'. Zero pageerrors (no JS exceptions) anywhere.

findings.title: Approval spender is inverted vs the executing router — every ERC20 sell reverts
findings.evidence: useSwapAllowance.ts:113 picks the spender as `const spender = selectedRoute === 'tegridy' ? TEGRIDY_ROUTER_ADDRESS : SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS;` and needsApproval (line 78) checks the same mapping. But useSwap.ts executes the OPPOSITE way: the 'tegridy' route goes through SwapFeeRouter (useSwap.ts:415-434, `address: SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS ... maxFeeBps`), while the 'uniswap' route and the aggregator-with-uniswap-fallback go to the real router (useSwap.ts:402-407 and 466-484, `address: UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER`). SwapFeeRouter pulls from the caller (SwapFeeRouter.sol:747 `IERC20(path[0]).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountIn)`) so its required spender is SFR; UniswapV2Router02 requires allowance to itself. Net effect, reachable today: selling TOWELI/USDC/etc (route='uniswap' since the native pool is empty) shows 'Approve TOWELI' which approves SFR (0x6d5791…), then 'Swap' calls UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER (0x7a250d…) → transferFrom fails → guaranteed revert at gas estimation. Conversely once the deep pool is seeded, route='tegridy' approves TegridyRouter (0xE9F8…) but executes via SFR → also reverts. Only the aggregator-route-with-tegridy-fallback combination matches by accident. ETH-input swaps are unaffected (no approval). The two execution-side fixes (fee-capture rerouting 'tegridy'→SFR, deep-pool fix 'uniswap'→real Uniswap) were never mirrored into useSwapAllowance.ts.
findings.suggestion: Make the spender derive from the venue that executes: 'tegridy' → SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS; 'uniswap' → UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER; 'aggregator' → selectedOnChainRoute.source ('tegridy'→SFR, 'uniswap'→UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER). Add a third allowance read for UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER in the useReadContracts batch and select activeAllowance with the same function used to pick the execution address, ideally a single shared `executionSpenderFor(route, fallback)` helper imported by both hooks so they can never drift again. Add a test asserting approve-spender === writeContract-target per route.

findings.title: Post-receipt success effect re-fires every second: duplicate 'WAGMI! Swap confirmed' toasts, false swap toast after a mere approval, reset timer never fires, duplicate analytics
findings.evidence: useSwap.ts:246-286 — the success effect's deps include `allowance` (line 286), and useSwapAllowance.ts:195-204 returns a fresh object literal every render (no useMemo). useSwapQuote.ts:261-265 runs a 1-second ticker (`setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000)`) once any quote has landed, so the page re-renders every second. While isSuccess && hash stay truthy (until reset()), the effect re-runs each second: the cleanup `clearTimeout(t)` cancels the pending 4s `reset(); setInputAmount('')` timer (line 284) before it can ever fire, then the body fires `toast.success('WAGMI! Swap confirmed'...)` and `trackSwap(...)` again (lines 268-278). Worse, after an APPROVE receipt the first run returns after 'Token approved' WITHOUT scheduling reset (lines 260-266), so the next 1s re-run sees `lastActionRef.current === null` and falls into the swap branch — firing 'WAGMI! Swap confirmed' + trackSwap for a swap that never happened, looping every second. allowance.refetchAllowance() + refetchFromBalance() also re-fire each tick (refetch storm).
findings.suggestion: Latch the receipt handling on the hash: keep a `handledHashRef` and bail if `hash === handledHashRef.current`; set it before toasting. Also memoize useSwapAllowance's return object (useMemo) and give the toasts stable ids (toast.success(..., { id: hash })) as defense in depth.

findings.title: DCA and price-alert keepers still have the SFR/TegridyRouter mismatch: minOut quoted from Uniswap but execution via SwapFeeRouter on the (empty) native pool — every triggered swap reverts today
findings.evidence: useDCA.ts:434-441 quotes `publicClient.readContract({ address: UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER, ... 'getAmountsOut' })` and computes minOut from that, then lines 496-530 execute `writeContract({ address: SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS, ... 'swapExactETHForTokens', args: [minOut, ...] })`. Identical pattern in useLimitOrders.ts: trigger + floor quoted on UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER (lines 319-330, 481-494) but execution on SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS (lines 400-435). DeployMVP.s.sol:253-254 wires `new SwapFeeRouter(d.router, ...)` where d.router is the TegridyRouter, i.e. SFR executes on the native TOWELI/WETH pool, which is EMPTY post-relaunch (2026-06-07 live diagnosis). So when a DCA tick or alert fires, the wallet prompt fails gas estimation and the user gets 'DCA swap failed' — and after the pool is seeded, the Uniswap-priced minOut against thin native-pool execution will revert whenever the venues diverge by more than slippage (the exact bug the main swap path was patched for on 2026-06-09, see useSwap.ts:395-399 comment). The main Swap tab is fixed (executes 'uniswap' on the real router) and the route-details panel naturally hides the Tegridy row while its output is 0 — but the keepers were never updated.
findings.suggestion: Quote and execute on the same venue in both keepers: either route keeper executions to UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER (matching their quote source, accepting no fee capture until the native pool is deep), or quote via SFR/TegridyRouter getAmountsOut and skip-with-toast when the native pool can't fill. Mirror the useSwap venue-selection logic instead of hardcoding SFR.

findings.title: Headline 'You Receive', 'Best rate via X' and 'Route Savings' advertise an aggregator price the app cannot execute — user can never receive the displayed amount
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:319 `const outputAmount = aggBetter ? aggComparison.userReceives : selectedOnChainRoute.output;` — the headline output is the full aggregator quote (e.g. CowSwap/Odos), but there is no aggregator execution path anywhere: executeSwap (useSwap.ts:379-408) executes an aggregator-selected quote on the on-chain fallback (SFR or Uniswap) with `onChainMin` derived from the ON-CHAIN venue's output. The route label says 'Best rate via CowSwap' (useSwapQuote.ts:423) and TradePage.tsx:384-388 shows 'Route Savings +x% vs worst venue' (computed at TradePage.tsx:98-108 across all quoted venues), yet the user receives roughly selectedOnChainRoute.output — the entire spread above the on-chain venue is fictional. The 'Min. Received' row is (correctly) anchored to the on-chain venue (useSwapQuote.ts:401-406, R033 H-01 amendment), so the visible Min Received can sit far below 'You Receive × (1-slippage)', which is internally inconsistent on the same panel.
findings.suggestion: Until real aggregator execution (Odos/Kyber build endpoints or CoW order placement) is wired, display the executing venue's output as 'You Receive' and demote aggregator quotes to an informational 'market comparison' row (additive — keep the comparison panel). Relabel 'Best rate via X' to something honest like 'Executes on Uniswap V2 (best executable route)'.

findings.title: Custom slippage input is unusable for fractional values — value re-formats with toFixed(2) on every keystroke
findings.evidence: TradePage.tsx:314 `value={isPreset ? '' : swap.slippage.toFixed(2)}` with onChange (317-325) immediately parsing and clamping each keystroke. Typing '0', '.', '3' produces: '0' → state 0 → field re-renders as '0.00'; appending '3' makes the string '0.003' → state 0.003 → renders '0.00' again. The comment at TradePage.tsx:274-276 says the input exists for 'users who need 0.3% or 3.5%', but exactly those values cannot be typed (each keystroke is reformatted before the decimal can be completed).
findings.suggestion: Keep a local string state for the field and commit the parsed/clamped number on blur or after a valid parse, only syncing the string from swap.slippage when the field is not focused (the pattern DCATab's slippage input already uses: raw number kept, clamp on blur).

findings.title: refreshQuote() does not re-fetch aggregator quotes despite its comment, and resets the staleness clock so the stale gate passes vacuously
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:437-446 — comment says 'Aggregator is a fetch effect — bumping the requestId triggers re-fetch', but `quoteRequestIdRef.current += 1` is a ref mutation and `setAggQuoteResult(null)` is not a dependency of the aggregator effect (deps at line 251 are [fromToken, toToken, parsedAmount, address, fromDecimals, chainId]); nothing re-runs the fetch. So after the R033 H-02 stale-quote bounce ('Quote is stale — refreshing now', useSwap.ts:343-347), the aggregator quote is wiped and never re-fetched until the user edits the input — a previously aggregator-best quote silently downgrades to the on-chain venue. Additionally `setQuoteFetchedAt(0)` makes `isQuoteStale` false immediately (lines 432-435 require quoteFetchedAt > 0), so a second Swap click passes the freshness gate before any refetch has actually settled.
findings.suggestion: Drive the aggregator effect off a `refreshNonce` state included in its dependency array, and stamp quoteFetchedAt only when fresh data lands (treat quoteFetchedAt===0 with a non-empty input as 'not fresh').

findings.title: Odos quotes for native-ETH legs use the 0xEeee sentinel where Odos expects the zero address — 'zero' normalization style returns the wrong constant
findings.evidence: aggregator.ts:31-40 — `case 'zero': return '0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE';` is byte-identical to the 'native' case, contradicting the style name; getOdosQuote (lines 116-117) is the only caller of 'zero'. Odos's documented native-token convention is 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000. If Odos rejects the 0xEeee form, getOdosQuote returns null silently (catch → null) and Odos never participates for ETH→TOWELI, the app's primary pair. Live verification attempt against api.odos.xyz returned HTTP 429 (rate limited), so this is code-vs-documented-API analysis, not a confirmed live failure — high-confidence but unverified at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Change the 'zero' branch to return the zero address and add a unit test pinning each aggregator's native-address convention; verify with one live Odos quote for ETH→TOWELI.

findings.title: On-chain quote reads fire per keystroke with no debounce, and quotes never auto-refresh — after 30s idle the first Swap click always bounces
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:88-95 — getAmountsOut useReadContract re-queries on every parsedAmount change (each keystroke creates a new query key; only the aggregator leg has the 800ms debounce at lines 229-249). Meanwhile the same read has no refetchInterval (only the reserves reads at lines 166/182/198 refresh every 30s), so a user who waits >30s hits the QUOTE_MAX_AGE_MS gate: executeSwap returns with toast 'Quote is stale — refreshing now' (useSwap.ts:343-347) — a guaranteed extra click on every considered trade. Uniswap auto-refreshes quotes (~per block) and debounces input.
findings.suggestion: Debounce parsedAmount (~300-500ms) before it reaches the read hooks, and add refetchInterval (10-15s) to the two getAmountsOut reads so a visible quote is always executable; optionally add a small countdown/refresh control (additive).

findings.title: Slippage and deadline are not persisted, and the deadline has state but no UI at all
findings.evidence: useSwap.ts:80-86 — `const [slippageRaw, setSlippageRaw] = useState(1.0)` and `const [deadline, setDeadline] = useState(5)` are plain state; nothing writes them to storage (grep: setDeadline is returned at useSwap.ts:532 but never called by any component). Every visit resets slippage to 1% and there is no way to change the 5-minute deadline. The codebase already persists far less important things (recent tokens, TokenSelectModal.tsx:33-49).
findings.suggestion: Persist slippage (and the FoT toggle) per-wallet in localStorage like recent tokens, and either render a deadline control in the settings cluster or remove the dead state; Uniswap persists both.

findings.title: ETH→WETH wrap is a dead flow: the pair is selectable but produces a 0 quote, and execution path would reject it as self-swap
findings.evidence: buildPath (useSwapQuote.ts:25-36) maps ETH→WETH to path [WETH, WETH]; getAmountsOut on an identical-token path reverts so output stays '0.0' and the button stays disabled; if a quote existed, executeSwap's guard (useSwap.ts:355-360) fires 'Cannot swap a token for itself'. TokenSelectModal only disables the literal other address (TradePage.tsx:524 disabledAddress), and ETH (0xEeee…) ≠ WETH (0xC02a…), so users can select the pair and get a silent dead form with no explanation — and the CoW limit flow explicitly tells users to 'wrap your ETH first' (LimitOrderTab.tsx:176) with no way to do it in-app.
findings.suggestion: Add a wrap/unwrap branch (WETH.deposit/withdraw) when the pair is ETH↔WETH — one writeContract, no router, no slippage — like Uniswap's wrap mode; at minimum show copy explaining wrap isn't supported.

findings.title: 'Compare all N+2 routes' count is wrong when a venue has no quote
findings.evidence: TradePage.tsx:411 `Compare all ${swap.allAggQuotes.length + 2} routes` hardcodes +2 for Tegridy and Uniswap, but the rows render conditionally (line 415 `swap.hasTegridyPair && swap.tegridyOutputFormatted &&` and line 421 `swap.uniOutputFormatted &&`). Today the Tegridy pool is empty so tegridyOutputFormatted is null — the button says e.g. 'Compare all 7 routes' and shows 6.
findings.suggestion: Compute the count from the actual renderable rows: allAggQuotes.length + (tegridyOutputFormatted ? 1 : 0) + (uniOutputFormatted ? 1 : 0).

findings.title: Price impact can show a positive % when the aggregator quote is BETTER than the pool mid-price (absolute diff)
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:381-387 single-hop branch: `const diff = midPriceScaled > execPriceScaled ? midPriceScaled - execPriceScaled : execPriceScaled - midPriceScaled;` — outputAmount here is the headline (possibly aggregator) output (line 319), so an aggregator quote above the Uniswap mid-price produces a positive 'Price Impact' even though the price is favorable; mixing the aggregator's exec price with Uniswap reserves is also venue-inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Compute impact from the executing on-chain route's own output (activeAmountsOut last element) rather than the headline outputAmount, and clamp favorable diffs to 0 (or show them as positive-green like Uniswap).

findings.title: addCustomToken skips on-chain verification when the wallet is on the wrong chain, but still stores the token into the mainnet-scoped list
findings.evidence: useSwap.ts:506-515 — `if (publicClient && chainId === CHAIN_ID) { ...verify... }` — when chainId !== CHAIN_ID the verification block is skipped entirely and execution falls through to `setCustomTokens(...)` (line 516), persisting into `tegridy_custom_tokens_v2_1` (the mainnet-scoped key, lines 94/135). TokenSelectModal's import reads also run on the connected chain (no chainId on the useReadContract at TokenSelectModal.tsx:169-181), so symbol/decimals can come from a different chain's contract. The FE-HIGH-6 rehydrate sweep would only evict it on a later mainnet load.
findings.suggestion: Refuse import when chainId !== CHAIN_ID (toast 'switch to mainnet to import tokens') or pin the modal's reads and the verification to chainId: CHAIN_ID.

findings.title: User's slippage setting is not forwarded to aggregator quote requests
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:233 — `getAggregatorPrice(sellToken, buyToken, parsedAmount.toString(), address, chainId, undefined, fromDecimals, ...)` passes undefined so every aggregator quote uses DEFAULT_MAX_SLIPPAGE_PCT 0.5% (aggregator.ts:19) regardless of the user's 0.1-20% setting, even though the hook receives `slippage` as a parameter and uses it for minimumReceived. Quotes whose venues consume slippage at quote time (SwapAPI/Odos/LiFi) therefore don't reflect the user's tolerance.
findings.suggestion: Pass the hook's `slippage` argument through (clampSlippage already bounds it); if uniform 0.5% ranking is the deliberate intent, document that and drop the unused parameter.

findings.title: SWAP_FEE_BPS hardcoded — fee display and route comparison silently wrong if the owner retunes feeBps on-chain
findings.evidence: constants.ts:104-108 `export const SWAP_FEE_BPS = 50; // 0.5%` with comment 'MUST stay in sync with … SwapFeeRouter.feeBps() (read on-chain if the owner ever retunes it)'. useSwapQuote.ts:274-276 nets the native-route quote with this constant and routeLabel discloses '(incl. 0.5% fee)' (line 426). A fee change on-chain would make the netting, the route choice, and the disclosure all wrong with no runtime check.
findings.suggestion: Read feeBps once via useReadContract (single view call, cacheable for the session) and fall back to the constant.

findings.title: useAddLiquidity reads are not chain-gated — wrong-network users see 'No pool exists … plant one' and zero balances
findings.evidence: useAddLiquidity.ts:42-48 (getPair, `query: { enabled: tokensSelected }`) and lines 54-71 (the 9-read batch, `query: { enabled: !!address … }`) have no chainId pin or onRightChain gate, unlike useSwapQuote.ts:81-82 which gates every read. On an L2, getPair targets TEGRIDY_FACTORY_ADDRESS on the wrong chain → pairExists false → LiquidityTab.tsx:501-504 renders 'No pool exists for this pair yet. Switch to Grow the Crop to plant one.' — misleading; writes are protected only by _ensureChain at lines 169-172.
findings.suggestion: Add `chainId: CHAIN_ID` to each read or gate enabled on chainId === CHAIN_ID and show a 'switch network' banner like the swap card does.

findings.title: Two separate custom-token stores: tokens imported in Swap don't appear in the Liquidity picker (and vice versa), and the liquidity store skips on-chain verification
findings.evidence: useSwap.ts:94 uses key `tegridy_custom_tokens_v2_${CHAIN_ID}` (with FE-HIGH-6 on-chain re-verification), while LiquidityTab.tsx:23 uses `tegridy_liquidity_custom_tokens` (no chain scoping, shape-only validation at lines 41-53, no on-chain symbol/decimals check). Same TokenSelectModal, different memories and different security posture.
findings.suggestion: Unify on the swap store (chain-scoped + verified) and pass it to both surfaces so the anti-spoof guarantees stay consistent.

findings.title: CoW path auto-approves unlimited (maxUint256) without the warning the swap surface mandates
findings.evidence: useCowLimitOrder.ts:147-153 — `args: [COW_VAULT_RELAYER_ADDRESS, maxUint256]` fires whenever allowance < sellAmount, preceded only by toast.info('Approve CoW to spend your sell token (one-time)'). The swap surface treats unlimited approval as opt-in with an explicit warning (useSwapAllowance.ts:185-193) and blocks it for custom tokens; here it's silent and mandatory. Vault-relayer unlimited approval is CoW's standard pattern, but it's inconsistent with the app's own stated stance.
findings.suggestion: Approve the exact sellAmount by default with an opt-in 'approve once for all future CoW orders' toggle, or at least reuse the unlimited-approval warning copy.

findings.title: MEV protection status not persisted — shows 'Add to wallet' every session even after adding
findings.evidence: useMevProtection.ts:34 `const [status, setStatus] = useState<MevProtectionStatus>('idle')` — plain state; nothing in the hook or MevProtectionPanel.tsx persists 'added', so the one-time setup is re-offered indefinitely. (Detecting the active RPC from the dapp is impossible, but the local 'user completed this' bit is persistable.)
findings.suggestion: Persist an 'added' flag per wallet address in localStorage and render 'Added ✓ — select the MEV Blocker network in your wallet' as the steady state, with a small re-add link.

findings.title: Tab bar mixes role=tab/aria-selected with aria-pressed and has no arrow-key navigation; quote updates have no aria-live
findings.evidence: TradePage.tsx:151-154 — each button has both `aria-selected={tab === t}` and `aria-pressed={tab === t}` under `role="tab"` (aria-pressed is invalid on tabs), there's no roving tabindex/Arrow-key handler for the tablist (WAI-ARIA tabs pattern), and the 'You Receive' value (lines 265-267) plus the route panel have no aria-live region, so screen readers never hear quote results. The token-select modal, by contrast, is fully wired (dialog role, focus trap, esc).
findings.suggestion: Drop aria-pressed on the tabs, add ArrowLeft/ArrowRight roving focus, and put aria-live="polite" on the receive amount + route summary.

findings.title: useSwapQuote's R042 HIGH-2 return memoization is defeated by unmemoized `path`/`routeDescription` arrays
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:75 `const path = fromToken && toToken ? buildPath(fromToken, toToken) : [];` builds a fresh array every render; `path` is in the return useMemo deps (line 496) and in priceImpact deps (line 391), so the 'wrap entire return in useMemo so consumers don't see a fresh identity' comment (lines 463-465) is ineffective — identity flips every render anyway (and the 1s ticker renders every second).
findings.suggestion: useMemo the path on [fromToken?.address, toToken?.address] (routeDescription then stabilizes too); cheap win that makes the existing memo wrapper actually work.

findings.title: Big TOWELI numbers render without thousands separators; quote loading is a bare '...' not a skeleton; tiny balances show as 0.0000
findings.evidence: formatting.ts:23-30 formatTokenAmount returns num.toFixed(4) for anything ≥ 0.0001 — a 75M TOWELI receive renders as '75000000.0000' (TradePage.tsx:266, 399, 418-431). The receive field while loading shows the literal string '...' (TradePage.tsx:266) rather than a shimmer/skeleton, and balances use raw Number(x).toFixed(4) (lines 206/251) so 0.00004 ETH displays as '0.0000'.
findings.suggestion: Add toLocaleString grouping (or compact 75.0M with a full-precision title tooltip) in formatTokenAmount, a small skeleton shimmer for the receive value, and floor-aware balance formatting ('<0.0001').

findings.title: PriceChart comment claims a same-origin proxy but fetches GeckoTerminal cross-origin — the Safari/Edge tracking-prevention problem the comment cites is still live; flip button hover is JS-only
findings.evidence: PriceChart.tsx:46-47 — comment 'Use same-origin proxy to avoid Edge/Safari tracking prevention blocking cross-origin API calls' sits directly above `const url = "https://api.geckoterminal.com/api/v2/..."` (direct cross-origin; CSP allows it). On ITP-aggressive browsers the fetch can fail and the component falls back to the GeckoTerminal iframe embed after 2 retries — functional but slower and contradicts the comment. Also TradePage.tsx:240-241 animates the flip button via onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave inline style mutation, so keyboard focus gets no equivalent affordance.
findings.suggestion: Either route OHLCV through the existing aggregator-proxy pattern (it can join the [provider] catchall without spending a Vercel function slot) or fix the comment; move the flip-button rotation to a CSS :hover/:focus-visible rule.

findings.title: Target-price field gives no market context — placeholder 25000000 is ~3x off current market and there's no live price reference
findings.evidence: LimitOrderTab.tsx:129-133 — placeholder="25000000" (TOWELI per ETH) with no current-price display anywhere in the tab; at current market (~$33k mcap / ~$0.000033 TOWELI) the real rate is roughly 70-80M TOWELI/ETH, so users must leave the app to know what a sane target is. The keeper fires on `currentPrice >= targetPrice` (useLimitOrders.ts:497) — without a reference, users will set already-met targets and trigger instant wallet prompts.
findings.suggestion: Show the live rate (one getAmountsOut for 1 ETH, already implemented in the poller) above the input with a 'use market' chip and ±1/5/10% quick buttons; the same helper benefits the CoW order builder.

good: Meta-aggregator design: 7 sources queried in parallel via Promise.allSettled with per-source response-shape validation (regex on amountOut), uniform clamped slippage (R045 M1), required chainId with short-circuit + defense-in-depth chain tag filtering (R045 H1), BigInt-safe sorting (aggregator.ts:339-391).

Quote race handling on the aggregator leg is genuinely correct: 800ms debounce + AbortController + monotonically increasing requestId guard so stale responses can never overwrite fresh ones (useSwapQuote.ts:219-251).

Hardened serverless aggregator proxy: single [provider] catchall (respects the Vercel 12-function cap), per-provider path/method/query allowlists, fail-closed origin gate incl. preview envs, Upstash rate limiting, 32KB body cap, bounded response reads, forced JSON content-type + nosniff, cookie/auth stripping (api/_lib/aggregator-proxy.js, api/aggregator/[provider]/[...path].js).

Quote staleness gate (30s, matching Uniswap's window) that blocks execution and forces refresh rather than letting a stale price sign (useSwapQuote.ts QUOTE_MAX_AGE_MS + useSwap.ts:343-347) — the refetch wiring has the gap noted in findings, but the gate itself is the right pattern.

Min-received honesty fix (R033 H-01 amended): the slippage floor derives from the venue that actually executes, displayed and submitted from the same formula — display==submit invariant (useSwapQuote.ts:393-406, useSwap.ts:377-383).

Native-route fee honesty: the Tegridy route is quoted and compared NET of the 0.5% protocol fee with a conservative linear haircut, only wins when it beats Uniswap after fees, and the route label discloses '(incl. 0.5% fee)' (useSwapQuote.ts:270-302, 422-429).

Custom-token security stack is best-in-class: chain-scoped localStorage with shape + spoofed-symbol validation on rehydrate, one-time on-chain symbol/decimals re-verification with eviction toasts, unlimited-approval hard-block for unverified tokens, permanent per-session unverified banner, EIP-55 checksum validation, scam-symbol import hard-block, Etherscan link before import-risk acceptance (useSwap.ts:88-180, useSwapAllowance.ts:95-111, TokenSelectModal.tsx:149-237, TradePage.tsx:184-200).

USDT-style two-step approve implemented properly (zero-write then target) with a state machine that survives wallet rejection and re-checks chainId before dispatching the second write (useSwapAllowance.ts:46-183).

Fee-on-transfer support: opt-in toggle + automatic detection on InsufficientOutput reverts with a one-tap retry that switches to the SupportingFeeOnTransferTokens router functions (useSwap.ts:288-313, 443-465).

TokenSelectModal is well-engineered: @tanstack/react-virtual list, focus trap, Escape close, body scroll lock, recent-tokens chips, image error fallbacks, full-screen mobile layout, bytes32-symbol lookup timeout fallback (MKR/SAI class).

DCA keeper concurrency control is unusually thorough: localStorage TTL lock + dedicated BroadcastChannel claim/release protocol + lock refresh at every async boundary + beforeunload release (useDCA.ts:9-121, 270-301); the R042 HIGH-5 Map+TTL fix in useLimitOrders prevents the cleanup-flush double-execution bug.

Honest-UX copy throughout the browser-keeper features: tabs renamed (DCA/Alerts), explicit 'browser-only, closing the tab stops execution' warnings, and the CoW path clearly marked as the real on-chain alternative (TradePage.tsx:21-34, DCATab.tsx:78-79, LimitOrderTab.tsx:110-111, 175-177).

CoW limit orders use the canonical GPv2 EIP-712 schema byte-for-byte with deterministic appData doc+hash, uint32 validTo overflow guard, balance + allowance prechecks, integer fixed-point limit math (no float drift into a signed amount), status polling with terminal-state short-circuit, and explorer.cow.fi links (cowProtocol.ts, useCowLimitOrder.ts, LimitOrderTab.tsx:69-104).

MEV protection is additive and consent-based: EIP-3085 wallet_addEthereumChain with user-rejection (4001/ACTION_REJECTED, cause-walking) classification and an honest manual-setup fallback; never silently swaps the user's RPC (mevProtection.ts, useMevProtection.ts).

PriceChart implementation quality: in-memory cache with TTL, retry with backoff + 429 handling, OHLC sanitation (zero/invalid filtering, hi/lo reordering, duplicate-timestamp dedupe for the lightweight-charts assertion), GeckoTerminal embed fallback with a deliberately tightened iframe sandbox, theme-aware chart chrome, ResizeObserver+rAF resizing, race-guarded loads.

Liquidity UX empathy: TGLP watchAsset one-tap wallet import, 'your liquidity is safe' panel with live redeemable-underlying amounts, impermanent-loss disclosure with concrete numbers, first-LP price-setting warning, slippage presets aligned with the swap tab.
Deep links work: ?tab= canonical knob with legacy /liquidity path synonym, Back/Forward sync, and shareable URLs written with replace:true (TradePage.tsx:38-90).
High-price-impact triple warning: red row styling >3%, banner >5%, plus the Towelie character nudge with dedup key (TradePage.tsx:110-119, 390-406).
missingVsBestInClass: USD value estimates under both amount fields and on Min Received (Uniswap/CoW show fiat everywhere; the app already has useToweliPrice + a Chainlink ETH/USD feed wired elsewhere).
Max / 25-50-75% balance buttons on the swap and liquidity inputs (with gas-reserve logic for native ETH).
No price chart on the Trade page itself — PriceChart exists but only renders on DashboardPage; an additive collapsible chart for the selected pair is table stakes (Dexscreener/Uniswap token view).

Pre-trade confirmation/simulation step: rate, route diagram, fee breakdown (protocol fee vs LP fee), gas estimate, and a typed-confirm gate for extreme price impact (Uniswap blocks >15% without explicit intent).
Exchange-rate row with invert toggle ('1 ETH = 75.2M TOWELI ↔ 1M TOWELI = 0.0133 ETH') and a quote auto-refresh countdown indicator.
Gas estimate display (aggregator quotes already return estimatedGas — it's fetched and then never shown anywhere).
Token-pair deep links (?inputCurrency/&outputCurrency like Uniswap) and persistence of the last-used pair; only the tab is in the URL today.
ETH↔WETH wrap/unwrap mode (currently a dead flow, see findings) and a one-tap 'wrap ETH' helper in the CoW order path which explicitly requires WETH.

EIP-5792 one-click approve+swap batching — the 38ac420 foundation (lib/eip5792.ts) is complete and tested but wired into nothing on the trade surface; wallets supporting atomic batch still get two prompts.
Recent-trades / transaction-history panel on the trade surface (lib/txHistory.ts exists; the success toast with explorer link is the only record).

Quote-while-disconnected: the entire swap form is replaced by the connect CTA, so prospects can't see pricing before connecting (Uniswap quotes without a wallet; the on-chain reads here don't need an address — only the aggregator leg does).
Pool stats on the Liquidity tab: TVL, 24h volume/fees, fee APR for the pair, and USD value of the user's position (Uniswap/Balancer-grade position cards).
Current-market-price reference + 'use market' helper in the Alerts/CoW limit flow, and a '% from market' indicator on the entered target.

Real aggregator/sell-side execution: quotes are compared across 7 venues but only on-chain venues are executable; CoW order placement code already exists (useCowLimitOrder) and could honestly capture the displayed aggregator savings as a market-order path.
pagesCovered: contracts/src/SwapFeeRouter.sol + contracts/script/DeployMVP.s.sol (cross-check: SFR inner router = TegridyRouter, SFR pulls via transferFrom(msg.sender))

findings.title: Homepage horizontally overflows: layout viewport expands to 414px on a 390px iPhone
findings.evidence: Measured via page.evaluate: scrollWidth=414, innerWidth=414 on '/' while ALL 20 other routes measure exactly 390/390 (results4.json). Wide-element scan pins the culprit: a decorative div with class 'absolute -left-6 -right-10 -top-8 -bottom-8 -z-10 pointer-events-none' measuring width 422px, left -8, right edge 414 — source: frontend/src/pages/HomePage.tsx:87. Visible consequence: with the nav menu open on home, 'Tegridy Score' (right edge 400), 'Treasury' (right 399) and the X close button (right 398) extend past the 390px visual viewport and render clipped (v7_home_menu.png vs the clean farm render in v7_farm_menu.png).
findings.suggestion: Add overflow-x-hidden/clip to the section wrapping HomePage.tsx:87, or reduce the -right-10 overhang (e.g. -right-4 inside an overflow-clipped parent). One-line fix that also fixes the clipped nav menu and the whole-page zoom-out on real iPhones.

findings.title: Unskippable ~10s art loader blocks EVERY deep link, every Safari session, and requires a tap to enter
findings.evidence: Run 1 (fresh context, no flags): all 21 routes captured ONLY the loader for 8+ seconds after load (iphone14_home_splash.png, iphone14_farm_1/2/3.png, iphone14_swap_1/2/3.png — full-screen rotating art with captions like 'POOL PARTY', 'CHAOS', 'NAKA #42'). 'TAP TO ENTER' (particle-rendered in canvas) only appears ~10s in (iphone14_home_2.png at ~9.8s; farm probe still showed art at 13s, probe_farm_after_tap6s.png shows TAP TO ENTER). A tap BEFORE the prompt appears does nothing (verified by probe). sessionStorage 'tf_loaded' is only set on completion (frontend/src/components/loader/AppLoader.tsx:31,536), so every new Safari session and every shared deep link (e.g. /risks, /contracts) replays the full gate before ANY content. Skip is ESC-only (AppLoader.tsx:130) — no touch equivalent on iPhone.
findings.suggestion: Keep the art moment but (a) show TAP TO ENTER (or a skip affordance) within 1-2s on touch devices, (b) consider gating only '/' and letting deep links (legal pages especially: /terms, /risks, /privacy) bypass, (c) persist the seen-flag in localStorage so returning visitors are not re-gated every session.

findings.title: First-visit overlay pile-up: onboarding modal + consent banner + Towelie bubble at once; consent buttons sit at the very bottom edge
findings.evidence: v3_home_1.png shows the 'Welcome to Tegridy Farms' modal stacked on the 'Privacy & telemetry' banner with the Decline/Accept buttons clipped at the viewport bottom edge. Re-captured solo in v5_home_consent_banner.png: button bottoms cut at the screenshot edge; DOM measurement puts Decline/Accept at top 819 / bottom 863 of an 896px layout viewport — i.e. inside the iOS home-indicator/toolbar zone on a real iPhone 14 (Safari bottom bar overlaps that band).
findings.suggestion: Add safe-area padding (env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) below the consent buttons, and sequence the overlays (consent first, onboarding after dismiss) so a first-time mobile user is not facing three layers at once.

findings.title: Towelie assistant bubble auto-pops on each route and occludes content, inputs, data, and even the open nav menu
findings.evidence: Fixed bottom-left bubble appears ~2.2s after every route's first visit (TowelieAssistant.tsx ROUTE_TIP_DELAY_MS, per-route 'towelie:seen:' keys). Observed covering: the earn-calculator TOWELI input (v4_home_1.png), the FDV stat value (v4_tokenomics_1.png), story text (v4_lore_1.png), the '38,794 lines of test code' stat (v4_security_1.png), the TVL card values (v4_treasury_1.png), footer legal links Risk Disclosure/Security on nearly every page's bottom (v4_gallery_3.png, v4_terms_3.png), and it renders ON TOP of the opened nav drawer (v7_farm_menu.png z-order conflict).
findings.suggestion: On <640px viewports: delay until idle, never overlap the open nav drawer (z-index below it), and offset above the tab bar so it stops covering footer legal links. Consider one global first-visit tip instead of per-route pops.

findings.title: No path to Farm/Swap/Dashboard from the homepage menu — tab bar absent on home and the hamburger only holds 4 secondary links
findings.evidence: The bottom tab bar (Dashboard/Farm/Trade/Tradermigos) is present on app routes (v4_farm_1.png) but absent on '/' (v4_home_1.png, v4_home_3.png). The hamburger drawer contains only ENGAGE (Gallery, Tegridy Score) and STATS (Tokenomics, Treasury) — DOM enumeration found exactly 4 links (menu3.cjs output; v7_home_menu.png). A mobile visitor on the homepage has no menu route to the core product pages; they must find in-page CTAs.
findings.suggestion: Either show the tab bar on '/' too, or add Farm/Trade/Dashboard links to the drawer. The drawer is ~90% empty vertical space (v7_farm_menu.png), so there is room.

findings.title: Page subtitles set in white directly over busy/light artwork are illegible at 390px
findings.evidence: v4_security_1.png: the subtitle's last line '...battle-tested smart contract design' crosses the white skull artwork and disappears. v4_faq_1.png: intro paragraph 'Look. We're not gonna bullshit you...' over pastel pink/blue art is barely readable. v4_dashboard_1.png: 'View your portfolio, positions, and earnings' lost in the camo-ape art. v4_swap_1.png / v4_liquidity_1.png: header subtitles wash out over bright barn art. v4_nft-finance_1.png: 'institutional-grade tools, all in one place' crosses light painting areas.
findings.suggestion: Add a consistent scrim (e.g. gradient or backdrop blur band) or text-shadow behind hero/subtitle text. The dark cards on the same pages are perfectly readable — only the over-art text suffers.

findings.title: Translucent sticky pill bar collides with H1s and ghosts underlying text through it
findings.evidence: v4_risks_1.png: 'Risk Disclosure' H1 partially tucked under the Treasury/Contracts/Risks/Terms/Privacy pill bar. v4_terms_1.png: 'Terms of Service' nearly touching the pills. v4_privacy_3.png (full-res): footer links ('...adermigos', '...angelog', 'FAQ') visibly double-exposed through the translucent pill bar while scrolled.
findings.suggestion: Increase the sticky bar's background opacity/blur and add scroll-margin-top to page H1s.

findings.title: Bottom tab chip row clips its 4th chip mid-word with no scroll affordance
findings.evidence: v4_nft-finance_1.png: chip row reads 'Token Lending | NFT Lending | NFT AMM | Launch…' with the last chip cut at the right edge and no fade/arrow hinting horizontal scrollability.
findings.suggestion: Add a right-edge fade gradient or wrap chips to two rows at <420px.

findings.title: Every route fires CSP-blocked and CORS-failed RPC/price requests; likely feeds the 'Price oracle is stale' banner
findings.evidence: Console on all 21 routes (results.json/results4.json): (1) 'Connecting to https://eth.merkle.io/ violates connect-src' repeated 4+ times per page — a wagmi/viem default fallback RPC not in the CSP allowlist; (2) 'https://eth.llamarpc.com/ blocked by CORS policy' + net::ERR_FAILED on every route; (3) 'https://api.geckoterminal.com/.../token_price/0x4206...8f9d blocked by CORS' on /liquidity, /dashboard, /lore, /security. /treasury then shows 'Price oracle is stale. USD figures shown derive from a delayed price feed' (v4_treasury_1.png).
findings.suggestion: Remove eth.merkle.io from the transport list (or add it to connect-src), drop llamarpc from browser-side transports (CORS-broken), and proxy the GeckoTerminal price call through the existing serverless API to restore USD figures.

findings.title: Background art speech-text bleeds behind UI panels and tier rows fade under the sub-nav
findings.evidence: v4_leaderboard_1.png: art captions ('...THIS TOWEL GETS...POINTS? IT'S A BEAR...SO EPIC!') half-visible behind the 'How Points Work' panel and +10/+25 chips, reading as broken text rather than background. v4_leaderboard_2.png: 'Degen'/'Connector' tier rows clipped fading under the sticky sub-nav mid-scroll.
findings.suggestion: Dim or blur the art layer behind the points panels so stray art words don't read as UI text.

good: Zero horizontal overflow on 20 of 21 routes — measured scrollWidth == innerWidth == 390 everywhere except '/' (results4.json). The grid/card system genuinely fits 390px.

Bottom mobile tab bar (Dashboard / Farm / Trade / Tradermigos) on app routes is excellent: 44px+ targets, clear active state, icons + labels, never overlapped by content (v4_farm_1.png, v4_gallery_3.png full-res).
Hamburger button is a proper 44x44 target with aria-label 'Open navigation menu'; drawer links have generous spacing and tap targets (v7_farm_menu.png).

Farm stat cards (STAKING APR / REWARD POOL / DAILY EMISSIONS / MAX BOOST / FEE SHARE) form a clean 2-column grid at 390px with no number truncation, and the APR carries an honest 'early-TVL bootstrap rate' caption (v4_farm_1.png).

Long-form pages (/terms, /privacy, /risks, /security, /changelog) are genuinely readable on mobile: comfortable line length, consistent type scale, accordion FAQ rows full-width and tappable (v4_terms_1.png, v4_risks_2.png, v4_faq_1.png).

Contract addresses truncate elegantly (0x420698...278f9D) with copy buttons and right-aligned mono values; the /contracts index with PENDING DEPLOY / AWAITING MULTISIG status chips scans well at 390px (v4_contracts_1/2.png).

Empty and pending states are honest and well-designed: Gold Card 'SOON' explainer (v4_premium_1.png), 'Connect to farm with tegridy' (v4_farm_1.png), treasury's stale-oracle warning with on-chain-is-authoritative note (v4_treasury_1.png), points 'No participants yet' (v4_leaderboard_1.png).

The splash art itself renders beautifully at 390px — full-bleed art uncropped at the subject, particle 'TEGRIDY FARMS' title fits the width, 44px mute button (iphone14_home_splash.png, iphone14_home_3.png) — the issue is its duration/gating, not its rendering.
No JavaScript pageerrors on any of the 21 routes, and no navigation failures (all goto's succeeded; results4.json pageErrors empty everywhere).
Onboarding modal is well-sized for 390px with dot pagination and a reachable Next button (v3_home_1.png).
viewport:mobile-main.splashAndTransitions: Splash (AppLoader): a full-screen canvas art slideshow with audio mute control; visually superb at 390px (art uncropped, particle-lettered title fits, TAP TO ENTER legible) — but it is a hard gate: ~10s of unskippable art before TAP TO ENTER appears, replays on every new Safari session AND on every deep-linked route until tapped (sessionStorage flag only set on completion; ESC skip is keyboard-only so unavailable on iPhone). In a fresh session, all 21 routes were unreachable behind it. After the gate: page-to-page transitions are instant SPA swaps with no skeletons observed; short pages (/swap, /liquidity, /dashboard, /history, /premium, /community) land directly on content with empty-state cards rather than spinners, which reads fine. The per-route Towelie bubble pop-in (~2.2s after each navigation) is effectively a second, recurring 'transition overlay' and is the most intrusive motion element after the splash. First-visit on '/' stacks splash, then onboarding modal + consent banner + Towelie bubble nearly simultaneously — the consent Decline/Accept row sits in the iOS home-indicator zone (measured bottom 863/896).
viewport:mobile-main.consoleAndNetwork: Repeated on ALL 21 routes (identical pattern, captured in results.json/results4.json): (1) CSP violation x4+ per page — 'Connecting to https://eth.merkle.io/ violates connect-src' + 'Fetch API cannot load https://eth.merkle.io/' (wagmi/viem default fallback RPC missing from the CSP allowlist); (2) CORS failure x2 per page — 'https://eth.llamarpc.com/ blocked by CORS policy: no Access-Control-Allow-Origin on preflight' + net::ERR_FAILED; (3) on /liquidity, /dashboard, /lore, /security: 'https://api.geckoterminal.com/api/v2/simple/networks/eth/token_price/0x420698cf...f9d blocked by CORS' + net::ERR_FAILED — browser-side price fetch dead, consistent with the /treasury 'Price oracle is stale' banner. Zero uncaught pageerrors; zero navigation failures; no 4xx/5xx from first-party API observed during captures.
pagesCovered: / (home, incl. splash gate, onboarding modal, consent banner, nav menu open)

findings.title: Commit-reveal commitIndex is guessed and persisted before tx confirmation — failed commits poison reveal indices; promised reconciliation is never implemented
findings.evidence: VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:1290-1302 — handleCommitVote calls bribes.commitVote(...) then immediately saves a record with `const tentativeIndex = existing.length; // contract pushes to same array so index ≈ current length` and the comment at :1295 says "we'll reconcile by reading voterCommits.length on next refetch" — but `voterCommits` is never read anywhere in the frontend (grep: only the ABI entry at contracts.ts:286 and this comment match). If the commit tx is rejected/fails, a phantom record persists in localStorage with no UI to delete it, and every subsequent commit gets an off-by-N commitIndex. revealVote(epoch, commitIndex, pair, power, salt) (useBribes.ts:218-228) with a wrong index reverts; per the UI's own copy ("Commits not revealed before the deadline lose their bond to treasury", VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:901) the 10 TOWELI bond is then forfeit. Reveal also never removes the record on success, allowing double-reveal attempts.
findings.suggestion: Read voterCommits length/entries (or watch the commit event for the emitted index) on confirmation, assign the real commitIndex then, only persist records after receipt success (keep the salt staged separately pre-broadcast like GaugeVoting does), and add a 'dismiss stale commit' affordance.

findings.title: Bounty funnel is broken end-to-end: no UI to view submissions, vote on them, complete, cancel, or refund a bounty
findings.evidence: MEME_BOUNTY_BOARD_ABI (contracts.ts:134-152) exposes voteForSubmission, getSubmission, submissionCount, completeBounty, cancelBounty, refundStaleBounty, hasVotedOnBounty — none are used in BountiesSection.tsx (only createBounty, submitWork, withdrawPayout/Refund, getBounty reads). The card copy promises "Community votes on submissions. Winner takes the reward." (BountiesSection.tsx:181) and rows show "{Number(submCount)} submissions" (:247), but submissions can never be listed, voted on, or finalized from the UI, so no winner can ever be picked without raw Etherscan calls.
findings.suggestion: Add an expanded-row submissions list (getSubmission × submissionCount) with vote buttons, a Complete button when conditions are met, plus creator-facing Cancel and permissionless refundStaleBounty actions.

findings.title: Legacy routes redirect to bare /community so /bounties and /bribes land on the wrong tab (Governance)
findings.evidence: App.tsx:150 `<Route path="bounties" element={<Navigate to="/community" replace />} />` and :153 `<Route path="bribes" element={<Navigate to="/community" replace />} />` drop the section; CommunityPage.tsx:43 defaults to 'grants' when ?section= is absent. The page's own comment (:29-30) promises deep-links "land on the right tab", and no internal link anywhere uses /community?section= (grep across src), so old bookmarks/external links to /bounties and /bribes silently open the Governance tab. /grants and /governance only work by coincidence of the default.
findings.suggestion: Redirect path="bounties" → /community?section=bounties and path="bribes" → /community?section=bribes.

findings.title: Active deadlines render as 'Ends just now' / 'just now' — formatTimeAgo returns 'just now' for every future timestamp
findings.evidence: formatting.ts:42-44 — `const seconds = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000 - timestamp); if (seconds < 5) return 'just now';` — a future deadline yields negative seconds, which always satisfies `< 5`. GrantsSection.tsx:286 `Ends ${formatTimeAgo(deadlineNum).replace(' ago', ' left')}` and BountiesSection.tsx:260 use this for non-expired items, so every live proposal/bounty shows "Ends just now" / "just now" instead of "6d left". The .replace(' ago',' left') hack never matches because 'just now' contains no ' ago'.
findings.suggestion: Add a formatTimeLeft/formatCountdown helper for future timestamps (one already exists in VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:54) instead of string-replacing formatTimeAgo output.

findings.title: Claimables panel formats every bribe token with formatEther (18 decimals) and shows raw addresses instead of known symbols
findings.evidence: VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:474-478 — `{formatTokenAmount(formatEther(c.amounts[i] ?? 0n), 4)} {tok.toLowerCase() === ZERO_ADDRESS ? 'ETH' : shortenAddress(tok)}`. A 6-decimal whitelisted token (e.g. USDC-like) would display 10^12× too small. GaugeRow does this correctly with whitelistMap meta (`formatUnits(b.amount, meta.decimals)`, :615), but whitelistMap is never passed to ClaimablesPanel, which also degrades symbols to 0x-short addresses.
findings.suggestion: Pass whitelistMap into ClaimablesPanel and format with formatUnits(amount, meta.decimals) + meta.symbol, falling back to formatEther/shortenAddress only for unknown tokens.

findings.title: GaugeVoting transaction errors are never surfaced — the try/catch around writeContract is dead code and the hook's error field is ignored
findings.evidence: GaugeVoting.tsx:109 destructures `const { writeContract, data: txHash, isPending: isSigning } = useWriteContract();` (no `error`), and :217-225 / :252-260 / :269-277 wrap `writeContract(...)` in try/catch → surfaceTxError. wagmi v2's non-async writeContract reports failures via the hook's error state, not by throwing synchronously, so a wallet rejection or revert produces no toast and no UI state change — the button just snaps back. Contrast useBribes.ts:344-348, which handles `writeError` with a toast.
findings.suggestion: Read `error` from useWriteContract (and isError from useWaitForTransactionReceipt) and surface via surfaceTxError/toast in an effect, mirroring useBribes.

findings.title: No tx success/error feedback and no refetch after writes — votes/creates leave stale UI and a dangling 'Voting FOR...' toast
findings.evidence: GrantsSection.tsx:40-41 and BountiesSection.tsx:43-44 use useWriteContract/useWaitForTransactionReceipt but never read error/isSuccess; handleVote fires `toast.info(support ? 'Voting FOR...' : ...)` (GrantsSection.tsx:83) before the wallet prompt and nothing follows on confirm/reject. None of the reads (proposalCount, getProposal, hasVotedOnProposal, bounty reads) set refetchInterval or refetch on receipt, so after a successful vote the "You have already voted" state and vote bars stay stale until window refocus.
findings.suggestion: Add an isSuccess/isError effect (success toast + targeted refetch of proposals/voteChecks) and an error toast for rejection, like useBribes does.

findings.title: Entire Community page is connect-walled — public read-only data (proposals, bounties, bribe leaderboard, gauge weights) is invisible without a wallet
findings.evidence: CommunityPage.tsx:111-133 — `{!isConnected ? (<ConnectButton card>) : (<tab panels>)}` hides all four sections behind useAccount().isConnected, even though every list is a public contract read that works with no address (the sections already handle `address` being undefined, e.g. GrantsSection voteCheckContracts returns [] at :67). Disconnected users can't even see the FeatureNotDeployed "coming soon" panels. Hidden Hand/Votium/Snapshot all render markets and proposals read-only.
findings.suggestion: Render the section content always; gate only the write affordances (vote/deposit/create buttons) behind connection with inline Connect CTAs.

findings.title: Proposal lifecycle actions missing: no Execute, Cancel, or Lapse UI despite ABI support and '24h execution delay' copy
findings.evidence: COMMUNITY_GRANTS_ABI (contracts.ts:128-130) includes executeProposal, cancelProposal, lapseProposal; GrantsSection only wires voteOnProposal + finalizeProposal (:76-93). The form copy says "Quorum-based approval with 24h execution delay" (:198) but a Passed (status 1) proposal shows no Execute button — STATUS_LABELS knows 'Passed'/'Executed'/'Lapsed' (:16-23) yet nothing in the UI can move a proposal between them.
findings.suggestion: Add Execute (when status=Passed and delay elapsed), proposer Cancel, and permissionless Lapse buttons on the relevant statuses.

findings.title: Lists are capped at the latest 10 items with no pagination — older proposals/bounties become unreachable
findings.evidence: GrantsSection.tsx:51-52 `const pageSize = Math.min(count, 10); const startIdx = Math.max(0, count - pageSize);` and BountiesSection.tsx:59-63 build read arrays for only the last 10 ids. There is no Load-more, page controls, or per-id deep link, so item #0-#N-11 of an active board can never be viewed.
findings.suggestion: Add a 'Load older' cursor that extends the multicall window, or numbered pagination.

findings.title: Banner instructs users to 'export the salt' but no export affordance exists
findings.evidence: GaugeVoting.tsx:410 — "Keep this browser's localStorage intact, or export the salt before then." There is no copy/download/QR button anywhere in the component; loadCommitment/saveCommitment (:31-47) are localStorage-only. A user following the UI's own advice has to open devtools. Losing the salt is explicitly fatal per :413 ("Without the salt this vote cannot be revealed").
findings.suggestion: Add a 'Copy reveal backup' button that serializes the CommitmentRecord (and a paste-to-restore input on the reveal panel). Same applies to the bribes-tab CommitRecord store.

findings.title: Loading state is conflated with empty state — 'No proposals yet' / 'No bounties yet' flashes while reads are in flight
findings.evidence:
GrantsSection.tsx:50 `const count = proposalCount !== undefined ? Number(proposalCount) : 0;` then :250 `{count === 0 ? (

No proposals yet. Be the first to create one.

) : ...}` — while proposalCount is undefined (loading) the empty copy renders. Same in BountiesSection.tsx:58 + :223. Also, when count>0 but proposalResults is still undefined, the list body renders blank with no skeleton. The CommunityPage Suspense skeleton (CommunityPage.tsx:143-150) never shows because the sections are statically imported, not React.lazy, and wagmi hooks don't suspend.
findings.suggestion: Branch on `proposalCount === undefined` to show a row skeleton (the bribes leaderboard at VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:1431-1451 is the in-house pattern to copy).

findings.title: Gauge rows show only truncated addresses — pair labels exist in useGaugeList but GaugeVoting doesn't use them
findings.evidence:
GaugeVoting.tsx:368 `

{shortenAddress(gauge, 6)}

` and the ballot summary at :483 also shows shortenAddress. The sibling bribes tab resolves human labels ("TOWELI / WETH") via useGaugeList (useGaugeList.ts:157-159), so the same epoch's gauges read as friendly names on one tab and as 0x1234…abcd on the next — voters can't tell which pool they're weighting.
findings.suggestion: Reuse useGaugeList for labels in GaugeVoting (it already memoizes and event-refreshes).

findings.title: Duplicate 'Transaction confirmed' toasts possible from the isSuccess effect re-running
findings.evidence: GaugeVoting.tsx:281-291 — effect deps are `[isSuccess, hasVotedThisEpoch, commitmentKey, refetchRevealWindow]`; after a reveal confirms, isSuccess stays true (no reset() is ever called on useWriteContract) and when the lastVotedEpoch read later flips hasVotedThisEpoch to true the effect re-runs, firing toast.success a second time before clearing the commitment. Also means the cleanup of the localStorage record is deferred until that read refreshes (no explicit refetch of lastVotedEpoch).
findings.suggestion: Track the toasted hash (or call reset() after handling, as useBribes.ts:341 does) and explicitly refetch lastVotedEpoch on receipt.

findings.title: Nested <button> inside <button>: SafeText 'show more' renders inside the row-expand button (invalid HTML, a11y hazard)
findings.evidence: BountiesSection.tsx:241 `<button onClick={() => setExpandedBounty(...)} className="w-full text-left">` wraps :250 `<SafeText value={description} previewChars={180} />`; SafeText.tsx:42-53 renders its own `<button>` when text exceeds 180 chars (descriptions can be 1000, textSafety.ts:55). Nested interactive controls are invalid HTML — browsers may re-parent the inner button, and screen readers/keyboard focus get a control inside a control. GrantsSection avoids this (SafeText sits in a plain div).
findings.suggestion: Make the row header a div with role=button/tabIndex like the gallery cards, or move SafeText outside the toggle button.

findings.title: handleCreate calls parseEther/Number on unvalidated inputs — '1e5'-style reward throws uncaught in the click handler; 0 or negative deadline passes to chain
findings.evidence: BountiesSection.tsx:86 `value: parseEther(newReward)` has no try/catch (viem throws InvalidDecimalNumberError on exponent notation, which number inputs permit), unlike GrantsSection.tsx:121-127 which guards the same call. :81 `Number(newDeadlineDays) * 86400` accepts '0' or negative ('0' is truthy so the `!newDeadlineDays` guard passes), producing an in-past deadline that reverts on-chain after gas. No belowMin/insufficient-balance checks either, unlike the bribes DepositCard.
findings.suggestion: Mirror GrantsSection's validation: try/catch parseEther with toast, require deadlineDays >= 1, and disable the submit button on invalid values.

findings.title: Header copy '54 original hand-drawn pieces from the Tegridy universe' misdescribes the collection — 31 of 54 are the Nakamigos drop
findings.evidence: GalleryPage.tsx:88 `{GALLERY_ORDER.length} original hand-drawn pieces from the Tegridy universe`; GALLERY_ORDER (artConfig.ts:276-302) interleaves 23 Tegridy pieces with naka01–naka31, whose entries are titled 'Naka #x' / 'Fresh from the deck' (artConfig.ts:46-76) — an external NFT collection's images, not original hand-drawn Tegridy art.
findings.suggestion: Adjust the copy additively (e.g. 'original Tegridy art plus the Nakamigos drop') — keep all art per the owner's constraint.

findings.title: Tablist lacks the ARIA tabs keyboard pattern and tab/panel wiring; selected-state ternary is dead code
findings.evidence: CommunityPage.tsx:84-108 — role="tablist"/role="tab" with aria-selected, but no arrow-key roving tabindex, no id/aria-controls linking tabs to the role="tabpanel" (:136), and when disconnected the tablist renders with no tabpanel at all. :95 `section === key ? 'text-white' : 'text-white hover:text-white'` — both branches are identical, so the inactive-tab dimming this clearly intended never happens (the emerald pill is the only indicator).
findings.suggestion: Add ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handling + aria-controls/id pairs, and make the inactive branch text-white/60.

findings.title: All 54 grid images are loading="lazy" including the above-the-fold first rows, and the 800×800 size hint mismatches real aspect ratios (CLS in the masonry columns)
findings.evidence: GalleryPage.tsx:117-126 — every card img gets `width={800} height={800} loading="lazy"`. Lazy-loading first-viewport images delays LCP; the square aspect-ratio hint reserves the wrong box for non-square pieces so the CSS-columns layout (`columns-1 sm:columns-2 md:columns-3`, :101) reflows as each image decodes.
findings.suggestion: Eager-load (+fetchpriority="high") the first ~6 items and store real intrinsic dimensions per piece in artConfig for accurate aspect-ratio reservation.

findings.title: Lightbox doesn't restore focus to the opener on close, has no touch swipe, and doesn't preload adjacent images
findings.evidence: ArtLightbox.tsx:42-74 implements a solid focus trap and arrow/Escape keys, but onClose never returns focus to the triggering grid card (focus drops to <body> — WCAG 2.4.3 concern); there are no touch/swipe handlers for mobile prev/next (buttons only); navigating waits on a fresh network fetch of pieces[selectedIndex±1].
findings.suggestion: Store the opener element and .focus() it on close; add pointer/swipe navigation; render hidden <link rel=preload>/Image() for neighbors.

findings.title: Vote affordance is invisible to disconnected users and live re-sorting teleports the card you just voted for
findings.evidence: GalleryPage.tsx:138 `{isConnected && (...vote button...)}` — vote counts are hidden entirely without a wallet, so the social-proof layer disappears. sortedPieces re-sorts on every vote (:74-77), so upvoting a piece can instantly move it to a different column position under the cursor. Also the card wrapper is role="button" containing the real vote <button> (:104-141) — nested interactive controls in the a11y tree (the comment at :103 only solved literal button-in-button).
findings.suggestion: Show counts (disabled button + 'connect to vote' tooltip) when disconnected; defer re-sort until next mount or add layout animation (framer layout prop) so movement is legible.

findings.title: Heavy per-render read fan-out: ~17+ contract reads per gauge across 6 polling intervals; event watchers only refresh hook-level queries
findings.evidence: VoteIncentivesSection.tsx — per gauge: 2 vote reads @30s (:1040-1064), token list @60s (:1080-1090), per-token amounts @60s (:1109-1115), 10 history epochs @120s (:1126-1136), 5 claimable epochs @60s (:1178-1190), plus useBribes' own 9 global + 6-per-whitelisted-token reads @60s. useBribes' refetchAll (useBribes.ts:294-298) triggered by its 5 event watchers refetches only the hook's queries, not these section-level ones, which rely solely on their intervals. Multicall batching makes this workable but it scales linearly with gauge count and runs even when the tab content is unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Consolidate into fewer useReadContracts batches keyed by epoch, drop history lookback to on-demand (expand row), and pipe the event-watcher refresh through the section queries via queryClient invalidation.

findings.title: Suspense fallback is dead code and the gauges tab bypasses the FeatureNotDeployed pattern used by the other three tabs
findings.evidence: CommunityPage.tsx:10-13 imports all sections statically (no React.lazy), so the Suspense fallback at :143-150 can never render. :160 `{section === 'gauges' && <GaugeVoting />}` has no page-level isDeployed gate; GaugeVoting falls back to a bespoke minimal card ("Gauge controller not deployed yet", GaugeVoting.tsx:298-308) instead of the standard FeatureNotDeployed SOON panel with title/subtitle that grants/bounties/bribes get (:151-159). Bribes is double-gated (page + VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:1341-1351 has a second, plainer guard that is now unreachable).
findings.suggestion: Either lazy() the section imports so the skeleton works, or remove the fallback; gate gauges with FeatureNotDeployed for consistency.

findings.title: RescueBanner tells depositors to call refundOrphanedBribe and advanceEpoch 'below' but provides no refund button
findings.evidence: VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:217-221 — banner copy: "any depositor can pull their own bribes back via refundOrphanedBribe(epoch, pair, token). Trigger advanceEpoch below…". advanceEpoch has a footer chip (:1533-1537) but no UI anywhere calls refundOrphanedBribe (grep: only the two copy mentions). A depositor in the rescue window must use Etherscan.
findings.suggestion: When the window is open, render per-(pair, token) Refund buttons for the connected depositor's net contributions.

findings.title: Stat card hardcodes 'per epoch (7 days)' while EPOCH_DURATION is read from chain
findings.evidence: GaugeVoting.tsx:328 `sub: 'per epoch (7 days)'` is a literal; :129 reads `EPOCH_DURATION` with a 604800 fallback into `duration`, which is used for the countdown but not the copy — a redeploy with a different duration would show a wrong label.
findings.suggestion: Derive the label from `duration` (e.g. `per epoch (${duration/86400} days)`).

findings.title: Art-index reuse and premature toasts
findings.evidence: CommunityPage.tsx:153 and :159 both pass `pageId="community" idx={1}` to FeatureNotDeployed, so the Governance and Vote-Incentives placeholders show the identical backdrop while idx 2 is used for bounties. GrantsSection.tsx:83/144 and BountiesSection.tsx:88/104 fire toast.info('Voting FOR…' / 'Creating…') before the wallet prompt — a rejected signature strands an optimistic toast. useBribes.ts:345 toasts 'Transaction failed' for user rejections too (writeError doesn't distinguish), which reads as a protocol failure.
findings.suggestion: Use distinct art idx values; move toasts to post-signature (hash available) and special-case UserRejectedRequestError with a neutral 'Transaction cancelled'.

findings.title: Zero-fee and pending-fee-to-zero states render as missing data; first-voter advantage not surfaced
findings.evidence: OverviewStrip (VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:282) shows '--' when `feeBps > 0` is false, so a legitimately 0% fee displays as no-data; PendingFeeBanner (:163) hides when `pending === 0`, so a queued fee cut to 0% is invisible. GaugeRow's marginal-earn badge requires `totalVotes > 0n` (:555), so the single most attractive state — a bribed gauge with zero votes where 1k votes takes the whole pot — shows no earn hint at all.
findings.suggestion: Treat fee as loaded-vs-unloaded (undefined) rather than zero-vs-nonzero, and show 'first voter takes the full pot' on bribed zero-vote gauges.

findings.title: DepositCard approve→deposit is a two-click flow with no step indicator; one-at-a-time button label is the only signal
findings.evidence: VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:710-717 — handleSubmit calls onApprove when needsApproval, then the user must click again after the allowance refetch flips the label (:822-824 'Approve TOKEN' → 'Deposit …'). The codebase already ships a StepIndicator component for multi-tx flows (InfoTooltip.tsx:207-249) that is unused here.
findings.suggestion: Drop in StepIndicator (Approve → Deposit) above the button so projects depositing ERC20 bribes see the two-step shape upfront.

findings.title: InfoTooltip can clip at viewport edges; tab switches use replace so Back doesn't traverse tabs
findings.evidence: InfoTooltip.tsx:63-67 positions a fixed w-56 bubble centered on the icon with translate only — icons near the screen edge (e.g. the leaderboard header tooltips on a 390px iPhone) will overflow horizontally; there is no collision detection (unverified at runtime — code-level assessment). CommunityPage.tsx:50 `setSearchParams(params, { replace: true })` means tab changes create no history entries, so browser Back leaves the page rather than returning to the prior tab (consistent with LendingPage, but worth a deliberate decision).
findings.suggestion: Add a simple edge-flip/clamp to InfoTooltip; consider push semantics for tab changes or document the choice.

good: URL-as-source-of-truth tab state (CommunityPage.tsx:40-51): section derived from ?section= with validation, default tab keeps a clean bare URL, shareable links — mirrors the LendingPage pattern (consistent app-wide).

Chain-safety discipline on every write: chainId pinned in all writeContract calls + pre-flight _ensureChain toasts (GrantsSection.tsx:36-39, BountiesSection.tsx:39-42, useBribes.ts throughout), and the standout R-CHAINID guard in VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:879-883 that blocks commit-hash construction on the wrong chain because a wrong-chainid hash would silently forfeit the bond.

GaugeVoting commit-reveal persistence done right where it matters most: salt saved to localStorage BEFORE broadcasting (GaugeVoting.tsx:247-251), keys scoped per (chainId, voter, tokenId, epoch), and an explicit red warning when an on-chain commitment exists but the local salt is missing (:412-414).

Stored-XSS hardening on user content: sanitizeUserText strips BiDi/Trojan-Source and control chars on write AND render, SafeText caps display with show-more, bounty URIs allowlisted to https/ipfs/ar with data: excluded (textSafety.ts, SafeText.tsx, BountiesSection R069 wiring).

Bribes leaderboard UX is genuinely Votium-grade in places: search/sort/hide-empty controls, shape-matching loading skeleton with role=status (VoteIncentivesSection.tsx:1431-1451), marginal earn-rate badge (≈ETH per 1k votes) and projected-earn preview, fee + net-pool preview, min-bribe and insufficient-balance validation with 'contract would revert' messaging, non-contiguous epoch ranges rendered honestly (:449-459), batched multi-epoch claims, and pull-pattern refund surfacing (PendingWithdrawalsPanel).

Persona-split information architecture on the bribes tab ('For projects' / 'For voters' cards with jump anchors) plus tooltip-annotated How-It-Works steps — strong objective clarity for a two-sided market.
useBribes hook: 5 contract-event watchers driving refetch, success/error toasts with deferred reset, multicall-batched global + per-token reads — the most complete tx-lifecycle handling on the page.

isDeployed gating end-to-end: zero-address contracts render FeatureNotDeployed 'SOON' panels instead of tx-firing UI (CommunityPage.tsx:151-159), and navConfig hides the Community nav entry entirely while all four contracts are zeroed (navConfig.ts:77-80) — the app doesn't advertise emptiness.
ErrorBoundary wraps the tab panels and remounts per section (key={section} on the m.div), so a crash in one tab can't latch the others; errors are reported via reportError.
GrantsSection form validation: isAddress + parseEther try/catch + positive-amount checks with aria-invalid, role=alert inline errors, char-counter with amber warning — best-practice form a11y.
ArtLightbox a11y: working focus trap, Escape/Arrow keys, body scroll lock, aria-modal/aria-label, 44px touch targets; gallery cards are keyboard-operable (Enter/Space) with descriptive aria-labels.

Gallery honesty: 'Votes are for fun only — stored locally in your browser, not on-chain' disclosure + sr-only repeat, per-address vote keying, 800ms vote debounce, quota-safe storage via safeSetItem with eviction.
ArtImg primitive: PLACEHOLDER_NFT onError fallback, default width/height to reserve layout, decoding=async, art-studio override support — used consistently across all backdrops.
WrongChainBanner shared primitive on the page head with a custom message and one-click switchChain.
missingVsBestInClass: USD values everywhere (Hidden Hand/Votium standard): bribes, claimables, emissions and TVL are denominated only in ETH/raw tokens — no $ per vote, no $/veTOWELI, no projected APR per gauge, which is THE headline number on every competitor bribe market.

Round/epoch history explorer: no past-epoch table (who bribed what, total paid, your earnings history, claim history) — only a 'lifetime ~ETH' micro-label per gauge; Hidden Hand and Votium both expose per-round archives.
Claim-all across gauges in one tx (claimBribesBatch exists per gauge, but a voter with 4 gauges clicks 4 times).

Snapshot integration is entirely absent (not even a stub): no snapshot.org space link, no delegation UI, no off-chain proposal mirror — the roadmap's Tier-1 'Snapshot delegation' item has no surface here (repo-wide grep confirms).
Per-entity deep links: no ?gauge=, ?proposal=, ?bounty= or /community?section=bounties#12 anchors — items can't be shared or linked from Discord/Twitter.
Notifications/alerts: no 'you have unclaimed bribes' badge on nav, no reveal-deadline reminder (bond forfeiture is time-critical), no push/email hooks.
Tx simulation/preview and gas context before writes (Uniswap-grade): votes, deposits and claims fire blind with no expected-outcome panel beyond the bribe earn estimate.
Bounty board basics vs any grants/quest platform: submission gallery with previews, submission voting, winner display, creator dashboards, status filters (Open/Completed/Expired), my-bounties view.

Gallery vs OpenSea/Blur-grade galleries: no sort/filter controls (votes/newest/title), no search, no per-piece permalink or share button, no download/full-resolution view, no pinch-zoom in lightbox, no swipe navigation on mobile.
Voting-power acquisition funnel: the bribes tab links to /farm to stake, but there's no inline 'how much would X TOWELI staked earn from current bribes' calculator (Votium-style ROI calculator).
