findings.title: First-visit splash is ~20s, unskippable, and ends in a mandatory CLICK TO ENTER gate
findings.evidence: On prod first visit, /farm showed splash scenes (FIGHT NIGHT art, near-black particle scenes, kaleidoscope) for ~15-20s before content; several scenes are almost pure black for 4+ seconds. On localhost HEAD the same splash ran 45s+ and ended in a 'TEGRIDY FARMS — CLICK TO ENTER' gate; clicking mid-splash does NOT skip (clicked at 15s and 31s, splash continued). DOM during splash exposes only a 'Mute' button — no skip control exists. Splash correctly plays once (localStorage tegridy_first_visit) and does not replay on reload — that part is good.
findings.suggestion: Keep the art (additive): add a visible 'Skip intro' button from second 1, make any click/keypress jump straight to the click-to-enter gate, and consider trimming the near-black middle scenes. A 20s+ gate is where first-time yield farmers bounce.

findings.title: Entire pool/farm content hidden behind connect wall — logged-out users cannot evaluate anything
findings.evidence: Logged-out prod /farm renders only: 5 stat chips + 'Connect to farm with tegridy' card + footer. get_page_text confirms no pool list, no TVL, no lock-tier APR table, no boost schedule. Localhost HEAD (connected) proves the page HAS this content: TOTAL VALUE LOCKED 250,395.488 TOWELI card, Season 3 banner, Liquidity Pools section (TOWELI/ETH 0.3% card with TVL/EST APR/EST 24H VOL), LP Farming stats (Reward Rate 285.71/day, Total Funded 2,000 TOWELI, Period Ends 2026-08-14), Boost Schedule (7d 0.40x → 1yr 1.29x with APYs). Aerodrome/Curve/Uniswap all show pools + APRs read-only before connect.
findings.suggestion: Render the read-only sections (pools, TVL, boost/lock APR schedule, emissions countdown) for logged-out users with stake/claim buttons swapped to 'Connect to stake'. All of this data comes from public RPC reads — no wallet needed.

findings.title: Dashboard is an empty void when logged out — no protocol stats, no preview, near-zero information
findings.evidence: Final logged-out state is just 'Connect Wallet / View your portfolio, positions, and earnings.' + one button over the jungle artwork; get_page_text returns only those 3 strings. On a 3432px ultrawide the data density is effectively zero. The /farm page proves protocol-level stats (APR, reward pool, emissions, price) are available without a wallet.
findings.suggestion: Additively overlay a protocol-stats strip (TOWELI price, TVL, stakers, 24h volume, treasury) and a demo/preview of the portfolio layout (greyed sample cards), keeping the jungle art as the backdrop. Aave/Uniswap dashboards always give logged-out visitors something to read.

findings.title: Connect CTA text overlaid directly on busy artwork with no scrim — subtext nearly unreadable
findings.evidence: Zoom at (600,230)-(980,320): white serif 'Connect Wallet' heading and white subtext 'View your portfolio, positions, and earnings.' sit directly over the white-faced soldier character — the subtext washes out completely over light areas of the art. /farm uses a proper dark card behind its identical CTA; /dashboard has none.
findings.suggestion: Add the same dark panel/backdrop-blur card used on /farm behind the dashboard CTA (additive — art stays fully visible around it).

findings.title: Primary RPC eth.llamarpc.com is down (HTTP 521) — every page load fires failing preflights
findings.evidence: read_network_requests on both pages: 'https://eth.llamarpc.com/ OPTIONS 521' (Cloudflare origin-down). performance.getEntriesByType shows the app fans out every read to 3 providers (publicnode, ankr, llamarpc) — dozens of llamarpc fetches per load, all failing behind the 521 preflight. Data still renders via publicnode/ankr (failover works), but each load wastes ~60 doomed requests and latency headroom.
findings.suggestion: Drop or down-rank llamarpc in the transport list (or add health-check-based exclusion). Also consider whether the 3x fan-out per read is intended — it looked like every call hits all three providers, ~176 fetches on one logged-out /farm load.

findings.title: Skeleton bait-and-switch: loading skeleton shows 8 stat cards + chart, then collapses to a bare connect prompt
findings.evidence: First dashboard paint rendered a full skeleton grid (8 placeholder stat cards + large chart placeholder + footer) for ~2-4s, then the page swapped to the tiny 'Connect Wallet' gate with none of that content. The skeleton advertises a layout the logged-out user never gets — jarring and feels broken. (Repro depends on wallet-reconnect resolution time; second reload skipped the skeleton.)
findings.suggestion: While connection status is resolving, show a neutral spinner or the connect-gate itself dimmed, not the connected-state skeleton.

findings.title: 'Light mode' toggle only recolors the navbar orange — body, cards, footer stay dark
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Toggle light mode' (aria-label) on /farm and /dashboard: header turns orange, but stat cards, connect card, background and footer remain in the dark palette. Zoom shows active 'Farm' nav link in light-green on orange — low contrast. If this is the intended 'day header' aesthetic the button's aria-label/iconography over-promises a real theme switch.
findings.suggestion: Either theme the content surfaces too, or relabel/restyle the control as an accent toggle so it doesn't read as a broken light mode. Check green-on-orange nav contrast (active link + Connect button) against WCAG AA.

findings.title: No TVL or USD context anywhere on the farm page
findings.evidence: The 5 stat chips are STAKING APR 5294.34%, REWARD POOL 6,400,000 TOWELI, DAILY EMISSIONS 71,219 TOWELI/day, MAX BOOST 4.0x, FEE SHARE 100% — all real (emissions match on-chain rewardRate 0.8243/s) but there is no TVL figure and no USD equivalent for any TOWELI amount, even though the app already fetches the GeckoTerminal price (api.geckoterminal.com token_price call observed) and shows $0.00004132 in the corner chip. A farmer cannot compute expected yield without TVL.
findings.suggestion: Add a TVL chip (it exists at HEAD connected view as 250,395.488 TOWELI — show it logged-out, with USD subtext) and USD subtext under the TOWELI amounts. A simple ROI/lock calculator (amount + lock duration → est. rewards) would close the page's core job.

findings.title: Towelie avatar overlaps the Protocol Active price chip, hiding the price
findings.evidence: Bottom-right chip reads 'Protocol Active $0.00004132' (verified via DOM), but the floating Towelie avatar sits on top of the price portion — zooms at (1430,545)-(1568,582) show only '$6'/'$0...' peeking out from behind the avatar.
findings.suggestion: Stack the chip above/left of the avatar or shift the avatar down-right so the price is never occluded. Also label the price ('TOWELI $0.000041') — a bare dollar figure next to 'Protocol Active' is ambiguous.

findings.title: More dropdown does not close on Escape
findings.evidence: Opened the More menu (Gallery, Tegridy Score, Tokenomics, Treasury), pressed Escape — menu stayed open in the next screenshot; it only closes on outside click. The wallet modal DOES close on Escape (good).
findings.suggestion: Wire Escape (and focus-out) to close the menu for keyboard parity.

findings.title: No visible keyboard focus indicators on nav links
findings.evidence: Pressed Tab 3 times on /dashboard; zoom of the nav bar (690,0)-(1050,26) shows no focus ring on Dashboard/Farm/Trade/More or any element. (First focusable is the visually-hidden 'Replay splash screen' button, which is a nice touch — but subsequent tab stops show no ring.)
findings.suggestion: Add a :focus-visible outline (e.g. 2px green) to nav links, buttons, and footer links.

findings.title: Jungle artwork pops in abruptly ~2-3s after the connect text, with the button appearing separately
findings.evidence: Reload sequence: t≈1s shows dark navy void with 'Connect Wallet' heading + subtext but NO button; t≈4s the full-bleed jungle art and green button appear at once with no fade. Three distinct visual states flash by on every cold load.
findings.suggestion: Fade the artwork in (opacity transition on image load) and render the button with the heading so the CTA block appears as one unit.

findings.title: Splash exit 'shatter' animation lingers ~10s, leaving glass-shard fragments overlaying and obscuring page content
findings.evidence: On localhost HEAD after CLICK TO ENTER, rotated triangular shards of the splash art remained on top of the farm page across 3 screenshots (~10s), covering stat cards and the pools section before finally clearing. Content is unreadable/uninteractable-looking during this period.
findings.suggestion: Cap the shard exit animation at ~1.5-2s and set pointer-events:none + a hard removal timeout so it can never strand fragments over content.

findings.page: /farm (HEAD, LP Farming section — will reach prod)
findings.title: LP Farming 'EST. APR — calculating…' badge never resolves
findings.evidence: On localhost HEAD connected view, the LP Farming header badge read 'EST. APR — calculating…' for the entire 25s+ observation while every other figure (reward rate, pending rewards, totals) had loaded.
findings.suggestion: If the APR genuinely can't be computed (pool too new / missing price), show 'N/A — pool bootstrapping' instead of a permanent 'calculating' spinner-state; verify the calculation isn't blocked by the dead llamarpc transport.

findings.page: /farm (HEAD, Your Position / Boost Schedule — will reach prod)
findings.title: Sub-1x 'Boost' values read as a penalty (Boost 0.61x, schedule starts at 0.40x)
findings.evidence: Localhost HEAD: Your Position shows 'Boost 0.61x'; Boost Schedule lists 7 Days 0.40x, 30 Days 0.46x, 90 Days 0.61x, 1 Year 1.29x, up to 4.0x. 'Boost: 0.61x' on a card implies you're earning 39% LESS than baseline — confusing even if mathematically it's a 0.4-4.0 multiplier scale.
findings.suggestion: Relabel as 'Lock multiplier' or normalize the display so the shortest lock = 1.0x, with the marketing 'MAX BOOST 4.0x' kept consistent.

findings.title: Disconnected swap card is a large empty box with a left-stuck Connect button
findings.evidence: Landed on /swap once: the Swap tab card is ~300px of empty space with tiny centered text 'Connect your wallet to swap' and a 'Connect Wallet' button hugging the card's left edge (not centered, vertically misaligned with the text).
findings.suggestion: Center the button under the text and show a read-only quote widget (ETH→TOWELI rate) while disconnected. (Noting only — /swap was not in my assignment.)

findings.title: Ultrawide layout: content band uses ~30% of a 3432px viewport; large dead side-zones above the art
findings.evidence: Viewport is 3432x1274. The stat ribbon and connect card sit in a centered ~960px column; the towel-characters artwork anchors the center-bottom nicely, but the upper-left/upper-right thirds are flat dark gradient. Between the connect card and the footer there is also a full empty band (~250px tall) with no content. By contrast /dashboard's full-bleed art uses the ultrawide canvas beautifully.
findings.suggestion: On wide breakpoints, widen the stat ribbon (6-7 chips incl. TVL/price) and use the empty mid-band for the boost-schedule table or pool preview — additive, art untouched.

findings.title: Stat chips have no tooltips or click-through
findings.evidence: Hovering STAKING APR (and others) produces no tooltip; the bootstrap-APR caveat is inline (good) but REWARD POOL / DAILY EMISSIONS / FEE SHARE have no 'how is this computed' affordance and nothing is clickable (e.g. FEE SHARE → /tokenomics).
findings.suggestion: Add hover tooltips with formula/source and link chips to their detail pages.

good: Document titles are correct per page (Farm | Tegridy Farms, Dashboard | Tegridy Farms, Swap | Tegridy Farms, FAQ | Tegridy Farms).

Splash plays only once per visitor (localStorage flag) — reloads and subsequent navigations go straight to content; there is also a deliberate hidden 'Replay splash screen' button as the first focusable element.

Farm stat numbers are REAL on-chain data, not placeholders: DAILY EMISSIONS 71,219/day exactly matches the deployed rewardRate (0.8243/s x 86400), REWARD POOL 6,400,000 TOWELI matches the seeded amount; no NaN/undefined/Invalid Date anywhere on either page.

Honest copy: the eye-popping 5294.34% APR carries an inline caveat 'early-TVL bootstrap rate — normalizes as TVL grows'; connect card discloses ERC-721 position mechanics and links security disclosures; footer repeats the risk disclaimer.

RPC failover works: with eth.llamarpc.com hard-down (521), all data still renders via publicnode/ankr — zero app console errors on prod loads of /farm and /dashboard (only noise was MetaMask's own extension contentscript error).
RainbowKit connect modal opens fast, themes correctly (dark modal in dark mode, light in light mode), closes on Escape and X, and was never left in a broken state.

Towelie chat companion is charming and well-behaved: typewriter personality lines, Close chat collapses to a mini 'Ask me' pill, 'Don't show again' opt-out offered, persists unobtrusively across pages.

The jungle dashboard artwork is excellent full-bleed ultrawide usage, and the /farm towel-characters art gives the connect gate real personality; footer is comprehensive (product/resources/community/legal + contract address chip with copy button).
Dashboard skeleton (when it appears) is a well-built placeholder grid — right shapes, subtle shimmer — the issue is only that it doesn't match the logged-out outcome.
Page transitions between farm/swap/dashboard are instant client-side swaps with no splash replay and no layout jank; domComplete ≈1.5s on prod.
live:farm-dashboard.splashAndTransitions: Splash: first visit only (localStorage-flagged), ~15-20s on prod and 45s+ on localhost dev, multi-scene art film (some scenes near-black for several seconds) with audio + Mute button, ending in a mandatory 'CLICK TO ENTER' gate; there is NO skip control and clicking mid-splash does not skip. On HEAD the exit is a 'glass shatter' animation whose shards lingered ~10s over live page content before clearing. Repeat visits: no splash, direct content — good. Skeletons: /dashboard shows a high-quality skeleton grid that mismatches the logged-out outcome (collapses to a bare connect prompt); /farm has a simple fade-in, no skeleton mismatch. Page-to-page client transitions are instant and clean with no splash replay; /dashboard cold load has a 3-stage pop (void+heading → button+full-bleed art snap-in) that needs a fade.
live:farm-dashboard.consoleAndNetwork: Prod console: clean on /farm and /dashboard (0 app errors across multiple loads; one 'Extension context invalidated' from the MetaMask extension itself, not the app). Network: eth.llamarpc.com OPTIONS preflight returns 521 (Cloudflare origin down) on every page load; the app fans every read out to 3 RPCs (ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com ~120ms OK, rpc.ankr.com/eth ~70ms OK, eth.llamarpc.com failing) — ~176 fetch entries on a single logged-out /farm load, so roughly a third of all RPC traffic is dead weight. One GeckoTerminal price call (api.geckoterminal.com token_price/0x420698...) succeeds ~100ms. No /api/* calls are made by these two pages at all. No 4xx/5xx besides the 521, no slow (>1.5s) calls observed.
pagesCovered: https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app/swap (incidental — landed once via nav, one finding noted)
http://localhost:5173/farm + /dashboard (HEAD cross-check only; dev wallet auto-reconnected so it showed connected state — no wallet actions taken)

findings.page: App shell / tab indicators (Community, NFT Finance, AMM, Lending)
findings.title: layoutId shared-element tab animations are dead under LazyMotion domAnimation
findings.evidence: App.tsx:221 wraps the app in `<LazyMotion features={domAnimation} strict>` and the comment at App.tsx:214-220 claims 'the app only uses basic opacity/y/scale/transition... not layout, not drag'. But 5 callsites use layout animations: CommunityPage.tsx:100-104 `<m.div layoutId="community-tab" ... transition={{ type: 'spring', stiffness: 400, damping: 30 }}/>`, LendingPage.tsx:209 layoutId="nft-finance-tab", AMMSection.tsx:472 layoutId="amm-tab-underline", NFTLendingSection.tsx:205 and LendingSection.tsx:583 layoutId="lending-tab-indicator". Layout animations require the domMax feature bundle; under domAnimation the layoutId prop is silently ignored, so the active-tab pill/underline teleports instead of springing. Visual state still renders correctly — only the configured animation never runs.
findings.suggestion: Either switch LazyMotion to domMax (~10kb more) or accept and delete the layoutId/spring props so the code matches reality; also fix the stale App.tsx comment.

findings.title: Stalled image preload = indefinite black screen with all skip paths inert
findings.evidence: AppLoader.tsx:205-218 — the RAF loop only starts inside `preloadImages(srcs).then(...)` (`rafId = requestAnimationFrame(tick)` is the last line of the .then). preload.ts:1-16 has no timeout: an image request that hangs (slow network, stalled CDN) keeps the promise pending forever. During this 'loading' phase the overlay is opaque black (#000, AppLoader.tsx:618). The ESC handler (AppLoader.tsx:131-144) only sets `s.phase='skip'` and the click handler (AppLoader.tsx:109-128) only acts in hold/textForm/vortex — with no tick running, neither escape path does anything. User is stuck on a black screen until the network resolves.
findings.suggestion: Add a Promise.race timeout (e.g. 3-4s) around preloadImages that falls through to the no-images textForm path, and make ESC/click during 'loading' call finalize() directly.

findings.title: Mobile users cannot skip the first ~11 s of the splash; ESC is the only early skip and is keyboard-only/undiscoverable
findings.evidence: AppLoader.tsx:112 — `if (!s.clicked && (s.phase === 'hold' || s.phase === 'textForm' || s.phase === 'vortex'))`: taps are ignored during void (0-1.5s, constants.ts T_VOID_END=1500) and the 4-piece art gallery (4×2600 ms, T_ART_DURATION=2600/T_ART_COUNT=4), i.e. roughly the first 11 s. The early skip is Escape-only (AppLoader.tsx:131-144) which doesn't exist on touch devices, and there is no visible 'Skip' control anywhere (only the mute button, AppLoader.tsx:634-657). 'TAP TO ENTER' only appears in the hold phase (phases/hold.ts:153). This replays every new tab/session (sessionStorage 'tf_loaded').
findings.suggestion: Additive: render a small 'Skip ▸' button (like the existing mute button) that triggers the existing 'skip' dissolve from any phase. Keeps all the art, gives every device an out.

findings.title: Seasonal event banner advertises reward multipliers nothing implements — Ape Month auto-activates 2026-07-01
findings.evidence: SeasonalEvent.tsx:4-23 hardcodes events: 'Harvest Season — 2x points on all staking activity' (ended 2026-06-05) and 'Ape Month — NFT boost bonus +10% for all holders' (2026-07-01→07-31, multiplier 1.1). Grep of lib/pointsEngine.ts finds no seasonal/event multiplier hook (only STREAK_MULTIPLIERS at pointsEngine.ts:60), and the on-chain JBAC boost is a fixed +0.5x (constants.ts:101 JBAC_BONUS_BPS=5000). When Ape Month flips active on July 1 the shell will banner a '+10% NFT boost for all holders' that neither the points engine nor the contracts apply — directly against the repo's 'nothing should render a number the chain can't back' rule (constants.ts:118-122).
findings.suggestion: Before 2026-07-01: either wire an event multiplier into pointsEngine and the banner copy to what's real, or empty the SEASONAL_EVENTS array until a backed event exists.

findings.title: 1000 ms full-screen pointer-blocking glitch overlay fires on every navigation — including in-page tab switches — on top of a full page remount
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:48-53 — every GlitchConfig has `duration: 1000`; the overlay is `fixed inset-0` zIndex 10000 with pointer events enabled for skip (GlitchTransition.tsx:675, 289-298), so it eats clicks for up to 1 s per nav. ActivityPage.tsx:45-48 and LearnPage.tsx:39-42 implement tabs via `navigate(TAB_PATHS[t])`, so switching Points→History or Tokenomics→FAQ triggers the full route glitch AND a complete remount (AppLayout.tsx:135 `<div key={location.pathname}>` wraps the Outlet), losing all tab state and re-running every query.
findings.suggestion: Additive tuning, not removal: exempt same-host tab navigations (e.g. compare tabFromPath buckets in RouteGlitch), or drop duration to ~400 ms for 'light' transitions. Consider removing the key={pathname} remount for same-component routes so tab switches keep state.

findings.title: Desktop glitch can fetch up to 16 full-resolution art images mid-transition with no preloading
findings.evidence: GlitchTransition.tsx:350-370 generateSlices picks `config.sliceCount` (up to 16, AppLayout.tsx:48) distinct images from the 40-entry ART_IMAGES list and renders each as FOUR full-bleed `backgroundImage: url(...)` layers (AnimatedSlice, GlitchTransition.tsx:435-459 — base + R/B/G channel divs). Unlike the mobile path (which preloads 3 images, GlitchTransition.tsx:76-97), the desktop path never preloads — a cold cache triggers a burst of up to 16 image downloads (art JPGs are ~150-200 KB each) for a 1 s effect, and slices render blank until each image arrives.
findings.suggestion: Preload a small fixed pool (3-5 images) like the mobile path, or reuse the splash-preloaded images; serve downsized variants for slices.

findings.title: Escape during the splash also permanently dismisses the OnboardingModal the user has never seen
findings.evidence: On first visit OnboardingModal mounts open (OnboardingModal.tsx:43-45, localStorage 'tegridy-onboarding-seen' unset) underneath the splash overlay. Modal.tsx:71-77 registers a document-level keydown listener: `if (e.key === 'Escape') { onClose(); return; }` and OnboardingModal's onClose (close, OnboardingModal.tsx:49-52) writes the seen flag. AppLoader.tsx:131-144 has its own window keydown ESC handler. Both fire on one keypress: ESC to skip the splash silently marks onboarding seen — the first-run education flow is destroyed by the most natural skip gesture. Also note the modal's focus trap (Modal.tsx:108-121) grabs focus while the splash is still covering it.
findings.suggestion: Gate OnboardingModal mounting on splash completion (e.g. render it only after AppLoader's onComplete), or have Modal ignore Escape while an element with z-index 9999 splash is present.

findings.title: Fixed header ignores env(safe-area-inset-top) while the app explicitly opts into iOS standalone mode
findings.evidence: index.html:10 sets `<meta name="apple-mobile-web-app-capable" content="yes">`, index.html:21 sets viewport-fit=cover, and manifest.webmanifest declares `"display": "standalone"`. TopNav.tsx:104-105 renders `<header className="fixed top-0 left-0 right-0 z-50 h-14">` with no safe-area-top padding, and AppLayout.tsx:133 hardcodes `pt-14`. In an installed/home-screen launch on a notched iPhone the status bar overlays the top of the header. Notably the wrong-network banner DOES handle it (AppLayout.tsx:113 `top: 'calc(56px + env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px))'`) — the header it sits under doesn't. Unverified on device; grounded in the meta/manifest + CSS combination.
findings.suggestion: Add `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)` to the header and `calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-top))` to the content offset, or drop the standalone meta if PWA install isn't a supported path.

findings.title: Credibility gating not applied to the ActivityPage tab strip — 'Gold Card' tab promoted while PREMIUM_ACCESS is zeroed
findings.evidence: navConfig.ts:40 `PREMIUM_LIVE = isDeployed(PREMIUM_ACCESS_ADDRESS)` is false (constants.ts:42 zero address), which hides Gold Card from Footer (Footer.tsx:23) per the 2026-06-09 credibility-gating policy. But ActivityPage.tsx:7-19 hardcodes the four tabs including `gold: 'Gold Card'` and renders all of them (ActivityPage.tsx:67-81), so every visit to /leaderboard, /history or /changelog shows a promoted Gold Card tab that dead-ends in a not-deployed surface.
findings.suggestion: Filter TAB_LABELS/TAB_PATHS through PREMIUM_LIVE the same way navConfig/Footer/BottomNav do — the tab reappears automatically on redeploy.

findings.title: sanitize() HTML-escapes strings that React renders as text → visible &/' entities
findings.evidence: TransactionReceipt.tsx:17-25 replaces & < > " ' with HTML entities, then every value is rendered via JSX text nodes, e.g. line 383 `{row.value}` and lines 368/372 `{sanitize(receipt.data.fromToken)}`. React already escapes text content, so a pool named "Randy's Pool" renders literally as `Randy's Pool` on the receipt card (and in the shared/copied image via html2canvas). The escaping provides no security benefit in this render path — it only corrupts display.
findings.suggestion: Drop the entity escaping for React-rendered values (keep length capping / hash validation); reserve escaping for any future innerHTML path.

findings.title: Share-to-X fallback URL points at tegridyfarms.io — not the production domain
findings.evidence: TransactionReceipt.tsx:231 `const url = etherscanUrl ?? 'https://tegridyfarms.io';` — production is https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app (usePageTitle.ts:4, index.html:28). For synthetic receipts without a tx hash, the tweet links to a domain the project may not own.
findings.suggestion: Use the canonical SITE_URL constant.

findings.title: Drawer focus-restore effect steals focus to the hamburger button on initial page load
findings.evidence: TopNav.tsx:91-100 — `useEffect(... if (open) {...} else { menuButtonRef.current?.focus(); } }, [open])`. The else-branch runs on the very first mount (open=false), not only after a close. On <640 px viewports the hamburger is visible, so page load programmatically focuses it (screen readers announce 'Open navigation menu', and :focus-visible may outline it). On desktop it's display:none so focus() is a no-op.
findings.suggestion: Track a wasOpen ref and only restore focus when transitioning open→closed.

findings.title: 640-767 px viewports get 80 px of dead bottom padding for a bottom nav that is hidden there; code comment contradicts the class
findings.evidence: BottomNav.tsx:60 uses `sm:hidden` (hidden ≥640 px) while its comment (lines 55-58) claims R038 'restores it for ≥640px tablets' — sm:hidden does the opposite. Meanwhile AppLayout.tsx:133 applies `pb-20 md:pb-0` and index.css:143-147 forces `.safe-area-content-bottom { padding-bottom: calc(5rem + ...) !important }` at max-width:767px — so between 640 and 767 px the page reserves ~80 px for a nav bar that isn't rendered.
findings.suggestion: Align the breakpoints: either show BottomNav to <768 (md:hidden + matching TopNav switch) or change the padding rules to max-width:639px.

findings.title: Light-mode override paints the copyright line dark purple on the footer's permanently dark background
findings.evidence: Footer.tsx:74 hardcodes `background: 'rgba(6,12,26,0.78)'` in both themes, but index.css:651-653 `[data-theme="light"] footer .text-white\/60 { color: var(--color-text-secondary); }` (#4c1d95) targets the '© 2026 Tegridy Farms' span (Footer.tsx:175 `text-white/60`). Deep purple on near-black navy is ~1.5:1 — effectively invisible in light mode. (The other light footer overrides at index.css:648-659 assume a light footer background that no longer exists.)
findings.suggestion: Either remove the light-mode footer text overrides (footer is dark in both themes) or theme the footer surface.

findings.title: Meta description / og:description go stale on pages that don't pass one
findings.evidence: usePageTitle.ts:61-67 sets description tags only `if (description)` and registers no cleanup — FarmPage.tsx:51 `usePageTitle('Farm')`, AdminPage.tsx:149, ContractsPage.tsx:291 and TreasuryPage.tsx:82 pass no description, so navigating Lore → Farm leaves Farm tagged with 'The origin story of Tegridy Farms…'. Similarly title/OG cleanup at usePageTitle.ts:58 resets only document.title, and the Nakamigos sub-app (nakamigos/App.jsx:148 sets document.title directly) inherits whatever og:url/canonical the last main-app page wrote.
findings.suggestion: Add a cleanup that restores the index.html default description, and give Farm/Contracts/Treasury real descriptions; have the nakamigos titles route through the same helper.

findings.title: animate-pulse-border class has no definition — intended pulsing border never renders
findings.evidence: SeasonalEvent.tsx:99 applies `animate-pulse-border` but no `@keyframes pulse-border` or `--animate-pulse-border` theme token exists in index.css (only pulse-ring/border-glow/skeleton-pulse, index.css:448-470 & 519-522). In Tailwind v4 an unknown utility generates no CSS, so the class is inert.
findings.suggestion: Define the keyframes/animation token or reuse the existing border-glow animation.

findings.title: Likely visual collision: Protocol-Active pill and Towelie avatar share fixed bottom-4 right-4 on desktop
findings.evidence: LiveActivity.tsx:43 `className="fixed bottom-4 right-4 z-40 hidden md:block"` (pill, maxWidth 200, pointer-events none) and TowelieAssistant.tsx:329 `className="fixed right-4 ... bottom-20 md:bottom-4"` z-[60] (56-64 px avatar). At ≥768 px both anchor to the same corner — the avatar overlaps/covers the right end of the pill. Unverified visually (code coordinates only), but both mount unconditionally in AppLayout.tsx:145-146.
findings.suggestion: Offset the pill (e.g. right-24 on md+) or stack it above the avatar.

findings.title: Back/forward navigation always scrolls to top — no scroll restoration on POP
findings.evidence: App.tsx:109-113 ScrollToTop runs `window.scrollTo(0, 0)` on every pathname change with no distinction between PUSH and POP (useNavigationType is not consulted). Browser-native scroll restoration is also defeated because the route content remounts (AppLayout.tsx:135 key={pathname}). Users returning from a detail page lose their reading position — Uniswap/OpenSea-grade apps restore it.
findings.suggestion: Use useNavigationType() and skip the scroll reset on 'POP' (or store per-key scroll offsets).

findings.title: Three splash art JPGs (~500 KB) are preloaded on every page view but the splash picks 4 random images out of 41
findings.evidence: index.html:70-72 preloads /art/mfers-heaven.jpg (166 KB), /art/mumu-bull.jpg (143 KB), /art/bobowelie.jpg (185 KB). loader/constants.ts ART_COLLECTION has 41 entries and AppLoader.tsx:201 does `shuffle(ART_COLLECTION).slice(0, T_ART_COUNT)` (4 of 41) — so each preloaded splash image has <10% chance of being used (bobowelie is justified — it's the TopNav button and Towelie avatar). Repeat visitors skip the splash entirely (sessionStorage) yet still preload all three; browsers also log 'preloaded but not used' warnings.
findings.suggestion: Keep bobowelie; drop the other two preloads or preload at fetchpriority=low only when tf_loaded is absent.

findings.title: Splash references /audio/ambient-loop.mp3 which does not exist — guaranteed 404 per splash interaction
findings.evidence: AppLoader.tsx:106 `audio.playAmbient('/audio/ambient-loop.mp3')`; Test-Path on frontend/public/audio returns False (directory absent). audio.ts:112-131 catches the failure silently, so no crash — but every first click/ESC on the splash fires a dead network request, and the mute button (AppLoader.tsx:634-657) mostly toggles audio that never plays (only the synthesized crack/shatter SFX are real).
findings.suggestion: Ship the loop file or remove the playAmbient call; keep the WebAudio SFX.

findings.title: 'Protocol Active' status pill is unconditional copy, not a health signal
findings.evidence: LiveActivity.tsx:59-60 renders `<PulseDot color="#22c55e"/> Protocol Active` whenever the route allows, regardless of RPC health, price availability, or pause state — it shows green even during a full provider outage (the price portion is the only live part). Given the repo's honesty-pass standard, a static 'Active' claim is a promise surface.
findings.suggestion: Drive the dot/label from something real (e.g. last successful RPC read or price fetch age: Active / Degraded).

findings.title: Inconsistent and incomplete tabs semantics across the three tab patterns
findings.evidence: ActivityPage.tsx:71 and LearnPage.tsx:66 use `aria-pressed` on plain buttons (toggle-button semantics) for what are tabs; CommunityPage.tsx:92-93 uses role="tab"/aria-selected but without a role="tablist" wrapper, roving tabindex, or arrow-key navigation. None of the three follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern, and they disagree with each other.
findings.suggestion: Standardize one accessible tab primitive (tablist/tab/tabpanel + arrow keys) and reuse it in all hosts.

findings.title: Raw localStorage access in render/effect paths despite having safeGetItem
findings.evidence: App.tsx:205 `if (!localStorage.getItem('tegridy_first_visit'))` (write goes through safeSetItem but the read is raw) and TopNav.tsx:21 `window.localStorage?.getItem('tegridy_admin')` — accessing window.localStorage itself throws SecurityError when site data is blocked (Chrome 'block third-party/site data' configurations); the optional chaining doesn't guard the property access. lib/storage.ts:113-119 exports safeGetItem for exactly this; most other shell code uses try/catch.
findings.suggestion: Route both reads through safeGetItem.

findings.title: NotFoundPage canonicalizes the bogus URL and the SPA serves it with HTTP 200
findings.evidence: App.tsx:88 `usePageTitle('404 — Page Not Found')` → usePageTitle.ts:52-56 sets `<link rel=canonical>` and og:url to window.location.pathname, i.e. the garbage path itself. Combined with Vercel SPA rewrites returning 200, crawlers see a canonicalized soft-404.
findings.suggestion: Skip canonical/og:url emission on the 404 page (add a `noCanonical` option) and add a noindex meta there.

findings.title: Sitemap lists a redirect-only URL, omits /nakamigos, and lastmod is frozen at 2026-04-19
findings.evidence: sitemap.xml includes https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app/lending which App.tsx:156 client-redirects to /nft-finance, omits the /nakamigos marketplace entirely, and every entry says `<lastmod>2026-04-19</lastmod>` (pre-relaunch). It also still promotes gated surfaces (/premium, /community, /nft-finance) whose pages are placeholder-gated today.
findings.suggestion: Regenerate: drop /lending, add /nakamigos, refresh lastmod as part of the deploy script.

findings.title: Dead exports + comment drift in the nav single-source-of-truth
findings.evidence: navConfig.ts:102-106 ALL_NAV ('used by the mobile drawer fallback') is consumed by zero components — TopNav.tsx:363 uses MORE_NAV_SECTIONS and BottomNav hardcodes tabs; only navConfig.test.ts asserts on ALL_NAV (and its comment at line 5 claims 'MORE_NAV / MORE_PATHS were removed' while MORE_NAV still exists at navConfig.ts:95 and is used by TopNav.tsx:165). navConfig.ts:64-65 also says 'Three sections of three items' but MORE_NAV_SECTIONS has 2 sections of 2-3.
findings.suggestion: Delete ALL_NAV (and its tests) or actually use it for the drawer; fix the comments so future agents don't trust stale IA docs.

findings.title: Conflicting min-width utilities on tab links
findings.evidence: BottomNav.tsx:72 `flex-1 min-w-0 min-h-[48px] min-w-[44px]` — min-w-0 (for truncation) and min-w-[44px] (tap target) are contradictory; which wins depends on Tailwind's generated order, not author intent.
findings.suggestion: Keep min-w-0 on the link and enforce the 44px floor via min-h + padding (already present), or move truncation onto the inner span only.

findings.title: Toast position never accounts for the fixed 56 px header or mobile bottom nav
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:153-164 `<Toaster position="top-right" .../>` with no offset/mobileOffset props — default sonner offset is 24-32 px, so toasts render partially behind/flush with the fixed h-14 header region on small screens. Style theming via CSS vars is otherwise well wired.
findings.suggestion: Add offset="72px" (and mobileOffset) so toasts clear the header.

findings.title: #main-content lacks tabindex="-1" for reliable skip-link focus
findings.evidence: AppLayout.tsx:97 renders the skip link and AppLayout.tsx:134 `<main id="main-content">` — without tabindex="-1" some browsers scroll but don't move sequential focus into the target, sending the next Tab back to the nav.
findings.suggestion: Add tabindex={-1} to the main element.

findings.title: Standalone-PWA finish is partial: no apple status-bar-style, no iOS startup images, no noscript fallback
findings.evidence: index.html:10 enables apple-mobile-web-app-capable and manifest.webmanifest declares standalone with valid icons (icon-192/512 verified present), but there is no `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style`, no apple-touch-startup-image set, and no `<noscript>` message anywhere in index.html:77-80 — a JS-disabled visitor gets a blank #root.
findings.suggestion: Add the status-bar-style meta, a one-line noscript notice, and (optionally) startup images.

findings.title: Duplicate entry and per-frame getImageData without willReadFrequently
findings.evidence: GlitchTransition.tsx:19+21 list both '/splash/new/28.avif' and '/splash/new/28.jpg' (same artwork twice in the slice pool; both files exist). MobileGlitchTransition's canvas context (GlitchTransition.tsx:107 `canvas.getContext('2d')`) does per-frame getImageData/putImageData block displacement (lines 203-214) without `{ willReadFrequently: true }`, which Chrome flags and slow-paths.
findings.suggestion: Dedupe #28 and pass willReadFrequently:true to both glitch canvases.

findings.title: btn-primary disabled state still carries the old purple inset highlight on a green button
findings.evidence: index.css:280 `.btn-primary:disabled { ... box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(167, 139, 250, 0.15); }` — the button was rethemed to the Kyle-green gradient (index.css:254-258) but the disabled shadow still references the purple (#a78bfa) palette. Similarly the light-mode nav-link comment at index.css:664 says 'against the cream backdrop' while the light header is Kenny orange (TopNav.tsx:108-109).
findings.suggestion: Update the disabled inset to a green/neutral tone and fix the comment.

findings.title: Splash plays on first session entry to ANY main-app route, including deep links to legal/info pages
findings.evidence: AppLoader wraps the entire AppLayout (AppLayout.tsx:92), not just '/'. A user deep-linking to /terms or /risks in a fresh tab gets the full ~14.5 s art experience (constants.ts T_TEXT_END=14500) before the legal text. sessionStorage 'tf_loaded' gating means this repeats per tab/session.
findings.suggestion: Additive: keep the splash everywhere if intended, but at minimum add the visible Skip control (see related finding); alternatively gate auto-play to '/' and let other routes skip straight in (replay stays available via the TopNav bobowelie button, TopNav.tsx:127-139).

findings.title: Route tips overpromise gated features
findings.evidence: TowelieAssistant.tsx:84 '/nft-finance': "Lend, borrow, trade NFTs. No oracles, no rugs.", line 83 '/community': "Vote, post bounties, propose grants...", line 90 '/premium': "Randy's Gold Card. Bonus rewards for the loyal." — all three surfaces are currently isDeployed-gated to FeatureNotDeployed placeholders (constants.ts zeroes; navConfig.ts:26-40), so the first-visit greeting promises functionality the page immediately denies.
findings.suggestion: Gate these three tips on the same *_LIVE flags so Towelie's copy and the page state agree.

good: Theme bootstrap is genuinely FOUC-proof and CSP-clean: external /theme-init.js runs synchronously pre-CSS, shares the exact storage key and dark default with ThemeContext, and syncs the theme-color meta (theme-init.js, ThemeContext.tsx:29-39)

Three-layer error containment: root ErrorBoundary in main.tsx, RouteErrorBoundary around the router (App.tsx:45-75), and a per-page ErrorBoundary with resetKeys=[pathname] (AppLayout.tsx:136) so a crashed page self-heals on navigation instead of being reload-only

Error reporting pipeline is unusually hardened: consent-gated deny-by-default (GDPR banner), secret/address/mnemonic redaction, URL stripping, dedup window, batching, and SSRF-style endpoint allowlisting (errorReporting.ts, consent.ts, ConsentBanner.tsx)

Route hygiene: every legacy/merged path has an explicit redirect (/trade, /learn, /lending, /launchpad, /nft-amm, /governance, /grants, /bounties, /bribes, /restake), a real in-layout 404 exists, the dev-only art-studio chunk is statically tree-shaken from prod with a redirect fallback (App.tsx:31-37, 122-168), and the Nakamigos sub-app has its own 404 title

Per-route content-shaped skeletons (SwapSkeleton/FarmSkeleton/DashboardSkeleton) with role=status/aria-busy/aria-live instead of one generic spinner (PageSkeletons.tsx), plus a shimmer system themed for both modes

Credibility gating is a single source of truth: NFT_FINANCE_LIVE/COMMUNITY_LIVE/PREMIUM_LIVE derive from isDeployed(constants) and propagate to PRIMARY_NAV, BottomNav, Footer — features un-gate automatically on redeploy and the wiring has tests (navConfig.ts, navConfig.test.ts)

wagmi config degrades gracefully: ranked multi-RPC fallback transport, and a no-WalletConnect-projectId path that still mounts the app with injected+coinbase connectors instead of crashing (wagmi.ts:23-53)

Splash engineering quality: sessionStorage repeat-gating decided during lazy state init (no flash), prefers-reduced-motion auto-skip that also sets the flag, DPR capping, mobile particle budgets, gesture-gated AudioContext, tainted-canvas guards, and full RAF/listener cleanup (AppLoader.tsx)

Accessibility groundwork above typical DeFi apps: skip link, focus-trapped mobile drawer with Escape + body scroll lock, Modal primitive with focus restore + aria-labelledby + backdrop opt-out, 44px tap-target floors, global :focus-visible outline, sr-only utility, reduced-motion CSS kill-switch, WCAG-checked nav-link contrast with documented ratios (TopNav.tsx:58-100, Modal.tsx, index.css)

LazyMotion strict + scripted motion.→m. migration across 45 files keeps the heavy motion engine off the critical path (App.tsx:214-223), and decorative shell pieces (ParticleBackground, GlitchTransition) are lazy-loaded so they don't block first paint (AppLayout.tsx:18-27)

index.html metadata is near-complete: raster og.png with secure_url/type/dims/alt, twitter card mirrors, canonical, JSON-LD, self-hosted preloaded fonts, preconnect/dns-prefetch for NFT CDNs and aggregator APIs, robots.txt + sitemap present, valid manifest with real 192/512 maskable icons
safe localStorage layer with quota estimation, prefix-allowlisted eviction, and safeJsonParse used across shell consumers (storage.ts)

Towelie assistant has real product care: per-route once-only tips, event cooldowns, idle snooze, rage-dismiss fatigue detection (3 dismissals → 30 min snooze), permanent disable, and a priority queue with head-of-line fix (TowelieAssistant.tsx, useTowelie.ts)

findings.title: Approval spender does not match execution venue — every ERC20-input swap on the 'tegridy' or 'uniswap' route cannot execute
findings.evidence: useSwapAllowance.ts:113 picks the spender as `const spender = selectedRoute === 'tegridy' ? TEGRIDY_ROUTER_ADDRESS : SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS;` (and the allowance reads at lines 52-78 check those same two spenders). But useSwap.ts executes the 'tegridy' route through SwapFeeRouter (line 423-427: `address: SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS ... functionName: 'swapExactTokensForETH'`) and the 'uniswap' route through the real Uniswap router (line 473-477: `address: UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER ... swapExactTokensForETH`). SwapFeeRouter.sol:747 does `IERC20(path[0]).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountIn)` — it needs allowance to SFR, not TegridyRouter; Uniswap Router02 likewise pulls from msg.sender and needs allowance to itself, not SFR. Git confirms the regression: 43c3ddb ('route genuine-Uniswap trades to the real Uniswap router') and 003445e ('capture the 0.5% protocol fee on native-pool routes') both postdate the last commit touching useSwapAllowance.ts (4b3a47f). Net effect today (TOWELI sell = ERC20-input, native pool empty, route='uniswap'): user approves SFR, swap goes to UniswapV2Router, transferFrom fails — wallet gas-estimation error or on-chain revert. After LP seed (route='tegridy'): user approves TegridyRouter, swap goes to SFR, same failure. The only working ERC20-input path is aggregator-route-with-tegridy-fallback (approves SFR, executes SFR). ETH-input swaps are unaffected (no approval).
findings.suggestion: Make the spender map 1:1 to the executor: 'tegridy' → SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS, 'uniswap' → UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER, aggregator → whichever on-chain fallback (selectedOnChainRoute.source) executes. Add a unit test asserting spender === writeContract target per route.

findings.title: DCA and browser limit-orders quote Uniswap prices but execute via SwapFeeRouter→TegridyRouter (the thin/empty native pool) — guaranteed reverts or mispriced minOut
findings.evidence: useDCA.ts:434-439 fetches minOut from `address: UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER ... getAmountsOut`, then lines 497-529 execute on `address: SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS` (whose inner router is TegridyRouter — the same wiring documented in useSwap.ts:397-400 'SFR is wired to the native TegridyRouter... a Uniswap-priced minOut sent through it executes on the (currently thin) native pool and reverts'). useLimitOrders.ts has the identical pattern: price-poll + re-quote on UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER (lines 320-330, 481-492) but executeOrder writes to SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS (lines 402-435). The deep-pool routing fix that was applied to useSwap (commit 43c3ddb) was never propagated to these two keepers. With the native TOWELI/WETH pool unseeded, every triggered DCA tick / limit fill reverts (or the native pair's getAmountsOut revert makes minOut games moot); after seeding, the Uniswap-priced floor frequently exceeds what the native pool can deliver.
findings.suggestion: Either quote and execute on the same venue (quote SFR's own router path), or route DCA/limit executions to the venue that produced the quote (UniswapV2Router) like useSwap now does — keeping the allowance check pointed at the same contract.

findings.title: Swap success effect re-fires every render for ~4s — duplicate 'WAGMI! Swap confirmed' toasts, phantom swap-confirmed toast after a plain approve, duplicated trackSwap analytics
findings.evidence: useSwap.ts:246-286: the receipt-success effect's dep array includes `allowance` (the object returned by useSwapAllowance is a fresh literal every render — not memoized, useSwapAllowance.ts:195-204) and `inputAmount`/`quote.selectedRoute`. While isSuccess is latched true (until the 4s `reset()` at line 284), useSwapQuote's 1-second staleness ticker (useSwapQuote.ts:261-265 `setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000)`) re-renders the consumer every second, so the effect re-runs each tick. On re-run after an approve, `lastActionRef.current` was already nulled by the first run (line 263), so control falls through to the swap branch: `toast.success('WAGMI! Swap confirmed'...)` (line 268, no toast id → sonner stacks duplicates) and `trackSwap(...)` (line 278) fire again with fallback live values. Result: stacked duplicate success toasts after a swap, a phantom 'Swap confirmed' toast ~1s after a mere token approval, and inflated swap analytics.
findings.suggestion: Guard with a lastHandledHashRef (the pattern already used in useLPFarming.ts:80-95), give the toast `id: hash`, and remove unstable deps (memoize the useSwapAllowance return object).

findings.title: normalizeTokenAddress 'zero' style returns the 0xEeee sentinel instead of the zero address — Odos native-ETH quotes silently dead
findings.evidence: aggregator.ts:35-39: `case 'zero': return '0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE';` — identical to the 'native' case. getOdosQuote (lines 116-117) calls `normalizeTokenAddress(tokenIn, 'zero')` because Odos expects 0x0000...0000 for native ETH; sending the 0xEeee address makes Odos reject the quote (res.ok false → null, swallowed by the catch). The meta-aggregator silently loses Odos as a source for every ETH-input swap — exactly the headline ETH→TOWELI flow.
findings.suggestion: Return '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' from the 'zero' branch and add a test for the Odos native-input path.

findings.title: refreshQuote never re-fetches aggregator quotes — after the 30s staleness gate trips, the aggregator leg is permanently lost until the user edits the input
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:437-446: `refreshQuote` bumps `quoteRequestIdRef.current += 1` with the comment 'bumping the requestId triggers re-fetch', but the aggregator fetch effect's deps are `[fromToken, toToken, parsedAmount, address, fromDecimals, chainId]` (line 251) — none change, so the effect never re-runs. `setAggQuoteResult(null)` just deletes the existing aggregator quote. So when useSwap.ts:343-347 blocks a stale swap and calls refreshQuote, only the on-chain legs refetch; the 7-aggregator comparison silently downgrades to on-chain-only, and the user can submit a worse route without knowing. Also, if the refetched uniAmountsOut is structurally identical, the quoteFetchedAt stamp effect (lines 254-258) never re-fires, leaving quoteFetchedAt=0 which makes isQuoteStale read false with no fresh stamp.
findings.suggestion: Drive the aggregator effect from a state-based requestId (useState counter included in the dep array) so refreshQuote actually re-fires it, and stamp quoteFetchedAt from the refetch promises.

findings.title: POOL_LAUNCH_TIMESTAMP hardcoded to 2025-03-01 — ~15 months before the pool existed — understating fee-based APR and '24h volume' by ~100x once fees accrue
findings.evidence: usePoolTVL.ts:10 `const POOL_LAUNCH_TIMESTAMP = new Date('2025-03-01').getTime() / 1000;` — but TEGRIDY_LP_ADDRESS was deployed in the 2026-06-06 relaunch (constants.ts:15-18). Lines 76-82 divide cumulative totalETHFees by poolAgeDays computed from that date (~466 days instead of ~5), so `dailyFees`, `aprNum`, and `vol24h` are ~100x too low the moment real fees exist. Additionally the displayed 'vol24h' is a lifetime daily average mislabeled as 24h.
findings.suggestion: Set the constant to the actual pair-creation timestamp (or read the pair's first-mint block once and cache), and label the figure 'avg daily volume'.

findings.title: eth_getLogs scans start at stale fromBlock 18000000 (Sep 2023) against contracts deployed June 2026 — public RPCs reject the wide range, silently zeroing swap count and loyalty score
findings.evidence: usePoints.ts:73-83 (`fromBlock: 18000000n` for SwapExecuted on the relaunch SwapFeeRouter) and useTegridyScore.ts:322-343 (same fromBlock for Staked on the relaunch staking contract). Both catch handlers silently fall back to 0 (`.catch(() => { ... setSwapCount(0) })`, and the score hook's own comment admits 'Public RPCs sometimes reject wide eth_getLogs ranges'). The configured transports (publicnode/ankr/llamarpc, wagmi.ts:12-21) all cap getLogs ranges well below the ~5M-block span requested, so points/activity/loyalty scores quietly read 0 for most users.
findings.suggestion: Hardcode the actual relaunch deploy block (a constant next to the addresses in constants.ts) as fromBlock, or chunk the scan.

findings.title: IPFS gateway list leads with cloudflare-ipfs.com (gateway sunset by Cloudflare in 2024) and resolveSafeUrl/safeUrl return ONLY that first gateway for consumers — ipfs:// images render broken with no fallback
findings.evidence: imageSafety.ts:57-61 `IPFS_GATEWAYS = ['https://cloudflare-ipfs.com/ipfs/', 'https://dweb.link/ipfs/', 'https://ipfs.io/ipfs/']` and resolveSafeUrl (lines 80-83) returns `IPFS_GATEWAYS[0]` for any ipfs:// URI. fetchWithIpfsFallback does race the list, but the `` consumers (safeUrl → CollectionDetailV2.tsx:12, useNFTDropV2 resolveAssetUrl) get a single dead-host URL. Cloudflare publicly deprecated/shut its public IPFS gateway in 2024 (external infra fact — verify with one fetch; if it 410s, every ipfs-hosted collection image is currently broken).
findings.suggestion: Reorder so a live gateway is first (ipfs.io or dweb.link), or better: have ArtImg/NftImage onError advance through ipfsCandidates().

findings.title: The 60s 'refetch' interval is a no-op — `setTokenLoading((p) => p)` sets identical state, so open-loan data and overdue status never refresh
findings.evidence: useMyLoans.ts:117-121: `const id = setInterval(() => { ... setTokenLoading((p) => p); }, REFETCH_MS);` with comment 'Re-trigger by toggling state'. Setting state to the same value bails out of re-render in React, and even a re-render would not re-run the fetch effect because its deps `[publicClient, onMainnet, tokenDeployed, tokenCount, address]` are unchanged. The NFT-loans effect (lines 125-163) has no interval at all, and `status: 'overdue'` is computed from a `now` captured once in useMemo (line 167) whose deps exclude time. Inert today (both lending addresses zeroed) but it is the recovery-pass code that will ship when lending un-gates.
findings.suggestion: Use a state tick (`setTick(t => t+1)`) included in the effect deps, or move the sweep into tanstack-query with refetchInterval.

findings.title: useTrackedTransactionReceipt reads fields wagmi never returns (receiptStatus/blockNumber/errorName at top level) — a reverted tx would report status 'confirmed'; currently dead code
findings.evidence: useTransactionReceipt.ts:117-127 casts the wagmi result to `{ receiptStatus?: 'success' | 'reverted'; blockNumber?: bigint; errorName?: string }`, but wagmi v2 exposes these as `data.status`, `data.blockNumber`, and `error.name`. Only the test mock (src/test-utils/wagmi-mocks.ts:185 'Additive passthrough for useTrackedTransactionReceipt') supplies the flat fields, so the tests pass while the runtime branch `result.receiptStatus === 'reverted'` (line 155) can never trip — a reverted receipt falls through to `status: 'confirmed'` (line 164). Grep shows no app component consumes the hook (only tests/mocks), so the R044 H3 'reorg defense' is both unwired and incorrect at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Read `data?.status` / `error?.name` from the real hook result, then actually adopt it in the tx-toast hooks (or delete it).

findings.title: All three R080 zod schema files are dead code — never imported by the boundaries they document
findings.evidence: Grep for `schemas/(aggregator|geckoTerminal|opensea)` across src returns zero matches. lib/aggregator.ts still validates by hand (e.g. line 94 `typeof data.amountOut !== 'string' || !/^\d+$/.test(...)`), useToweliPrice.ts:121 walks `d?.data?.attributes?.token_prices` untyped, and nakamigos api consumers use raw .json(). Each schema file even carries instructions ('Apply via parseOrNull(schema, data) at every such boundary') that were never executed, and parseOrNull is duplicated 3x.
findings.suggestion: Wire parseOrNull into the seven aggregator parsers, the two GeckoTerminal call sites, and the OpenSea proxy consumers — or delete the files so future audits don't assume the validation exists.

findings.title: The purpose-built txErrors helper is unused in the money paths — wallet cancellations render as scary red 'Transaction failed' / raw error toasts in 8+ hooks
findings.evidence: Grep: surfaceTxError/isUserRejection are imported only by GaugeVoting.tsx (plus the unrelated mevProtection copy). Meanwhile useFarmActions.ts:76, useLPFarming.ts:111, useAddLiquidity.ts:159, useRestaking.ts:142 all toast `writeError.message?.slice(0, 120)` raw; useRevenueStats.ts:100 and useBribes.ts:345 toast generic 'Transaction failed' for any writeError including user rejection; useNFTDropV2.ts:232 toasts 'Mint failed' on rejection. txErrors.ts exists precisely to classify UserRejectedRequestError (including the nested-cause walk, lines 56-72) as a soft 'Cancelled' info toast.
findings.suggestion: Replace the per-hook raw toasts with surfaceTxError(err, toast, { component }) — one mechanical sweep.

findings.title: Module-level sessionStorage/crypto.randomUUID access can crash the whole app at import time in storage-blocked or non-secure contexts; failed-flush queue is unbounded
findings.evidence: analytics.ts:20-30: `getSessionId()` runs at module scope (`const sessionId = getSessionId();`) with no try/catch — browsers with storage disabled (cookie-blocked iframes/webviews) throw SecurityError from `sessionStorage.getItem`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` requires a secure context — either kills the bundle at import. Also lines 72-83: on fetch failure the batch is re-queued forever (`queue = [...batch, ...queue]`) with no cap, so a down endpoint grows memory for the life of the tab.
findings.suggestion: Wrap getSessionId in try/catch with a Math.random fallback, and cap the queue (e.g. drop oldest past 200 events).

findings.title: Stale contradictory comment block above LP_FARMING_ADDRESS still says the address is ZEROED and must be restored
findings.evidence: constants.ts:25-27 reads '// ZEROED 2026-05-31 (relaunch supersedes Wave 0...)... Restore the real address after the relaunch redeploy.' directly above line 28 which now holds the live relaunch address 0x1171268A... (deployed 2026-06-08). Anyone skimming the gating table will misread the farm as gated.
findings.suggestion: Delete the stale ZEROED comment; keep only the RELAUNCH note.

findings.title: Refund transactions toast 'Mint confirmed!' / 'Mint failed'
findings.evidence: useNFTDropV2.ts:225-236: the single receipt effect toasts `toast.success('Mint confirmed!')` and `toast.error('Mint failed')` for any hash, but the hook also submits `refund()` (line 204) through the same writeContract — a successful refund shows 'Mint confirmed!'.
findings.suggestion: Track lastAction ('mint'|'refund') in a ref, mirror useSwap's lastActionRef pattern.

findings.title: categorizeTx matches zeroed-contract addresses — any tx to 0x000...0 (ETH burns) is labeled 'Restake'
findings.evidence: txHistory.ts:97 `if (to === TEGRIDY_RESTAKING_ADDRESS.toLowerCase())` — TEGRIDY_RESTAKING_ADDRESS is the zero address (constants.ts:7), as are COMMUNITY_GRANTS/MEME_BOUNTY/PREMIUM/VOTE_INCENTIVES below it, so the first zero-compare wins and a burn/zero-send row gets categorized 'Restake'.
findings.suggestion: Skip comparisons for addresses failing isDeployed().

findings.title: Default token list ships legacy MATIC (Polygon migrated to POL in Sept 2024)
findings.evidence: tokenList.ts:106-111: `symbol: 'MATIC', name: 'Polygon', address: 0x7D1AfA7B...` — the legacy token; best-in-class lists show POL (0x455e53...). Cosmetic but signals staleness in a curated list.
findings.suggestion: Add POL (keep MATIC if you want the legacy pair tradable).

findings.title: Score tip and streak copy reference the removed daily-visit streak mechanic
findings.evidence: useTegridyScore.ts:155 tip says 'Visit daily and swap to build your streak', but pointsEngine.ts:194-197 deprecated recordDailyVisit to a no-op ('Daily visit streaks removed -- not verifiable on-chain'), so the streak can never grow and the tip is unactionable.
findings.suggestion: Reword the activity tip to swaps/staking only.

findings.title: R042 HIGH-2 return-object memoization is defeated — `path` is a new array every render, so the memo (and routeDescription) recompute every render anyway
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:75 `const path = fromToken && toToken ? buildPath(fromToken, toToken) : [];` creates a fresh array each render; it is in the final useMemo dep list (line 496) whose stated purpose is 'consumers don't see a fresh identity on every render' (lines 463-465). Identity therefore flips every render regardless.
findings.suggestion: useMemo the path on [fromToken, toToken].

findings.title: flush() drops the batch on HTTP error responses — only network failures persist to localStorage
findings.evidence: errorReporting.ts:137-147: `fetch(endpoint, {...}).catch(() => persistToLocalStorage(toSend))` — fetch only rejects on network errors; a 4xx/5xx resolves, res.ok is never checked, and the batch is silently lost.
findings.suggestion: Add `.then(r => { if (!r.ok) persistToLocalStorage(toSend); })`.

findings.title: Polling load and inconsistency: limit orders fire up to 50 sequential getAmountsOut every 15s; CoW poll lacks the hidden-tab gate the other keepers have
findings.evidence: useLimitOrders.ts:41 PRICE_POLL_INTERVAL=15_000 with a per-active-order readContract loop (lines 473-503, MAX_ORDERS=50) — heaviest poller in the app on public RPCs. useCowLimitOrder.ts:259-264 polls every 30s without the `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` skip that useDCA.ts:556 and useLimitOrders.ts:511 both apply.
findings.suggestion: Batch the order quotes in a single multicall per tick and add the visibility gate to the CoW poll.

findings.title: Minor inconsistencies: un-cleaned setTimeout(reset) timers, and stake() throws while sibling actions return silently
findings.evidence: useAddLiquidity.ts:146/153/160 schedule `setTimeout(() => reset(), 4000)` inside effects without cleanup (harmless but leaky vs the cleanup pattern used in useSwap.ts:284-285). useFarmActions.ts:99 `if (wei === null) throw new Error('Invalid amount');` — an exception in an onClick path, while approve() at line 85 silently returns for the same condition.
findings.suggestion: Return + toast instead of throw; clear the timers in effect cleanup.

findings.title: Fabricated '(est.)' volume/APR from an assumed turnover ratio contradicts the project's honesty-pass standard
findings.evidence: usePoolTVL.ts:93-103: when no fees exist, vol24h is invented as `tvl * dailyVolumeRatio` with ratios 0.01-0.04 picked by TVL bucket, and APR derived from that fiction. It is labeled '~ (est.)' but renders a number the chain can't back — the exact pattern constants.ts:116-122 forbids for the season banner ('nothing should render a number the chain can't back').
findings.suggestion: Show '—' with a 'volume appears after first trades' microcopy instead of synthetic estimates (additive copy change, no section removal).

findings.title: Negative-value formatting quirks and 88 raw .toFixed() call sites bypassing the central util
findings.evidence: formatting.ts:11 renders negatives as `$-12.34` (sign inside, vs convention `-$12.34`) and formatNumber gives `-5000.00` without thousands separators (line 20 falls through all >= checks for negatives). Grep counts 88 `.toFixed(` occurrences across 24 component files despite formatCurrency/formatNumber/formatTokenAmount existing — number formatting is scattered, not centralized.
findings.suggestion: Handle sign in formatCurrency/formatNumber and sweep components onto the utils.

findings.title: Dead exports worth pruning or wiring: ERROR_COPY, randomToweliQuote, poolFlavorLabel, lockLabelForSeconds, useTrackedTransactionReceipt, the EIP-5792 foundation
findings.evidence: Grep shows ERROR_COPY, randomToweliQuote, poolFlavorLabel and lockLabelForSeconds are defined in copy.ts (lines 121-152) with no consumers; useTrackedTransactionReceipt is consumed only by tests/mocks; eip5792.ts is self-described 'FOUNDATION ONLY (2026-06-01)' and still unwired into approve+swap/stake despite being a Tier-1 roadmap item.
findings.suggestion: Either wire them (ERROR_COPY into the txErrors sweep, EIP-5792 into the approve+swap path) or delete to keep the audit surface honest.

findings.title: Price alerts are device-global but the cap message says 'per wallet'; sendNotification fires inside a state updater (double-fires under StrictMode); unused _currentPrice param
findings.evidence: usePriceAlerts.ts:15 single STORAGE_KEY 'tegridy-price-alerts' (no address scoping) while line 107 toasts 'Up to 20 price alerts per wallet'; lines 69-88 call sendNotification inside the setAlerts updater — updaters can run twice in dev StrictMode. usePriceHistory.ts:25 takes `_currentPrice?: number` that is never used.
findings.suggestion: Move the notification out of the updater, fix the copy, drop the dead param.

findings.title: rpc.ankr.com/eth in the fallback list likely requires an API key now (unverified) — would make slot 2 a guaranteed-miss before rank() heals it
findings.evidence: wagmi.ts:15 `http('https://rpc.ankr.com/eth')` — Ankr moved its public endpoints behind registration/keyed access (external infra change; unverified hypothesis — confirm with one curl). The llamarpc comment (lines 16-17) shows the team already tracks dead public RPCs; ankr may be in the same state. rank:true mitigates but first-hit users still pay the timeout.
findings.suggestion: Curl-test the three public RPCs in CI weekly, or swap ankr for drpc/1rpc.

findings.title: POLAccumulator marked live:false on Tokenomics despite being deployed in the 2026-06-06 relaunch
findings.evidence: TokenomicsPage.tsx:44 `{ label: 'POLAccumulator', address: POL_ACCUMULATOR_ADDRESS, live: false }` while constants.ts:23 holds the live relaunch address 0x2A5f65f4... (RELAUNCH 2026-06-06 comment). Found while verifying address-table consistency; the page file itself was outside this audit's assigned scope, so flagging for the page-auditor to confirm rendering impact.
findings.suggestion: Derive `live` from isDeployed(address) instead of a hand-maintained flag.

good: Address gating architecture is coherent end-to-end: constants.ts zeroes the 10 undeployed contracts with dated comments, isDeployed() is the single predicate, navConfig.ts derives NFT_FINANCE_LIVE/COMMUNITY_LIVE/PREMIUM_LIVE from it (credibility gating with a clear rationale comment), and every gated hook (useRestaking, useBribes, useGaugeList, useMyLoans, usePremiumAccess) checks it before any read/write — features genuinely auto-un-gate when addresses land.

wagmi.ts is well-engineered: viem fallback transport with rank:true health-ranking, dated operational notes on dead RPCs, and the FE-E2E-01 no-projectId fallback path that keeps the app mounting in CI/preview without WalletConnect.

Telemetry is privacy-correct: deny-by-default consent gate (consent.ts) enforced in both analytics.track and errorReporting.reportError; shared sanitize() scrubs private keys/mnemonics/JWTs/bearer tokens/wallet addresses/secret-KV pairs; VITE_ env scan shows only legitimately-public values (WC projectId, anon keys, public endpoints); error endpoint has an SSRF-style allowlist blocking private/link-local/metadata hosts.

storage.ts is a genuinely robust localStorage layer: quota estimation, oldest-first eviction across both key prefixes, exported safeJsonParse — and useToweliPrice/usePriceHistory layer a versioned, freshness-bounded (future-skew + 24h max-age) cache on top of it.

Swap-input safety is layered: safeParseEther regex+try/catch wrapper everywhere, slippage clamped to 20% in useSwap, custom tokens re-verified against on-chain symbol/decimals at rehydrate AND import (FE-HIGH-6), symbol-collision spoof filtering, unlimited-approval blocked for unverified tokens, USDT-style two-step forceApprove state machine, and a fee-on-transfer auto-retry path.

useToweliPrice is a 3-leg oracle done right client-side: pair reserves + Chainlink with staleness/answeredInRound/min-max sanity checks + TegridyTWAP divergence override, with the GeckoTerminal API price accepted only within ±1% of on-chain and explicitly display-only.

DCA/limit keepers have serious multi-tab hardening: localStorage TTL locks + BroadcastChannel claim/release with tab IDs, beforeunload release, lock refresh across async boundaries, execution-record TTL maps that survive re-renders (R042 HIGH-5), per-schedule slippage clamps, and stale-target abort gates.

CoW integration (cowProtocol.ts + useCowLimitOrder) follows the canonical GPv2 EIP-712 order schema byte-for-byte, routes through the hardened same-origin proxy, validates uint32 validTo, checks balance+vault-relayer allowance pre-sign, and persists order records per chain+owner.

Honesty engineering is real and recent: usePoolData derives reward runway from balanceOf − totalStaked − totalUnsettled (no fake periodFinish), aggregator spread-capture display was deleted as 'fictional revenue', towelieKnowledge.ts carries a 2026-06-11 honesty pass on every yield claim, and constants.ts CURRENT_SEASON explicitly forbids rendering unfunded numbers.

Security utility files (imageSafety scheme allowlist incl. SVG-data: rejection, textSafety BiDi/Trojan-Source stripping, txHistory zod row validation before any clickable href, nftMetadata royalty/link validation, useIrysUpload pre-SDK size caps against wallet-drain funding) are all battle-tested-pattern implementations with clear threat-model comments.

Every write hook pins chainId on writeContract AND pre-checks chainId !== CHAIN_ID with a toast; receipt waits are chainId-pinned (FE-LOW-04); reads are chainId-pinned and gated on onMainnet so wrong-chain garbage can't render.

Polling discipline is mostly good: 30-60s intervals with refetchOnWindowFocus, event-driven refetch via useWatchContractEvent in useBribes/useGaugeList, visibility-gated keeper ticks, and deliberate removal of refetch storms (R043 H-062-04 comments in useNFTDropV2/useLPFarming).

The pageArt()/ART_OVERRIDES system is a clean deterministic art-rotation with studio overrides, a documented bobowelie brand-exclusion, and additive-only override semantics — consistent with the owner's preserve-art constraint.

txErrors.ts itself (cause-chain walking user-rejection detection) and revertDecoder.ts (viem BaseError.walk to structured custom-error names with a 60-entry friendly-message table) are high quality — the gap is adoption, not design.

Transaction simulation/preview before signing (Tenderly/eth_call simulate showing expected balance changes) — writes go straight to the wallet; the aggregator quotes even carry estimatedGas that is never surfaced
Standard token-list ingestion (Uniswap tokenlists.org JSON with logos/decimals) — only a 14-token hardcoded array plus manual address import; no remote list, no logo fallback service
Server-side or delegated execution for DCA/limit orders — both are browser-resident keepers that stop when the tab closes (CoW covers limit sells only; DCA has no CoW/Composable-order fallback)
Indexer-backed history/analytics — useProtocolStats self-describes volume as 'fees ÷ feeRate approximation'; no per-epoch revenue, per-user PnL, or real 24h volume until the Ponder/Dune work lands
Push notifications for price alerts / order fills when the tab is closed (Notification API only fires while open; the nakamigos side has VAPID plumbing but the Tegridy alerts don't use it)
ENS resolution and avatar display for addresses (shortenAddress everywhere; no ENS reverse lookup in treasury/referral/loan surfaces)
Multi-venue smart order routing beyond the single WETH-hop heuristic — buildPath only does direct or X-WETH-Y; no split routes, no V3 quoting
EIP-5792 one-click approve+swap/stake — the foundation module exists and is roadmap Tier-1, but no money path batches calls yet
Gas cost estimate in the swap confirm row (aggregators return estimatedGas; Uniswap/1inch show '~$x.xx network cost')
Per-wallet scoping for price alerts and a history/export (CSV) affordance for tx history beyond the validated table
