findings.title: My Pools bypasses the isDeployed gate and shows owner/admin controls for ANY tracked address; 'ownership verified on-chain' copy is false
findings.evidence: AMMSection.tsx:2466 `function MyPoolsTab({ deployed: _deployed })` — the deployed flag is discarded; line 2557 `<PoolCard poolAddress={addr as Address} isOwner index={i} />` passes isOwner unconditionally, and line 1496 `const showOwnerControls = isOwner || poolOwnerIsUser;` then renders Manage Liquidity, Pool Settings (pause/propose/execute) and Emergency Drain for every tracked pool regardless of actual on-chain owner. The 'Track a Pool' card (line 2518) claims 'Pool ownership is verified on-chain.' but handleAddPool (2471) only checks isValidAddress. All write handlers in PoolCard/PoolAdminPanel (handleAddLiquidity 1498, handleWithdraw 1528, call() 1090) gate on chainId only — never on `deployed` or code-at-address. With TEGRIDY_NFT_POOL_FACTORY_ADDRESS = address(0) (constants.ts:50), a user can paste any address, and `addLiquidity` with `value: parseEther(liqEth)` (1511) sent to an EOA succeeds on-chain and transfers the ETH away (EOAs accept arbitrary calldata + value). This is the one control on the page that fires value-bearing writes while its feature is gated.
findings.suggestion: In MyPoolsTab respect `deployed` (render the shared FeatureNotDeployed or disable Track/PoolCard writes); derive isOwner from poolInfo.owner only (drop the unconditional prop); before tracking, verify `getBytecode(addr) !== '0x'` and that `factory.isPool(addr)` (or getPoolInfo succeeds), making the 'verified on-chain' copy true.

findings.title: Refetches fired in render body — render/refetch loop after any successful admin tx
findings.evidence: OwnerAdminPanelV2.tsx:84-88: `if (isSuccess) { void refetchPhase(); void refetchContractURI(); void refetchPaused(); }` sits directly in the component body, not in a useEffect. isSuccess stays true until the next tx, and each refetch resolves → query data/dataUpdatedAt updates → re-render → refetches fire again, indefinitely while the panel is mounted. Every other tx-success handler in this tree uses useEffect (e.g. LendingSection.tsx:715, AMMSection.tsx:1471).
findings.suggestion: Move into `useEffect(() => { if (isSuccess) {...} }, [isSuccess])` like the sibling components. (Currently latent because TEGRIDY_LAUNCHPAD_V2_ADDRESS is zeroed, but it ships with the un-gate.)

findings.title: Draft auto-save clobbers the saved draft ~500ms after the wizard opens, so 'Resume' restores an empty wizard
findings.evidence: useWizardPersist.ts:74-91 — the persist effect runs on `[state]`, which includes the initial mount with `initialState`; after the 500ms throttle it writes `{...initialState}` over the stored draft under the same STORAGE_KEY. CreateWizard.tsx:33 calls `useWizardPersist(state)` unconditionally and the Resume banner's handleResume (line 38) does `readDraft()` at click time — any click later than ~500ms after opening the wizard reads back the just-overwritten empty draft (step 1, empty fields, no manifest IDs). The whole crash-recovery feature ('a browser crash mid-upload doesn't nuke 5555 tokens of work', useWizardPersist.ts:66-67) is defeated.
findings.suggestion: Skip persisting until the user has interacted (e.g. don't save while `state` deep-equals initialState, or capture the draft into memory on mount before the first save, or gate the first save behind a 'dirty' flag set by any non-HYDRATE action).

findings.title: dispatch during render + tx config built outside try/catch (uncaught parseEther/BigInt throws), and no maxSupply/mintPrice validation
findings.evidence: Step5_Deploy.tsx:95-101: `if (isSuccess && deployedCollection && !state.deployedAddress) { dispatch({ type: 'DEPLOY_SUCCESS', ... }) }` runs in the render body — updates the parent CreateWizard's reducer while Step5 renders (React 'cannot update a component while rendering a different component' warning). Also lines 51-68 build `cfg` with `parseEther(state.mintPrice || '0')` and `BigInt(state.maxSupply || '0')` BEFORE the try block at line 70 — a value like '1e4' or '0.0.5' (typeable in number inputs) throws uncaught in the click handler with no error surfaced. Nothing prevents deploying with maxSupply '0' or maxSupply cleared.
findings.suggestion: Move the DEPLOY_SUCCESS dispatch into a useEffect keyed on [isSuccess, deployedCollection]; move cfg construction inside the try; validate maxSupply ≥ 1, maxPerWallet ≤ maxSupply before enabling Deploy.

findings.title: Repay button disappears the second the local clock passes the deadline — borrower cannot repay during the on-chain grace period
findings.evidence: NFTLendingSection.tsx:1091 `{isBorrower && status === 'active' && (<button onClick={handleRepay} ...)}` and the repayment quote read is `enabled: isBorrower && status === 'active'` (line 948). getLoanStatus (line 80) flips to 'overdue' purely on `Date.now() > deadline`. The product copy promises a '1-hour grace period' (LendingPage.tsx:32, ConnectPrompt.tsx:41) and the sibling LendingSection allows repay while overdue (LendingSection.tsx:1629 `(status === 'active' || status === 'overdue')`). A borrower seconds past deadline — still inside grace — loses the repay affordance entirely and is steered toward default.
findings.suggestion: Mirror LendingSection: keep Repay (and the getRepaymentAmount read) enabled for status 'overdue' until defaultClaimed; ideally read the contract's isDefaulted/grace state instead of local clock.

findings.title: Lender 'Claim Collateral' shown during grace period when the claim would revert
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:1640 `{role === 'lender' && (defaulted || status === 'overdue') && !loan.defaultClaimed && (...)}` — `status === 'overdue'` is local-clock past-deadline; the isDefaulted read (1526-1532) is fetched but OR-ed rather than required, so during the 1-hour grace window (defaulted=false, overdue=true) the button renders and claimDefaultedCollateral reverts on-chain.
findings.suggestion: Require `defaulted === true` to enable the button; while overdue-but-in-grace show a disabled state with a 'grace period — claimable in Xm' countdown.

findings.title: Contract reads fire against address(0) — TEGRIDY_LENDING is zeroed but protocolFeeBps/offerCount/loanCount have no enabled gate
findings.evidence: constants.ts:47 `TEGRIDY_LENDING_ADDRESS = '0x0000...0000'` (ZEROED 2026-05-31). LendingSection.tsx:457-461 (protocolFeeBps), 1743-1747 (offerCount), 1794-1798 (loanCount) call useReadContract with no `query: { enabled: deployed }`. eth_call to 0x0 returns '0x', decode fails, react-query retries — wasted RPC + error churn on every visit to the default tab. NFTLendingSection (lines 110/116/122) and LaunchpadSection (line 47) gate the exact same reads with `enabled: isDeployed(...)` — this file is the odd one out.
findings.suggestion: Add `query: { enabled: deployed }` to all three reads (the `deployed` const already exists at line 1846).

findings.title: text-black tokens on dark surfaces — LTV 'safe' color contradicts its own green bar; repaid badge, APR cells, labels near-invisible
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:168 computeLTV returns `'text-black'` for the safe <50% bucket while the LTV bar at line 1215 paints the same bucket emerald `'#34d399'` — clear sign the text token regressed (likely a find/replace casualty). Same pattern: STATUS_COLORS.repaid `text: 'text-black'` on bg-emerald-500/30 over rgba(13,21,48) cards (line 249); APR table cells `text-black` (1068, 1124, 1599); `= {aprPercent}%` (822); Estimated Earnings value `font-mono text-black` (900); EmptyState icon `text-black` on purple-500/40 (310). The page background is #060c1a and CARD_BG is rgba(13,21,48,0.6) — black text on these is unreadable wherever the rotated art behind it is dark. NFTLendingSection (newer pass) uses text-emerald-400 for the same semantics.
findings.suggestion: Restore the emerald/status tokens (text-emerald-400 for safe LTV/repaid/APR) to match the bar colors and the sibling section. Additive only — no art changes needed.

findings.title: No refetch/invalidation of offer & loan lists after create/accept success — UI shows stale market until reload
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:715-723 (create success only toasts + clears form), 1003-1012 (accept success only toasts + collapses row). useAllOffers/useAllLoans (1742/1793) have no watch/refetchInterval and are never invalidated, so a newly created offer doesn't appear in Borrow, an accepted offer stays listed as available, and My Loans doesn't show the new loan until a full page reload. Same in NFTLendingSection (253-261, 676-686: no offer/loan list refetch on success).
findings.suggestion: On isSuccess, invalidate/refetch offerCount/loanCount + the batch reads (queryClient.invalidateQueries or the refetch handles wagmi returns).

findings.title: Restake is promised by this page's copy and by '/restake' links, but no restake UI exists in any of the four sections
findings.evidence: LendingPage.tsx:19 subtitle 'Staking + Restake', :32 'or restake for bonus rewards', :55 'restake for bonus rewards' — yet sections are lending/nftlending/amm/launchpad only; the actual restake UI lives on FarmPage (FarmPage.tsx:309-331). StakingCard.tsx:322 and DashboardPage.tsx:428 link 'Restake for bonus yield →' to `/restake`, which App.tsx:151 redirects to /nft-finance — landing users on the P2P loan market with no restake control. Also :30 'Connect to lend & borrow TOWELI' / :32 'Supply TOWELI for yield' is wrong — lenders supply ETH against TOWELI staking NFTs, not TOWELI.
findings.suggestion: Point the /restake redirect and the two in-app links at /farm (where restaking lives), and correct the lending prompt copy to 'lend ETH against staking NFTs'. Keep all sections/art as-is.

findings.title: Tracked pools from the pre-relaunch deployment render an infinite skeleton — PoolCard has no error state
findings.evidence: AMMSection.tsx:1483-1490: `if (!poolInfo) { return (<div ... animate-pulse>...) }` is the only non-data branch; useReadContract isError is never consumed. localStorage key 'tegridy-amm-tracked-pools' (line 109) survives the relaunch, so pools tracked against the old (now-dead) factory addresses fail getPoolInfo forever and pulse indefinitely with no message and no way to know why (the remove button still works but nothing tells the user the pool is gone).
findings.suggestion: Branch on isError → compact 'Pool unreachable (old deployment?) — remove from tracking' card with the existing remove affordance.

findings.title: LTV/Position Value silently shows 0 when TOWELI price is unavailable — which is the current live state (unseeded pool)
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:1048-1055 computes positionEthValue from `useTOWELIPrice().priceInEth` with no check of the context's `priceUnavailable`/`oracleStale` flags (PriceContext exposes them, PriceContext.tsx:18-26). computeLTV (162-171) returns `{ ratio: 0 }` when positionValueEth <= 0, so the expanded offer shows 'Position Value 0 ETH' and 'LTV Ratio 0.0%' — reading as zero-risk instead of 'price unavailable'. Per project memory the TOWELI/WETH pool is currently empty, so this is the path every user hits.
findings.suggestion: When priceUnavailable/oracleStale, render 'price unavailable' for Position Value and suppress the LTV number/bar instead of 0.0%.

findings.title: CLOSED/DUTCH_AUCTION/CANCELLED all surface as 'Paused' — the exact mislabel the R071 fix note says was corrected
findings.evidence: launchpadConstants.ts:11-17 documents the fix ('mislabeled CLOSED as "Paused" — paused() is a separate boolean'), but PhaseBadge (launchpadShared.tsx:48-54) still maps every phase other than 1/2 to `label: 'Paused'` — so a live Dutch auction (phase 3) badges as 'Paused'. CollectionDetailV2.tsx:54 `if (drop.currentPhase === 0) return 'Minting Paused'` and :362 'Minting is currently paused for this collection.' label CLOSED as paused while a genuinely-paused contract gets a separate banner (:296-309) — two different states share one word.
findings.suggestion: PhaseBadge: derive from PHASE_LABELS (add Dutch Auction/Cancelled/Closed configs). CollectionDetailV2: say 'Minting closed — the creator hasn't opened the sale' for phase 0.

findings.title: Stale Arweave quote reused after the user goes back and changes the image set
findings.evidence: Step4_FundUpload.tsx:57-59: `else if (phase === 'idle' && state.quoteWei !== null) { setPhase('quoted'); }` — once a quote exists (or is restored from a draft via CreateWizard.tsx:41), re-entering Step 4 never re-quotes even though `bytesToPay` (lines 39-42) may now be much larger after adding images in Step 2. The 20% FUNDING_BUFFER_BPS won't cover a meaningfully bigger folder; the upload then fails mid-pipeline after the fund leg.
findings.suggestion: Store the byte total alongside quoteWei and re-quote when `bytesToPay` differs (or always re-quote on step entry; quoting is free).

findings.title: autoTracked never resets — the second pool deployed in a session is never auto-tracked or announced
findings.evidence: AMMSection.tsx:1958-1983: the PoolCreated decode effect early-returns `if (!isDeploySuccess || !deployReceipt || autoTracked) return;` and `autoTracked` (line 1917) is set once and never cleared (the success path resets collection/nftIds/ethDeposit but not autoTracked). Deploying a second pool silently skips addTrackedPool + the success toast.
findings.suggestion: Reset autoTracked when a new deployTx hash appears (effect on deployTx), or key the guard on the receipt's txHash instead of a boolean.

findings.title: Stat labels/tooltips disagree with the numbers: 'Total Offers' includes cancelled offers; 'Active Loans' counts all loans ever
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:451 `const offerCountNum = allOffers.length` (includes inactive) under tooltip 'Number of active loan offers available for borrowers to accept' (line 480). NFTLendingSection.tsx:160 'Active Loans' renders `loanCount` = total loanCount read (line 112-117), which includes repaid and defaulted loans.
findings.suggestion: Filter `o.active` for the offer stat; for NFT lending either relabel to 'Total Loans' or filter parsed loans by status.

findings.title: Refund transactions toast 'Mint confirmed!' / 'Mint failed'
findings.evidence: useNFTDropV2.ts:225-236: the single tx-result effect toasts `'Mint confirmed!'` on isSuccess and `'Mint failed'` on error for every write through this hook — including `refund()` (line 204). A user pulling funds from a cancelled sale sees 'Mint confirmed!'.
findings.suggestion: Track the last action ('mint' | 'refund') in a ref and word the toasts accordingly.

findings.title: Computed validation warnings are built then thrown away — 'files not referenced in CSV' never shown from this step
findings.evidence: Step2_Upload.tsx:27-50: `const warnings: string[] = [...state.validationWarnings]; ... warnings.push(...img.warnings); ... warnings.push(\`${extraFiles.length} uploaded file(s) not referenced in CSV\`);` but the dispatch at line 50 is `dispatch({ type: 'VALIDATION_ERRORS', errors })` — warnings is never dispatched or rendered (the warning surface at line 275 reads state.validationWarnings, which only CSV_PARSED sets in Step 3).
findings.suggestion: Dispatch the merged warnings too (extend VALIDATION_ERRORS payload or add a VALIDATION_WARNINGS action).

findings.title: Raw parseEther/BigInt on user input can throw uncaught in click handlers; the repo's safeParseEther lib is unused here
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:746 `const principalWei = parseEther(principal);` and :765-767 `parseEther(minCollateral), parseEther(minCollateralETH || '0')` are not wrapped — a number-input value like '1e-19' (valid for type=number) makes viem throw, the handler dies silently, no toast. OwnerAdminPanelV2.tsx:280 `BigInt(maxPerWallet)` throws on '1.5'; :267 `parseEther(mintPrice)` likewise. lib\safeParseEther.ts exists precisely for this and is used elsewhere in the app.
findings.suggestion: Route these through safeParseEther (and a safe BigInt parse) with a toast on invalid input, matching the rest of the app.

findings.title: Lender earnings preview ignores the protocol fee its own stats card advertises; PnL assumes full-term interest
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:726-732 estimatedEarnings = p*rate*years with no protocolFeeBps deduction, while the StatsBar tooltip (line 502) says the fee is 'taken from interest earned by lenders'. TxSummary (909) tells the lender 'you earn ~X ETH'. PnlSummaryCard (1417-1437) computes interest from `deadline - startTime` (full term) even though repayment is pro-rata — overstating both 'Interest Earned' and 'Interest Paid' for early repayments.
findings.suggestion: Net the preview by protocolFeeBps (already fetched in StatsBar) and label PnL figures as 'max (full-term) estimate', or derive actual interest from repayment events when available.

findings.title: Hardcoded '0.5%' protocol fee and permanent placeholder copy that won't update when the contracts deploy
findings.evidence: AMMSection.tsx:421 `{ label: 'Protocol Fee', value: '0.5%' ...}` is hardcoded (LendingSection reads protocolFeeBps on-chain; this section never does — drift risk if the owner retunes). AMMSection.tsx:998 TradeHistory placeholder always says 'Trade history will appear here once the protocol is live' even when `deployed` is true; line 2503 'Cumulative LP fees (available after launch)' likewise renders forever — three surfaces that will still say 'after launch' after launch.
findings.suggestion: Read protocolFeeBps from the factory; gate the placeholder copy on `deployed` (and wire TradeHistory to the proven PoolTradeHistory getLogs pattern once live).

findings.title: 'Total Revenue' = mintPrice × totalMinted — wrong for Dutch-auction or repriced drops
findings.evidence: launchpadShared.tsx:272 `const totalRevenue = Number(formatEther(drop.mintPrice * BigInt(drop.totalMinted)));` assumes every token sold at the current flat mintPrice; Dutch-auction mints (variable clearing prices) and any mid-sale setMintPrice change make this number fiction, presented unqualified on the creator dashboard.
findings.suggestion: Label it 'Est. revenue (flat-price)' or compute from the contract's actual proceeds/paidPerWallet sums.

findings.title: Three different not-deployed gate patterns for sibling features
findings.evidence: LendingPage.tsx:236-240: only nftlending gets the shared FeatureNotDeployed placeholder; 'lending' renders the full interactive LendingSection with an amber banner (LendingSection.tsx:1855-1861) + per-button DisabledWrap; 'amm' renders full UI with its own inline amber div (AMMSection.tsx:2661-2668); 'launchpad' returns a bespoke plain card (LaunchpadSection.tsx:98-109). Four gated features, three UX treatments — users get inconsistent signals about what 'not live' means.
findings.suggestion: Pick one pattern (FeatureNotDeployed hero with an optional 'explore the interface' expander) and apply it to all gated sections — additive, keeps existing art.

findings.title: Unbounded batch reads of every offer and loan ever created; no pagination anywhere
findings.evidence: LendingSection.tsx:1751-1758 builds `Array.from({ length: count })` getOffer calls (same for loans at 1802-1809); NFTLendingSection.tsx:484-495 likewise. At a few thousand offers this is a giant multicall on every visit and an ever-growing render list. LaunchpadSection.tsx:53 hard-caps at 20 collections silently — items 21+ are invisible with no 'load more'.
findings.suggestion: Page the reads (newest-N + load more), and surface the launchpad cap ('showing 20 of N + Load more').

findings.title: Expanded trade history re-runs two getLogs calls every block
findings.evidence: AMMSection.tsx:1318 `useBlockNumber({ watch: true, query: { refetchInterval: 30_000 } })` plus blockNumber in the effect deps (1324-1375) means the full 10k-block getLogs pair re-executes on every new block (~12s) while expanded — the comment promises refetch 'when the latest block advances past our last fetch by a reasonable delta' but no delta check exists.
findings.suggestion: Keep lastFetchedBlock in a ref and only re-run when `blockNumber - lastFetched > 25` (or drop watch and rely on the 30s interval).

findings.title: Nested tabs aren't URL-addressable — dashboard 'view your loan' links can't land on My Loans
findings.evidence: Only ?section= is in the URL (LendingPage.tsx:91). LendingSection's lend/borrow/myloans (line 1845 useState), AMM's trade/create/pools (2650) and NFT lending's tabs (103) all reset to default on every navigation. DashboardPage.tsx:731 links a specific loan to '/nft-finance?section=nftlending' but the user still lands on the Lend tab and must find their loan manually.
findings.suggestion: Add a ?tab= param (and optional ?offer=/#loan-id anchor) handled the same R007 Pattern-A way.

findings.title: Accessibility gaps: labels not associated with inputs, clickable rows/headers without keyboard support, inner tab bars lack tab roles
findings.evidence: Every `<label className={labelClass}>` in AMMSection/LendingSection lacks htmlFor/id pairing (e.g. AMMSection.tsx:756-764, LendingSection.tsx:782-794) — CollectionDetailV2 (380/394) shows the codebase knows the right pattern. SortHeader is a clickable <th onClick> with no button/keyboard handler (LendingSection.tsx:94-98); OfferRow rows toggle on tr onClick only (1059-1062); inner TabNavs (LendingSection.tsx:563, AMMSection.tsx:452) have no role=tablist/tab/aria-selected though the page-level toggle does (LendingPage.tsx:188-199); quantity +/− buttons unlabeled (AMMSection.tsx:786-801, CollectionDetailV2.tsx:416-430); TraitEditor dialog has no focus trap/initial focus (TraitEditor.tsx:61-80, Esc works).
findings.suggestion: id/htmlFor every input, wrap sort labels in <button>, add role=button+tabIndex+Enter handling to expandable rows, mirror the page-level tablist roles, aria-label steppers, trap focus in TraitEditor.

findings.title: Dev-grade inputs for money-critical admin actions: raw unix timestamp, bps fields, native window.confirm
findings.evidence: OwnerAdminPanelV2.tsx:303-309 Dutch auction start is a bare 'Start (unix)' number field (no datetime picker, no 'now + 1h' helper, no current-time hint); phase grid (181-194) defaults to '0' (Closed) without highlighting the actual on-chain phase already fetched at line 46 — one stray 'Set Phase' click closes a live mint; cancelSale uses `window.confirm` (407-411) while the app ships ui\TypedConfirmation.tsx for exactly this class of irreversible action.
findings.suggestion: datetime-local input converted to unix; pre-select/highlight the on-chain phase in the grid; use TypedConfirmation for cancelSale.

findings.title: Per-LoanRow 1Hz re-renders for minute-granularity display; dead exported showcase components ship in the bundle
findings.evidence: useCountdown ticks setInterval every 1000ms (useCountdown.ts:25) per LoanRow, but LendingSection renders only `Xd:HHh:MMm` (line 42 of hook output, used at 1617) — N loans = N stateful 1Hz re-render loops for a minutes display. ComingSoonState (LendingSection.tsx:350-445), SkeletonLayout (220), LendingPulseDot (268) and ComingSoon (AMMSection.tsx:2581-2644) are exported '@internal Reserved' dead code kept alive in the page chunk.
findings.suggestion: Accept a tick-interval param (60s when not urgent); move the reserved components behind a lazy import or delete-on-confirm with the owner.

findings.title: Tab-switch history semantics contradict the comment; aria-controls points at nonexistent panels when disconnected
findings.evidence: LendingPage.tsx:97 `setSearchParams(params, { replace: true })` under the comment 'deep-links + Back/Forward stay correct' (88-90) — with replace, Back skips tab changes entirely (defensible, but the comment overclaims). When !isConnected, tabs still set `aria-controls={nft-finance-panel-...}` (199) but no element with that id exists since ConnectPrompt replaces the panel (219-224).
findings.suggestion: Either drop replace for explicit tab clicks or fix the comment; render the panel id on the ConnectPrompt wrapper.

findings.title: No 'My Offers' management or cancel-offer affordance — lender ETH escrowed with no UI path to recover it

findings.title: Clicking 'Gallery' in any nav lands on the Floor/listings tab — gallery is unreachable from every nav surface
findings.evidence: App.jsx:358 builds the gallery URL as empty segment: navigate(`/nakamigos/${collectionSlug}/${newTab === "gallery" ? "" : newTab}`) → pathname '/nakamigos/nakamigos/'. parseRoute (App.jsx:91) maps a bare collection path to listings: `const second = segments[1] || "listings";`. So every gallery navigation — Header PRIMARY_NAV 'Gallery' (Header.jsx:128), MobileNav gallery icon (MobileNav.jsx:5), keyboard '1'/'g' (App.jsx:114-121,453), header logo click (Header.jsx:367), About.onNavigateGallery and TraitExplorer.onFilterGallery 'filter then jump to gallery' flows (App.jsx:629,647) — resolves to tab 'listings', and the 'Floor' nav item lights up active instead. /nakamigos/<slug>/gallery typed directly works (VALID_TABS includes 'gallery', constants.js:69), proving the tab itself renders. navRouting.test.jsx only asserts nav keys ∈ VALID_TABS, not URL construction, so the guard missed it. Likely regression from flipping the default tab to 'listings' without updating the gallery→'' shorthand.
findings.suggestion: In handleTabChange, navigate to the explicit segment (`/nakamigos/${slug}/gallery`), or make parseRoute's default segment 'gallery' again — and add a unit test that round-trips handleTabChange URL building through parseRoute for every VALID_TABS entry.

findings.title: Shared ?token= links never open the modal: the URL-sync effect deletes the param before the reader effect runs
findings.evidence: Modal.jsx:343 copies `${origin}/nakamigos/${slug}/gallery?token=${nft.id}` as the share link. In CollectionView, the URL↔modal sync effect is declared first (App.jsx:280-288): on mount selected is null so `next = null`, `current = '<id>'`, they differ → `url.searchParams.delete("token"); window.history.replaceState(...)`. The param-reading effect is declared after it (App.jsx:291-309) and reads `new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("token")` — by then the param is already gone, so it sets tokenParamHandled=true and never opens the modal or calls fetchTokensByIds. React runs same-component effects in declaration order, so this is deterministic: human recipients land on the gallery tab with no modal (unfurl bots still get the OG card from the edge middleware, masking the breakage).
findings.suggestion: Read the token param ONCE before the sync effect can touch the URL (e.g. capture window.location.search in a module-level/useRef initializer at mount, or move the reader effect above the sync effect and guard the sync effect until the param has been consumed).

findings.title: Keyboard and assistive-tech users cannot enter the app — 'CLICK TO ENTER' is a click-only gate on a non-focusable div, on every visit
findings.evidence: SplashScreen.jsx:749-755: the only path to onComplete is `onClick={handleEnter}` on a plain <div> with no role, tabIndex, or keydown handler; the 'CLICK TO ENTER' element is a <motion.span> (SplashScreen.jsx:1372-1381), also non-focusable. App.jsx:161-163 renders nothing but the splash until splashDone, and the splash replays on every entry to /nakamigos (App.jsx:138-143, intentional per the comment). There is no skip control. Net effect: a keyboard-only or switch-access user is hard-blocked from the entire Tradermigos sub-app.
findings.suggestion: Additive fix that keeps the splash exactly as designed: add tabIndex={0}, role="button", an aria-label, autofocus when phase==='ready', and an Enter/Space keydown that calls handleEnter.

findings.title: At exactly 768px viewport width every navigation surface is hidden (iPad Mini/9.7"/10.2" portrait = 768 CSS px)
findings.evidence: App.css:1370 hides desktop tabs at ≤768 (`@media (max-width: 768px) { .desktop-nav { display: none; } }`); App.css:1437 hides the hamburger at ≥768 with !important; App.css:3704-3707 only shows .mobile-bottom-nav at ≤767. At width == 768 all three rules apply → no desktop nav, no hamburger, no bottom nav. Conflicts with the standing 'flawless on iPads' requirement.
findings.suggestion: Align the boundaries: make the bottom-nav breakpoint ≤768 (or desktop-nav hide ≤767) so the two ranges share an edge.

findings.title: ErrorBoundary 'Go Home' sets window.location.hash on a BrowserRouter app — it does not navigate, so a deterministically-crashing tab is an inescapable loop
findings.evidence: ErrorBoundary.jsx:134: `window.location.hash = "#/nakamigos/"` — but the app mounts under BrowserRouter (nakamigos/main.jsx:13 standalone; the embedded app uses the parent's BrowserRouter via frontend/src/App.tsx:121). Hash changes don't change pathname, so the route — and the crashing tab — re-renders; the button also does setState({hasError:false}) first, so render-time crashes are immediately re-caught and the user is back on the same error screen. The tab boundary deliberately passes no onReset (App.jsx:743-745: 'the Go Home button is the escape hatch') — i.e., the documented escape hatch is broken. NotFound.jsx:31 has the same dead hash fallback (mitigated because both App.jsx call sites pass onGoHome).
findings.suggestion: Replace the hash write with a hard `window.location.href = '/nakamigos'` (matching the app-level boundary at App.jsx:967) or accept a navigate callback prop.

findings.title: PageTransition is dead code at runtime — the key={tab} error-latch fix remounts it on every tab change, so its tabKey-change detector never fires
findings.evidence: App.jsx:745-749: `<ErrorBoundary key={tab}> <Suspense> <PageTransition tabKey={tab}>`. A key change unmounts and remounts the whole subtree, so PageTransition mounts fresh with `prevKeyRef.current = tabKey` (PageTransition.jsx:147) and its transition effect bails at PageTransition.jsx:167 (`if (prevKeyRef.current === tabKey) return;`). The entire glitch/cover/reveal choreography (PageTransition.jsx:14-142 injected styles, 3-phase state machine) never executes; tabs now hard-swap. The latch fix itself works (errors don't persist across tabs) — but it silently disabled the transition feature the component exists for, and injectStyles() still runs per mount (PageTransition.jsx:161-163, removes+re-adds the style tag).
findings.suggestion: Either accept and delete-route the transition (owner decision), or keep the boundary keyed while hoisting PageTransition ABOVE the keyed boundary so it survives tab changes and animates the swap.

findings.title: Two theme systems write the same documentElement data-theme attribute — visiting Tradermigos permanently clobbers the main app's light/dark theme until reload or manual toggle
findings.evidence: nakamigos/contexts/ThemeContext.jsx:105 sets `document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", themeId)` with values default|midnight|sovereign, plus body classes (lines 103-104) and meta theme-color (108-111), with NO unmount cleanup. The main app's ThemeContext.tsx:30 sets the same attribute with dark|light and only re-applies inside a [theme] effect — it stays mounted across routes, so leaving /nakamigos never restores it. A light-mode user who visits /nakamigos returns to a main app where every `[data-theme="light"]` selector (index.css:551-680) stops matching — the UI silently reverts to dark and the mobile browser chrome keeps the nakamigos theme-color.
findings.suggestion: Scope the nakamigos attribute to the .nakamigos-app element only (App.css already supports `.nakamigos-app[data-theme=…]`, App.css:101-135) and add a ThemeProvider unmount cleanup that restores the main app's data-theme + meta theme-color.

findings.title: 4 of 5 tour steps anchor to selectors that don't exist anywhere in the codebase — the tour degrades to floating centered tooltips with no spotlight
findings.evidence: Onboarding.jsx STEPS selectors vs grep over frontend/src/nakamigos: step 1 `.gallery-grid, .virtual-gallery-grid` — .gallery-grid exists only in Favorites.jsx:56 and MyCollection.jsx:370/394, not on the default tab, and no element has class virtual-gallery-grid (VirtualGalleryGrid renders .nft-card items only, VirtualGalleryGrid.jsx:276); steps 2/4/5 reference `[data-tour=…]`, `.tab-floor`, `.listings-tab`, `button[data-tab='floor']`, `.cart-icon`, `.cart-btn` — zero matches (the Header cart button has no className, Header.jsx:504-508; nav buttons are `.nav-tab` only, Header.jsx:388). Only step 3 (.wallet-btn) anchors. resolveTarget falls back to a centered tooltip with setSpotlightRect(null) (Onboarding.jsx:154-162), and step 1's copy ('Browse the … collection with rarity scores') shows over the Floor tab since the default route is listings. The well-built spotlight/pulse machinery effectively never runs.
findings.suggestion: Add the data-tour attributes to Header's cart button, the Floor nav-tab, and the 'Keys' button, and a data-tour='gallery' on VirtualGalleryGrid's container — purely additive, makes the existing spotlight code light up.

findings.title: Three independent always-on pollers fetch the same stats/activity endpoints — up to ~6 requests/min per idle visitor, none gated on tab visibility
findings.evidence: useSmartAlerts.js:7,328-331 polls fetchCollectionStats + fetchActivity every 30s unconditionally (floor alerts are enabled by default, DEFAULT_CONFIG line 14); PriceAlerts.jsx:8,58-71 polls fetchCollectionStats every 30s (usePriceAlerts is mounted at App.jsx:566 on every tab); useCollection.js:9-10,80-85 polls stats+activity every 60s (5min with WS). Only useDmUnread checks document.hidden (useDmUnread.js:32). No shared cache: react-query is used only for listings (useListings.js). Given the prod Upstash rate-limiter incident in memory, this is the first thing to consolidate.
findings.suggestion: Route stats/activity through react-query with a shared queryKey + refetchInterval, and gate refetchIntervalInBackground off; alert engines can subscribe to the same cache.

findings.title: The reduced-motion rule `.splash-screen { display:none }` targets a class the splash never applies — and if it ever matched it would soft-lock the app
findings.evidence: App.css:3551 (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .splash-screen { display: none; } }`) and App.css:1988 style a .splash-screen class, but SplashScreen.jsx:752 renders className={exitPhase === "glitch" ? "splash-glitch" : ""} — 'splash-screen' is never applied (grep confirms only App.css references it). So reduced-motion users still get the full rAF physics + framer-motion splash (framer animates inline styles; the CSS animation-duration kill at App.css:3545-3550 doesn't affect it). Worse, if someone 'fixed' the class without reading App.jsx:161-163, display:none would hide the only element whose click calls onComplete → permanent black screen for reduced-motion users.
findings.suggestion: Honor the preference in JS instead: in SplashScreen, if matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches, skip physics/exit choreography and show a static title + Enter button (keeps the art, drops the motion); delete or rewrite the dead CSS rule.

findings.title: Deep link to a token outside the loaded pages opens an empty placeholder modal (no image, no traits) — it never fetches the token, unlike the ?token= path
findings.evidence: App.jsx:330-338: when the deep-linked id isn't in nfts.allTokens it does `setSelected({ id: deepLinkTokenId, name: `#${deepLinkTokenId}`, attributes: [], image: null })` with no fetch. The ?token= handler right above it (App.jsx:301-308) calls fetchTokensByIds for exactly this case. Modal.jsx has no metadata self-fetch (only sales history + order validation, Modal.jsx:55,130). With 40 tokens per page (useNfts.js:29), virtually any shared /nft/:id link beyond the first page shows a blank shell.
findings.suggestion: Reuse the fetchTokensByIds fallback from the ?token= handler in the /nft/:id effect.

findings.title: Confirmed: every cart/favorite/toast/activity change re-renders the entire CollectionView tree — the fine-grained context split is defeated by top-level consumption + prop drilling
findings.evidence: CollectionView (App.jsx:250-267) consumes useToast, useFavorites, useCart, useCollection (activities update on every poll/WS event), useListings, useNfts at the top and passes slices down as props to Header and every tab. One addToCart → CartContext value changes → CollectionView re-renders → renderTab() re-renders the active tab and Header's memo (Header.jsx:253) is defeated because activities/cartCount/lastRefresh props change anyway. The contexts themselves are well-memoized (CartContext.jsx:46-49 etc.) but no leaf consumes them directly.
findings.suggestion: Have leaf components (Header badge, cart drawer, tab bodies) consume the contexts directly, and split the high-churn activities feed out of useCollection's return object so ticker updates don't ripple through renderTab.

findings.title: Clicking Install a second time after dismissing the native prompt throws — deferredPrompt isn't cleared on 'dismissed' outcome
findings.evidence: InstallPrompt.jsx:22-29: `await deferredPrompt.prompt(); const { outcome } = await deferredPrompt.userChoice; if (outcome === "accepted") setDeferredPrompt(null);` — a BeforeInstallPromptEvent's prompt() can only be called once; on 'dismissed' the stale event stays in state, the banner stays visible, and the next click rejects with InvalidStateError inside an un-try/catch'd async handler (and the embedded app doesn't install nakamigos/main.jsx's global unhandledrejection hook).
findings.suggestion: setDeferredPrompt(null) regardless of outcome (Chrome may re-fire beforeinstallprompt later), and wrap in try/catch.

findings.title: Closing a deep-linked modal (X or Escape) silently switches the underlying tab from Gallery to Floor
findings.evidence: App.jsx:762 and App.jsx:496: onClose/Escape do `navigate(`/nakamigos/${collectionSlug}`, { replace: true })` when pathname includes '/nft/'. parseRoute maps the bare collection path to 'listings' (App.jsx:91), but /:collection/nft/:id renders tab 'gallery' (App.jsx:95) — so the content under the modal swaps from gallery to listings on close. Same root cause family as the gallery-segment bug.
findings.suggestion: Navigate to `/nakamigos/${slug}/gallery` (or whatever segment the gallery fix lands on).

findings.title: The hamburger button and .mobile-nav drawer are dead UI — CSS hides the hamburger at every viewport width
findings.evidence: Base .hamburger is display:none (App.css:1023-1027); shown at ≤768 (App.css:1371) but re-hidden with !important at ≤767 (App.css:3713) and at ≥768 (App.css:1437) — the show rule can never win at any width (no other stylesheet defines .hamburger; grep outside nakamigos returns nothing). Header.jsx still ships the button (438-442), the mobileOpen state, and the visibleAll drawer (561-569) — unreachable code paths that also confused the 768px nav-gap picture.
findings.suggestion: Owner call: either revive the drawer for the tablet width band (fixing the 768px gap) or excise the dead state/markup; don't leave both.

findings.title: Fallback data fabricates activity by real, named wallets with fresh fake timestamps — a trust risk that contradicts the project's honesty-pass standard
findings.evidence: constants.js:176-182 FALLBACK_WHALES invents 'vitalik.eth Bought 3, 4m ago', 'pranksy.eth Swept 8, 23m ago' etc.; constants.js:184-189 FALLBACK_ACTIVITY generates sales stamped `Date.now() - 120000` so they always render as '2 minutes ago'; api.js:504 and api.js:585 serve these when live endpoints fail. The only disclosure is the small DEMO badge (Header.jsx:446-453), which is hidden entirely at ≤390px (App.css:4294-4297 hides .header-status-group).
findings.suggestion: Watermark fallback rows inline ('sample data') or use obviously-synthetic ENS names; keep the badge visible at all widths.

findings.title: More menu lacks Escape-close, focus management, and recomputes its fixed position only at open
findings.evidence: Header.jsx:306-314 captures getBoundingClientRect once in toggleMore; the portal (402-433) is position:fixed with that stale top/right, so a resize/scroll while open leaves it floating; no keydown handler (Escape doesn't close; App.jsx's global Escape handler doesn't know about it), no focus trap or arrow-key navigation despite aria-haspopup/aria-expanded being set.
findings.suggestion: Close on Escape + focus the first item on open + reposition on resize (or anchor with position:absolute inside the relative wrapper that already exists at Header.jsx:392).

findings.title: Clicking the connected-wallet address instantly disconnects with no menu or confirm
findings.evidence: Header.jsx:316-323 handleConnect: `if (wallet) { setWallet(); return; }` where setWallet is handleDisconnect (App.jsx:513-516). One misclick on your own address = disconnect + toast. Best-in-class headers (OpenSea/Uniswap/RainbowKit's own ConnectButton) open an account menu (copy address / explorer / disconnect).
findings.suggestion: Swap the bare onClick for a small account popover; the disconnect toast already exists.

findings.title: Background mounts 20 full-res ghost-art JPEGs (~2.3 MB, two files >400 KB) plus 6 always-animating blur(60-100px) layers with no lazy/idle loading and no reduced-motion gating outside Starfield
findings.evidence: Background.jsx:72-102 BG_ART lists 20 /splash/*.jpg images (measured: G8jE1EcWMAAvHTy.jpg 454 KB, G-AVjGGakAAuW7Z.jpg 425 KB; total ≈2.3 MB) rendered as with no loading="lazy"/decoding="async" (GhostArt, 104-136); MeshGradient/LightRays/GlassOrbs/DustMotes run infinite framer-motion loops over filter:blur(30-100px) surfaces (139-296); only Starfield checks prefers-reduced-motion (Background.jsx:365). Renders on every nakamigos page including landing.
findings.suggestion: Keep all the art (owner constraint) — add loading="lazy" decoding="async", defer GhostArt mounting to requestIdleCallback after first paint, serve webp/avif variants, and skip the infinite motion loops (render static frames) under prefers-reduced-motion.

findings.title: Splash entry costs ~7s of forced wait per visit: 4s purely synthetic progress, a mandatory click, then a 2.65s exit chain
findings.evidence: SplashScreen.jsx:647 TOTAL_DURATION=4000 drives a timer-only progress bar (no real loading is measured); phase 'ready' requires a click (677); the exit chain is glitch 900 + flash 150 + cover 1200 + collapse 400 = 2650ms desktop (688-700) before onComplete. The splash replays on every entry to /nakamigos by explicit owner request (App.jsx:138-143) — the duration, not the existence, is the cost.
findings.suggestion: Keep the splash; tie the progress bar to actual chunk/data readiness so it can finish early, and trim the desktop exit to the mobile timings (400/100/600/300 = 1.4s) which already feel complete.

findings.title: Non-chunk errors render the raw stack trace to end users
findings.evidence: ErrorBoundary.jsx:102-104 prints `(this.state.error?.message …) + "\n\n" + (this.state.error?.stack || "")` in the user-facing card (wordBreak:break-all, maxHeight 300). Useful in dev, hostile in prod for a retail marketplace.
findings.suggestion: Show the message only, gate the stack behind import.meta.env.DEV or a 'details' disclosure.

findings.title: Splash stats plaque and loading messages are hardcoded to the default collection regardless of destination
findings.evidence: SplashScreen.jsx:1409-1414 always reads COLLECTIONS[DEFAULT_COLLECTION] ('20,000 WORKS / ERC-721 / ETHEREUM') even when entering via a junglebay/gnssart deep link; the status line concatenates LOADING_MESSAGES of all three collections (1389) so a Nakamigos visitor sees 'Swinging through the jungle canopy…'. Charming but imprecise — the per-collection LOADING_MESSAGES sets in constants.js:419-447 were clearly written to be collection-scoped.
findings.suggestion: Parse the target collection from location.pathname inside SplashScreen and feed the matching messages/stats.

findings.title: Assorted polish: 'x' dismiss glyph, parseInt-lenient token ids, Ticker interval runs while tab hidden, IS_MOBILE frozen at module load
findings.evidence: InstallPrompt.jsx:71 dismiss button renders the letter 'x' (not × / an SVG); parseRoute App.jsx:94 parseInt('12abc')=12 so /nft/12abc resolves to token 12; Header.jsx Ticker setInterval (13-23) and StaleIndicator (76-78) keep firing when document.hidden; SplashScreen.jsx:5 computes IS_MOBILE once at module load so a rotated tablet keeps the wrong piece set until reload.
findings.suggestion: Each is a one-line fix; bundle them into the next UX batch.

findings.title: Two toast systems live in one product: nakamigos hand-rolled Toast vs the main app's sonner
findings.evidence: nakamigos ToastContext.jsx + Toast.jsx implement a custom queue (well: 500ms dedupe ToastContext.jsx:12, undo buttons, aria-live), while the rest of Tegridy Farms uses sonner — duplicated behavior, slightly different look/stacking. Not a bug; an consistency/maintenance note.
findings.suggestion: Long-term: adapt addToast to wrap sonner with the nakamigos skin so dedupe/undo semantics live in one place.

findings.title: Seaport domain pinned to v1.5 with the code's own 'verify if OpenSea migrates to 1.6' note still unresolved (unverified runtime impact)
findings.evidence: constants.js:95-105 pins SEAPORT_ADDRESS to 1.5 (0x…aF14dC) and SEAPORT_DOMAIN version '1.5' described as 'use this everywhere for Seaport signing'; the comment itself flags 1.6 (0x…3eB395). OpenSea's default protocol has been Seaport 1.6 since 2024. Whether fulfillment paths honor each order's own protocolAddress was not verified in this pass — flagging as a must-verify before relying on native listing/offer signing, not as a confirmed bug.
findings.suggestion: Audit api.js/orderbook.js signing + fulfillment to confirm protocolAddress is taken from the order, and add a 1.6 domain constant if native orders should match OpenSea's current protocol.

findings.title: Filter, sort, search, and scroll state are not URL-persisted or restored — tab switches destroy context
findings.evidence: Gallery.jsx:20-26 holds search/viewMode/priceRange in local state; useNfts.js:13 holds activeFilters/sortBy in hook state; handleTabChange always window.scrollTo top (App.jsx:360); the key={tab} boundary plus renderTab component swap remount tabs, so returning to Gallery loses filters, search, sort, and scroll position. Blur/OpenSea keep filter state in the querystring and restore scroll.
findings.suggestion: Serialize activeFilters/sortBy/search into searchParams (the router is already there) and skip the scroll-to-top when navigating back to a previously-visited tab.

good: Layered error-boundary architecture is genuinely good: app-level boundary with hard-reload reset (App.jsx:967), per-surface boundaries for modal/cart/overlays each with scoped onReset (App.jsx:754-861), and the key={tab} un-latch fix verifiably prevents one crashed tab from bricking the rest (App.jsx:741-745) — Try Again correctly retries in place for transient errors. Chunk-load failures are detected and auto-reloaded with a bounded 3-attempt/30s sessionStorage guard (ErrorBoundary.jsx:27-44).

navRouting.test.jsx encodes real shipped-bug classes as cheap source-level guards (nav ⊆ VALID_TABS, every VALID_TABS has a renderTab case, TradeWindow/TradesPanel import without TDZ throw) — exactly the right altitude for this codebase.

useNfts is well-engineered: AbortController invalidation on collection switch (62-75), pagination dedupe by id (43-49), memoized rarity/filter/sort pipeline (130-158), throttled auto-load only for <1000-supply collections (84-98), and loadAll as a resumable effect loop.

All 7 contexts memoize their values, throw on use-outside-provider, persist per-collection-slug keys, and normalize token ids to strings (FavoritesContext.jsx:23) — and WalletContext is a clean bridge to the parent wagmi/RainbowKit providers split into state/actions/UI sub-contexts so consumers can subscribe narrowly.

Modal and Onboarding both implement real a11y mechanics: focus trap + focus restore + Escape layering via stopImmediatePropagation (Modal.jsx:159-195), keyboard nav with Tab trapping and ref-counted body scroll lock (Onboarding.jsx:237-259, lib/scrollLock.js).

The splash physics engine has thoughtful perf engineering despite its extravagance: rAF paused on visibilitychange, spark count caps, trail length reduced, depth-blur disabled with a comment, single batched setState per frame, canvas GPU memory disposed on unmount, mobile-reduced art set, and an 8s force-ready failsafe (SplashScreen.jsx:182-192, 321, 663-672).

Theming is properly scoped: CSS variables applied to .nakamigos-app rather than :root, per-theme variable blocks in App.css:101-135, theme-aware Background palettes via MutationObserver, and a documented z-index hierarchy at the top of App.css.

Honest data-state signaling: LIVE/DEMO api-badge with title text, StaleIndicator ('Xm ago') on listings freshness, wrong-network role=alert banner with inline switch action, and per-tab loading/empty/error states in Gallery (error banner with Retry, differentiated empty states for search vs filters vs no data).

Power-user keyboard layer (j/k card navigation, digit tab jumps, f/c favorite/cart on focused card, / search focus, ? help overlay) with input-element guards, plus a discoverable 'Keys' affordance bottom-left.
useDmUnread is the model poller the others should copy: visibility-gated interval, increase-only notifications after first load, never-throws fetch.

Lite/Pro trading mode is a coherent system: single source sets (LITE_HIDDEN_*) shared by Header, MobileNav, and a redirect effect for hidden tabs (App.jsx:315-319), persisted, with Ctrl+Shift+P toggle.
Background wraps itself in a swallow-only error boundary so the decorative layer can never take down the app (Background.jsx:616-621), and Starfield respects prefers-reduced-motion.
Toast system: 500ms message dedupe at the provider, undo actions, full timer cleanup on unmount, aria-live=polite container.

Deliberate, documented decisions throughout (splash-on-every-entry rationale, SIWE button hidden until a feature gates on it, Google Fonts deferred to nakamigos mount with the 503 incident explained, gallery onFilter→tab flows) — the comments record intent, which made this audit's regression detection possible.
missingVsBestInClass: Browser back/forward does not close or restore the NFT detail modal — selected state and the ?token=/nft/:id URL are synced one-way only (no popstate handling); OpenSea/Blur treat item views as history entries so Back closes the modal.

No shareable/persistent gallery state: filters, sort, search, and Lite/Pro mode never reach the URL, so users can't deep-link a filtered view and lose all of it on tab switch (Dexscreener/Blur keep this in the querystring).
No scroll-position restoration when returning to a tab — every navigation scrolls to top (App.jsx:360), so browsing position in a 20k-item gallery is always lost.

No data cache across tab switches: only listings use react-query; stats, activity, tokens, trades, portfolio all refetch from zero each time a tab remounts. Best-in-class apps make tab switches instant from cache with background revalidation.
No prefetch of lazy tab chunks on nav hover/idle — first visit to each tab pays chunk download + skeleton; trivial win with import() on mouseenter.
No USD values at the shell level: header ticker, cart badge area, and floor stats are ETH-only; every comparable marketplace (OpenSea/Blur/Magic Eden) shows fiat equivalents inline.
No aria-current on active nav tabs in Header/MobileNav (active state is color+weight only) and the More dropdown lacks menu semantics/keyboard support — competitor navs are fully keyboard-operable.

No app-wide reduced-motion strategy for the JS-driven motion layers (framer-motion loops, splash physics, canvas systems) — a single MotionConfig reducedMotion='user' plus a JS matchMedia gate would cover what the CSS rule cannot.
No visible skip/fast-path on the splash for repeat visitors (an additive 'press Enter / skip' affordance would keep the owner's splash-every-entry intent while unblocking keyboard users).
No collection switcher inside a collection view — moving from Nakamigos to Jungle Bay requires going back to the landing page; competitor headers offer an inline collection dropdown.
No onboarding re-entry point: once dismissed, the tour is unreachable (no 'replay tour' in the Keys/help overlay), so the (currently broken) anchors will be invisible even after they're fixed.
pagesCovered: nakamigos/App.jsx (full) — routing (parseRoute/VALID_TABS), tab renderer, deep links (?token= and /nft/:id), error-boundary layering, keyboard shortcuts, provider nesting
nakamigos/constants.js (full) — collections config, VALID_TABS, Seaport constants, fallback data, lore/loading messages
nakamigos/App.css — tokens, theme-scoped vars, media-query matrix (hamburger/desktop-nav/bottom-nav breakpoints), reduced-motion + forced-colors blocks, z-index hierarchy

components: Header.jsx, MobileNav.jsx, SplashScreen.jsx (full incl. physics engine + exit choreography), PageTransition.jsx, Background.jsx, ErrorBoundary.jsx, NotFound.jsx, Onboarding.jsx, InstallPrompt.jsx, Toast.jsx, Gallery.jsx, Modal.jsx (shell/effects portion)

public/splash asset weights (grounding the Background payload finding)

findings.title: Loans never refresh after initial load — the 60s interval is a no-op identity setState, and loan status is computed against a frozen timestamp
findings.evidence: C:\Users\jimbo\OneDrive\Desktop\tegriddy farms\frontend\src\hooks\useMyLoans.ts:117-121: `const id = setInterval(() => { if (cancelled) return; // Re-trigger by toggling state — kept simple for the recovery pass. setTokenLoading((p) => p); }, REFETCH_MS);` — `(p) => p` returns the identical value so React bails out (no re-render), and even if it re-rendered the effect deps [publicClient, onMainnet, tokenDeployed, tokenCount, address] are unchanged so the fetch never re-runs. The NFT-loan effect (lines 125-163) has no interval at all. Compounding it, useMyLoans.ts:167 captures `const now = BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000));` inside a useMemo keyed only on [tokenResults, nftResults, address] — since results never refresh, `now` is frozen, so a loan crossing its deadline while the dashboard is open never flips to 'overdue' (status at line 183/207 uses the frozen now). The header comment at line 8-9 claims '60s refetch' — it does not happen. Only a loanCount change (new loan created) re-triggers the scan; repaid/defaulted/overdue transitions go stale indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Drive refetch with a real tick: add a `refreshNonce` state incremented by the interval and include it in both effects' deps; recompute `now` per render (or include a minute-tick state in the useMemo deps) so overdue status updates live.

findings.title: Earnings Projection extrapolates the bootstrap APR to 1 year, ignoring the reward-pool runway and omitting the disclaimer the hook explicitly provides
findings.evidence: C:\Users\jimbo\OneDrive\Desktop\tegriddy farms\frontend\src\pages\DashboardPage.tsx:451 `<Projections staked={stakedTotal} apr={pool.aprNum || 0} ... />` and lines 756-771: `const daily = (staked * apr / 100) / 365 * boost;` rendered for 7/30/90/365 days. usePoolData.ts:76-77 exposes `secondsRemaining` ('Seconds of emission runway left at the current rate') and line 84 exposes `aprDisclaimer: 'Bootstrap rate — falls as staking grows'` — neither is consumed by Projections or shown anywhere on the page. With the documented emission cliff (~Sept-4 per the multi-cycle review) the '1 Year' figure projects rewards that mathematically exceed `rewardsRemaining`. This page repo has had multiple explicit 'honesty passes'; this surface escaped them.
findings.suggestion: Additively render pool.aprDisclaimer under the Projections heading, and cap/flag horizons longer than pool.secondsRemaining (e.g. '~ runway ends in Nd at current rate').

findings.title: Mounting the Dashboard can auto-fire DCA/limit-order wallet popups, while the banner copy claims the user must 'Go to Swap to execute'
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:72-73 mounts `useDCA()` and `useLimitOrders()` just to show counts, but useDCA.ts:537-563 runs `checkDue()` immediately on mount and every 30s, calling `executeDCASwap(s)` which ends in `writeContract(...)` (wallet popup, lines 495-530) — and useLimitOrders.ts:442-522 polls getAmountsOut every 15s and calls `executeOrder(order)` → writeContract. Meanwhile the dashboard banner (DashboardPage.tsx:317-318) says '{n} DCA swap(s) due — Go to Swap to execute'. So a user with a due schedule gets an unprompted signing request on the Dashboard itself, directly contradicting the on-screen copy. Verified end-to-end in code; the cross-tab lock only prevents double-execution, not the popup itself.
findings.suggestion: Either make the copy honest ('a swap prompt will appear here when due') or split the hooks into a read-only variant (counts from localStorage only) for the Dashboard so execution stays on /swap.

findings.title: Active limit orders are mislabeled 'price alerts' directly above the real Price Alerts widget
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:326-335: the card driven by `limitOrders.activeOrders.length` renders `'{n} active price alert{s}'` — but these are limit orders (useLimitOrders), and the actual PriceAlertWidget (a different feature, usePriceAlerts) renders ~6 lines below at line 341. Two distinct features share one name on the same screen.
findings.suggestion: Change the copy to '{n} active limit order(s)'.

findings.title: ETH balance and TOWELI balance reads are not chain-pinned — on a wrong network the portfolio USD prices the other chain's native token as ETH
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:67 `useBalance({ address })` (no chainId) and lines 81-87 `useReadContract({ address: TOWELI_ADDRESS, ... })` (no chainId), both feeding portfolioUsd at lines 94-106. The codebase's own R047 M1 fix (DashboardPage.tsx:582-594) pins `chainId: CHAIN_ID` for exactly this reason, and useLpPosition/useNFTBoost/useMyLoans all pin CHAIN_ID. A wallet on e.g. Base/Polygon shows that chain's native balance multiplied by mainnet ETH/USD in both the 'ETH Balance' card and the headline Portfolio Value (the wrong-network banner shows, but the number still renders confidently).
findings.suggestion: Add `chainId: CHAIN_ID` to the useBalance and toweliBalance reads, matching the R047 M1 pattern used 500 lines below.

findings.title: Portfolio Value silently drops all ETH-denominated legs when the Chainlink oracle is stale, with no indicator on the headline number
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:96-106: `(price.oracleStale ? 0 : ethBal * price.ethUsd)` and the lpUsd WETH leg `(price.oracleStale ? 0 : lpPos.wethAmount * price.ethUsd)` — when oracleStale flips true (useToweliPrice.ts:153-167, >5min stale or out-of-bounds), the headline Portfolio Value loses the entire ETH + WETH value with zero visual cue on that number; only the small TOWELI Price sub-label shows a 'Stale' chip (line 251), and only when priceChangeStr is empty. A user mid-session sees their portfolio 'drop' by their full ETH balance.
findings.suggestion: When oracleStale, show a stale badge next to the Portfolio Value counter (additive) rather than silently zeroing components, or keep the last-good ethUsd with the stale flag.

findings.title: Loans tab flashes the 'No outstanding loans' empty state while loans are still loading — isLoading is exposed but unused
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:513 `{myLoans.loans.length > 0 ? <OutstandingLoans .../> : <empty state>}` — useMyLoans returns `isLoading: tokenLoading || nftLoading` (useMyLoans.ts:230) and the chunked scan can take seconds (loanCount × getLoan reads in chunks of 50, lines 88-116), but the page never checks it. Users with loans see 'No outstanding loans' + borrow CTAs for the duration of the scan.
findings.suggestion: Gate on myLoans.isLoading with a Skeleton card before falling through to the empty state.

findings.title: Claim success never refetches the position — Claimable stays stale up to 30s and the claim button is immediately re-clickable
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:118-124 fires only a toast on `farmActions.isSuccess`; `pos.refetchAll` (useUserPosition.ts:66-68) exists but is never wired to claim success. useUserPosition refreshes on a 30s interval (line 25/42), so after 'Rewards claimed successfully!' the 'Claimable' card and the `Claim Rewards (X TOWELI)` button (lines 359-369, still rendered because pendingTotal is stale ≥0.01) show the pre-claim amount for up to 30s; a second click sends a getReward tx for ~0 rewards. Same pattern for ETHRevenueClaim (lines 606-611): toast fires but the pendingETH read relies on the shared 15s poller to catch up while the 'Claim ETH' button re-enables.
findings.suggestion: Call pos.refetchAll() (and a pendingETH refetch) inside the success effects, mirroring useRevenueStats.ts:92-104 which already does `refetch()` on isSuccess.

findings.title: Disconnected view hides everything, including wallet-independent content (price chart, TOWELI price, sparkline)
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:146-169: `if (!isConnected) return <Connect Wallet hero>` — PriceChart, TOWELI price card, sparkline, and the GeckoTerminal data all require no wallet, yet none render. Zapper/DeBank/Dexscreener-grade dashboards show market data pre-connect and use it as the connect hook.
findings.suggestion: Additively render the Price Chart + price stat card under the connect CTA (keeping the existing art hero untouched).

findings.title: POL Accumulator 'Coming Soon' card is now dead code — the contract is deployed, so the gate hides it forever and nothing live replaced it
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:372 `{!isDeployed(POL_ACCUMULATOR_ADDRESS) && (...Coming Soon card...)}` vs constants.ts:23 `export const POL_ACCUMULATOR_ADDRESS = '0x2A5f65f4C74b1e49e77aE9A57e20fBDb0cED11D2'` (RELAUNCH 2026-06-06 DeployMVP). isDeployed() is a zero-address check (constants.ts:112-114), so the condition is permanently false: the card (and its idx=8 art slot) can never render, and there is no live POL stats widget in its place.
findings.suggestion: Replace the gate's false branch with a live POL widget (accumulated LP, last buy) when deployed — keeping the Coming Soon card for the undeployed case.

findings.title: 'ETH owed' shows principal only (no accrued interest) and uses raw formatEther with unbounded decimals
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:647 `const owed = borrower.reduce((acc, l) => acc + l.principal, 0n);` rendered at line 677 as `{formatEther(owed)} ETH owed` — the actual repayment is principal + APR-accrued interest (aprBps is displayed per-row at line 742 but never accrued into the totals). Also `formatEther` returns full 18-decimal strings ('0.123456789012345678 ETH') at lines 677, 682, 741 instead of the project's formatWei/formatTokenAmount helpers.
findings.suggestion: Accrue interest (principal * aprBps * elapsed / year / 10000) into the owed figure or relabel to 'principal', and run amounts through formatWei(…, 18, 4).

findings.title: 'Claimable' card's skeleton is gated on price loading, not position loading
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:217: `{ l: 'Claimable', numVal: pendingTotal, ..., loading: !price.isLoaded }` — pendingTotal comes from useUserPosition (a wagmi read), not the price feed. If the price loads first the card shows '0.00' while the position is still fetching; if the price feed never loads (priceUnavailable) the card shows a skeleton forever even though the TOWELI amount is known.
findings.suggestion: Gate on pos.isLoading for the value and keep price.isLoaded only for the USD sub-line.

findings.title: ETHRevenueClaim's error indicator is unreachable dead code — a failed pendingETH read renders null instead of an error
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:613 `if (pending > 0)` wraps the whole card; on a read error `pendingETH` is undefined → `pending = 0` (line 600) → the component returns null at line 640, so the `{pendingError && <span ... title="Failed to load" />}` dot at lines 624-626 can never render. RPC failure is indistinguishable from 'nothing to claim'.
findings.suggestion: Render a small error row when `pendingError && !pending` so claimable ETH can't silently vanish behind an RPC failure.

findings.title: useTegridyScore scans Staked logs from block 18,000,000 — three years before the 2026-06-06 relaunch deploy
findings.evidence: useTegridyScore.ts:326-328: `// Start from approximate contract deploy block to avoid scanning entire chain history` / `fromBlock: 18000000n` — block 18M is ~Sep 2023; TEGRIDY_STAKING_ADDRESS was deployed 2026-06-06 (constants.ts relaunch comments). The ~5M-block eth_getLogs range is exactly the 'wide range public RPCs reject' the catch block at lines 338-343 warns about, silently zeroing the loyalty score (10% weight) for most users.
findings.suggestion: Pin fromBlock to the actual June-2026 deploy block.

findings.title: PriceContext memo dep list omits twapPriceInEth / twapOverrideActive / priceSafeForSwaps — consumers can read stale TWAP/swap-safety flags
findings.evidence: PriceContext.tsx:15-29: `useMemo(() => price, [price.priceInEth, price.priceInUsd, price.ethUsd, price.isLoaded, price.oracleStale, price.priceChange, price.priceUnavailable, price.displayPriceStale, price.apiPriceDiscrepant, price.priceDiscrepancy])` — useToweliPrice also returns `twapPriceInEth`, `twapOverrideActive`, `priceSafeForSwaps` (useToweliPrice.ts:276-279). When only those flip (e.g. TWAP starts overriding spot while priceInUsd lands on the same value via the API fallback path), the memo returns the previous object and every consumer keeps the stale flags. Dashboard itself doesn't read them, but it consumes this provider and swap surfaces do.
findings.suggestion: Add the three missing fields to the dep array.

findings.title: Tabs implement role attributes but not the ARIA tabs pattern: no aria-controls/id pairing, no arrow-key navigation, tabpanels not focusable
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:265-288: buttons have `role="tab"` + `aria-selected` and panels have `role="tabpanel"` + `aria-label`, but there is no `id`/`aria-controls` linkage, no `tabIndex={-1}` roving focus or ArrowLeft/ArrowRight handling on the tablist, and panels lack `tabIndex={0}`. Screen-reader/keyboard users get the announcement but not the interaction model the roles promise.
findings.suggestion: Wire id/aria-controls pairs, add onKeyDown arrow-key roving focus, and tabIndex={0} on the active panel.

findings.title: LoanRow countdown bottoms out at 'Due in 0h' and stays there once the deadline passes (status never flips to overdue while mounted)
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:715-720: `const remaining = Number(loan.deadline) - nowSec; ... const countdown = loan.status === 'overdue' ? 'Overdue' : days > 0 ? `${days}d ${hours}h` : `${hours}h`;` — for 0 < remaining < 3600 this renders '0h', and once remaining goes negative it still renders '0h' under the 'Due in' label because loan.status comes from the frozen useMyLoans memo (see the high-severity refresh finding). The per-row minute tick (lines 710-714) updates the number but not the status.
findings.suggestion: Derive overdue locally from `remaining <= 0` in LoanRow (defense in depth even after fixing useMyLoans), and show minutes below 1h.

findings.title: Two ~550-line executor hooks (with 15s/30s pollers, getAmountsOut RPC loops, BroadcastChannel plumbing) are mounted only to render two badge counts
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:72-73 `const dca = useDCA(); const limitOrders = useLimitOrders();` — the page consumes only `dca.dueSchedules.length` (line 309) and `limitOrders.activeOrders.length` (line 326). useLimitOrders fires a getAmountsOut read per active order every 15s (useLimitOrders.ts:441-513) from the dashboard in addition to the swap page.
findings.suggestion: Extract a read-only `useDCASummary`/`useLimitOrderSummary` that parses the same localStorage payloads without pollers or writeContract.

findings.title: No empty state when there is nothing to claim, and unsettledRewards is invisible on the dashboard
findings.evidence: DashboardPage.tsx:537-573: with pendingTotal < 0.01 and pendingETH = 0, the Rewards tab renders only the ReferralWidget — no 'nothing to claim right now' framing. useUserPosition exposes `unsettledRewards`/`unsettledFormatted` (useUserPosition.ts:89-90) and useFarmActions exposes `claimUnsettled` (line 199), but they're only surfaced on the Farm page (StakingCard.tsx:217-224); a user with unsettled rewards sees an empty-looking Rewards tab here.
findings.suggestion: Add a friendly all-claimed empty card plus an Unsettled Rewards row (amount + Claim Unsettled) when pos.unsettledRewards > 0n.

findings.title: pendingETH is polled via three differently-shaped queries; only two dedupe
findings.evidence: useFarmActions.ts:16-23 (useReadContract pendingETH, 15s, chainId pinned), DashboardPage.tsx:588-595 (useReadContract pendingETH, chainId pinned — same queryKey, dedupes), but useRevenueStats.ts:28 fetches pendingETH inside a useReadContracts multicall batch (30s, no chainId pin) — a separate cache entry, so the same value is fetched on two independent schedules, and the batch isn't chain-pinned unlike its siblings.
findings.suggestion: Pin chainId on the useRevenueStats batch and consider sourcing ETHRevenueClaim from useRevenueStats.pendingRevenueBig instead of a third read.

findings.title: Hardcoded #22c55e stat colors, no-op hover classes, and a near-invisible 'On-chain verified' label
