findings.page: Cancel order — BidManager / MyListings / MyCollection / OrderBookPanel (api-offers.js)
findings.title: Seaport cancel() ABI encodes totalOriginalConsiderationItems into the counter slot — cancels a phantom order; the real listing/bid stays live and fillable while UI reports success
findings.evidence: Four copies of the same broken ABI end the OrderComponents tuple with `uint256 totalOriginalConsiderationItems` instead of `uint256 counter`: api-offers.js:668 (cancelOrder), BidManager.jsx:279 (cancelBid), MyListings.jsx:353, OrderBookPanel.jsx:66 — e.g. "function cancel(tuple(... bytes32 conduitKey, uint256 totalOriginalConsiderationItems)[] orders)". Seaport's cancel() takes OrderComponents whose last field is the signer's counter and derives the order hash from it. ethers v6 encodes object values for named tuple components BY NAME, so `seaport.cancel([params])` (api-offers.js:675, BidManager.jsx:286, MyListings.jsx:356, OrderBookPanel.jsx:69) pulls params.totalOriginalConsiderationItems (2 or 3) into the counter slot — params.counter (OpenSea orders) is ignored, and native-order params (built in orderbook.js:271-313) have no counter at all. With a real counter of 0, the derived hash never matches the signed order; the cancel tx mines successfully (gas burned, OrderCancelled emitted for a phantom hash), the UI optimistically removes the row and toasts 'cancelled successfully' (BidManager.jsx:442-444, MyListings.jsx:389-390), but the WETH bid / listing remains 100% fillable. Observable symptom: the 'cancelled' bid reappears on the next 30s refresh. The repo already contains the correct pattern — trades.js:955-972 cancelTradeOnChain uses `uint256 counter` in the ABI and fetches the live `getCounter(address)` before encoding.
findings.suggestion: Replace the four broken cancel paths with the trades.js cancelTradeOnChain pattern: ABI tuple ending in `uint256 counter`, fetch `getCounter(offerer)` live, and build the components object explicitly. Add a regression test asserting the derived hash equals order_hash/seaportOrderHash before sending. Until fixed, every 'Cancel' button in BidManager/MyListings/MyCollection/OrderBookPanel is a silent no-op that costs gas.

findings.title: Rejecting the post-success backend-notify signature makes a CONFIRMED on-chain trade/purchase report as 'cancelled' (and ShoppingCart keeps the bought item)
findings.evidence: After fulfillOrder confirms, the code prompts a second wallet signMessage to notify the backend, OUTSIDE any local try/catch: trades.js:602 `const fillSignature = await signer.signMessage(fillMessage);` (acceptTrade), trades.js:889 (acceptOpenTrade), orderbook.js:178 (fulfillNativeOrder). If the user rejects this informational prompt, the outer catch maps it to rejection — trades.js:618-619 returns `{ error: "rejected", message: "Trade cancelled by user" }`, orderbook.js:215-216 returns "Transaction cancelled by user" — even though the swap/purchase already settled on-chain. Consumers then mislead: TradeCard.run silences 'rejected' and never refreshes (TradesPanel.jsx:217-222), ShoppingCart breaks the sweep loop and leaves the now-OWNED item in the cart (ShoppingCart.jsx:264-266), and recordTransaction is never called.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the notify signMessage in its own try/catch that swallows rejection and still returns `{ success: true, hash }` (the backend already self-heals via the pre-flight getOrderStatus check). Better: drop the second prompt entirely by letting the server verify the fill from the tx receipt/OrderFulfilled event, as the code comments already contemplate.

findings.title: Bundle listing is a fake flow — no order is created, but the user gets a success-style toast and fee breakdown
findings.evidence: BundleListing.jsx:108-122 handleSubmit: `await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 600)); addToast("Bundle listing submitted! Your NFTs will be listed as a package.", "info"); onListingCreated?.(); onClose();` — no wallet interaction, no Seaport order, no API call. The modal shows price input, duration selector, platform-fee breakdown and 'You Receive' (lines 296-335) for a listing that never exists. This directly contradicts the project's honesty-pass mandate (commit 7639fdf 'honesty pass across every promise surface').
findings.suggestion: Either wire it to a real Seaport bundle order (one order with N ERC-721 offer items — createNativeListing already has every building block) or gate the button behind a 'Coming soon' state. Do not ship a simulated success toast on a money surface.

findings.title: Sniper '+ Cart' adds raw listing objects (no id/name/image) — items render blank, dedupe collides on undefined, and the sweep ALWAYS skips them as 'no longer listed'
findings.evidence: RaritySniper.jsx:333 `onAddToCart?.(item.listing)` passes the raw fetchListings shape ({tokenId, price, orderHash…}, no `id`) — App.jsx:662-666 confirms `listings={listings}` (raw) and `onAddToCart={addToCart}`. CartContext.jsx:24 dedupes on `String(n.id)` so a second sniper-add silently no-ops ("undefined" === "undefined") and removeFromCart(undefined) removes every sniper item at once. ShoppingCart then can never match them: ShoppingCart.jsx:40 and :242 `listings.find(l => String(l.tokenId) === String(item.id))` never matches (item.id undefined) → staleItems always flags them and handleConfirmSweep hits `if (!currentListing) { addToast("…no longer listed — skipping"); onRemove(item.id); }` (ShoppingCart.jsx:243-247) — sniper-added items are unbuyable by construction. Contrast: Listings.jsx builds enriched `listedNfts` with id/name/image before any cart/sweep use (Listings.jsx:156-191).
findings.suggestion: In RaritySniper, add `{...item.listing, id: item.tokenId, name: item.token.name, image: item.token.image}` (it already has `item.token`), or normalize inside addToCart to key on tokenId.

findings.title: Typing exponential notation ('1e-8', '2e3') into the offer price crashes the render via BigInt()
findings.evidence: MakeOfferModal.jsx:290-292 (and again 308-310): `const [whole = "0", frac = ""] = price.split("."); const priceWei = BigInt(whole) * BigInt(1e18) + …` — type="number" inputs accept 'e' notation, so price="1e-8" passes the `parseFloat(price) > 0` guard but `BigInt("1e-8")` throws a SyntaxError inside the render IIFE, crashing the modal (caught only by the route error boundary).
findings.suggestion: Use viem's parseEther inside a try/catch (already imported in api-offers.js) or sanitize with a decimal regex before the BigInt math; reject 'e/E' in onChange like the trade window inputs should too.

findings.title: 'Trait Floor' pricing strategy is dead code — attr.traitFloor is never populated, so it silently prices everything at collection floor
findings.evidence: BulkListingWizard.jsx:138 and :501 `const tf = attr.traitFloor || 0;` — repo-wide grep shows no code ever sets `traitFloor` on token attributes (Deals.jsx and TraitExplorer.jsx compute their own separate maps). normalizeToken (api.js:114-120) maps attributes to {key, value} only. Result: a seller choosing 'Price each by highest trait floor' (PRICING_MODES desc, line 23) gets `base = maxTraitFloor > 0 ? maxTraitFloor : floor` → always floor — rare NFTs are listed at floor price with no warning.
findings.suggestion: Feed the wizard the trait-floor map Deals.jsx already computes from live listings (Deals.jsx:479-505), or disable the mode with an explanatory tooltip until wired.

findings.title: Ladder pricing gives the RAREST NFT the START price — with the suggested placeholders (0.10 → 0.50) the rarest item lists cheapest
findings.evidence: BulkListingWizard.jsx:148-152 (dup at 510-514): `const sorted = [...selectedNfts].sort((a,b) => (a.rank||99999)-(b.rank||99999));` then `price = start + ((end - start) * i) / (count - 1)` — i=0 is the rarest (rank 1) and receives `start`. Input placeholders are START '0.10' and END '0.50' (lines 241, 258), so following the UI's own example prices the rarest token at 0.10 and the most common at 0.50 — inverted from the 'Distribute prices by rarity' expectation.
findings.suggestion: Either reverse the assignment (rarest gets END/highest) or relabel inputs explicitly ('Rarest item price' / 'Most common item price') and swap the placeholders. Show the resulting min/max next to the rarest/commonest thumbnails in the table for confirmation.

findings.title: Gas estimate hardcodes 30 gwei — 'EST. GAS' is ~30-300× too high at current ~0.1-1 gwei basefees
findings.evidence: SweepCalculator.jsx:13-16 `function estimateGas(count, gasPriceGwei = 30)` is only ever called as `estimateGas(effectiveCount)` (lines 224, 234) — never with a live gas price. ShoppingCart fetches live feeData (ShoppingCart.jsx:111-118) but its fallback uses the same stale `0.0045 // ~150k gas * 30 gwei` constant (line 104). This is the same class of stale-gas display the project already diagnosed in the swap-gas investigation (project_2026_06_07_swap_gas_diagnosis).
findings.suggestion: Reuse ShoppingCart's provider.getFeeData() path (or a cached eth_gasPrice via the Alchemy proxy) and fall back to a clearly-labeled 'rough estimate' only when no provider exists.

findings.title: Bid-side cumulative depth accumulates in ascending price order — inverted bid-depth curve that contradicts the other depth chart on the same page
findings.evidence: DepthChart.jsx:28-31 bucketPrices accumulates `cum` over buckets built low→high price for BOTH sides; bid depth should be 'bids at or above price' (cumulative grows as price falls). OrderBookPanel's embedded chart does it correctly: OrderBookPanel.jsx:415 `bucketize(bidPrices, 8).reverse()` then accumulates (lines 419-420), so the highest bid has the smallest cumulative. Listings.jsx renders BOTH (line 485 OrderBookPanel, line 488 standalone DepthChart) — the two visualizations disagree about the same bids.
findings.suggestion: In DepthChart.jsx, accumulate bid buckets from highest price down (mirror OrderBookPanel.jsx:415-420), and consider extracting one shared bucketize/cumulate helper so the two charts can't drift again.

findings.title: Collection/trait offer prices likely show the offer's TOTAL value, not per-item — quantity is fetched but never used
findings.evidence: api-offers.js:115-122 maps `price: safePriceFromWei(o.price.value)` and explicitly captures `quantity: o.protocol_data?.parameters?.offer?.[0]?.startAmount || "1"`, but no consumer divides by it: CollectionOffersPanel.jsx:96/114 renders offer.price directly as 'BEST COLLECTION OFFER', deriveTraitOffers (api-offers.js:138-148) compares raw o.price. For a 10-unit criteria offer of 1 WETH total, the panel would advertise a 1.0 WETH best offer when the per-item bid is 0.1. UNVERIFIED HYPOTHESIS regarding OpenSea's price.value semantics for multi-quantity criteria offers — verify against a live multi-quantity offer before patching.
findings.suggestion: Confirm semantics against the OpenSea API, then display `price / Number(quantity)` with a 'xN' badge like OpenSea's own offers table.

findings.title: Expired/cancelled/finalized offers are not filtered out and show live Accept buttons
findings.evidence: BidManager.jsx:368-375 maps fetchTokenOffers results straight into receivedOffers; fetchTokenOffers (api-offers.js:74-87) returns normalizeOffer objects including `cancelled`/`finalized`/`expiry` but applies no filter. Contrast OfferPanel.jsx:135-139 which filters `o.expiry … ms > Date.now()` before rendering. Accepting a dead offer walks into setApprovalForAll + a fulfillment_data error ('Could not get fulfillment data').
findings.suggestion: Apply the same `!o.cancelled && !o.finalized && !expired` filter OfferPanel uses, and show timeLeft coloring (expiryColor already exists in the file).

findings.title: API failure renders as 'No active trades' — fetch error is silently discarded
findings.evidence: TradesPanel.jsx:414 `const { trades: rows } = await fetchTrades({ wallet, role: direction, status: statusFilter });` — fetchTrades returns `{ trades: [], error }` on non-OK/network failure (trades.js:422-426) but `error` is never read; the panel then shows the 'No … trades' empty state (TradesPanel.jsx:502-511). During an /api/orderbook outage a user with live incoming trades sees an empty inbox with no retry affordance — exactly the misleading-emptiness pattern the 2026-06-09 magnetism review flagged.
findings.suggestion: Capture the error and render the error-banner + Retry pattern MyCollection uses (MyCollection.jsx:362-367) instead of the empty state.

findings.title: Sweeps are N sequential wallet transactions — no Seaport batch fill and no reuse of the existing EIP-5792 atomic-batch helper
findings.evidence: ShoppingCart.jsx:237-258 and SweepCalculator.jsx:288-293 loop `await fulfillNativeOrder(...) / fulfillSeaportOrder(...)` once per item — one wallet confirmation and one base-tx gas overhead per NFT. Seaport natively supports fulfillAvailableAdvancedOrders (already allowlisted in SEAPORT_FULFILLMENT_FUNCTIONS, api.js:13-14), and trades.js:120-168 already implements tryAtomicBatch (wallet_sendCalls) used by acceptTrade — neither is used for sweeps.
findings.suggestion: Batch native+OpenSea fills into one fulfillAvailableAdvancedOrders call (skip-on-fail semantics built into Seaport), or at minimum wrap the sequential calls in tryAtomicBatch for 5792 wallets. This is the single biggest UX/gas gap vs Blur/Gem.

findings.title: Polling storm: ~21 OpenSea proxy calls every 30 seconds, bypassing the app's own React Query rate-limit policy
findings.evidence: fetchReceivedOffers (BidManager.jsx:355-382) calls fetchWalletNfts then fetchTokenOffers for 20 tokens in parallel, and the interval re-runs it every 30s (BidManager.jsx:428-432 REFRESH_INTERVAL = 30_000). queryConfig.js:47-52 documents that 30s 'was too aggressive for rate-limited API' and sets offers staleTime to 2 minutes — BidManager ignores that layer entirely (raw openseaGet, no cache).
findings.suggestion: Move these fetches into React Query with the offersQuery config (shared cache with OfferPanel), or lengthen the interval and skip refetch when document.hidden (TradesPanel already does the hidden check, line 424).

findings.title: 'Fair Value' / 'Total Savings' methodology is gameable by a single outlier ask — no sample-size or sanity guard on trait floors
findings.evidence: Deals.jsx:479-505 builds per-trait floors from the two lowest ASKS sharing the trait, and discount = (maxTraitFloor - price)/maxTraitFloor (line 572). For a sparse trait with only one other listing, that one ask IS the 'fair value' — anyone listing a rare-trait token at 100 ETH makes every other listing with that trait a '90%+ deal'. The header even labels the column 'Fair Value' (line 901) and sums `maxTraitFloor - price` as 'Total Savings' (line 682). Asks-only, no sales data, no minimum cohort.
findings.suggestion: Additive guardrails: require ≥3 listings per trait before a trait floor counts, cap maxTraitFloor at e.g. 5× collection floor (valuation.js already caps at 5× for the same reason), and blend recent sales (fetchTokenSalesHistory exists). Label the column 'Trait floor' instead of 'Fair Value'.

findings.title: Snipe score saturates at 999 and is dominated by price index near the floor — ordering is barely rarity-driven where it matters
findings.evidence: RaritySniper.jsx:10-14: `priceScore = Math.max(0.01, pricePercentile)` floors the cheapest listing at 0.01, so score = rarityScore/0.01*10 = rarity×1000, capped `Math.min(…, 999)` — any token rarer than ~the bottom 0.1% pins at 999 when it's among the cheapest, and ties are broken arbitrarily. The 'deal score' is thus not defensible as a ranking near the floor.
findings.suggestion: Score = actual price vs expected price for that rank (residual from the rank-price regression Deals' ScatterPlot already computes, Deals.jsx:298-316). Keep the current score as a fallback when fewer than ~10 listings exist.

findings.title: 30-second poll resets the panel to skeletons every cycle and successful accepts surface generic errors / stale lists
findings.evidence: OfferPanel.jsx:15-27: every interval tick calls `setLoading(true)` then replaces state, so `{loading ? skeleton : …}` (line 121) flashes skeletons over real offers every 30s. handleAccept discards the specific failure reason — line 48 `addToast?.("Failed to accept offer. Please try again.", "error")` while acceptOffer returns precise messages ('Could not get fulfillment data', 'Unexpected transaction target — aborting for safety', api-offers.js:732/745/753); success doesn't trigger an immediate refetch (accepted offer lingers until next poll).
findings.suggestion: Keep previous data while refetching (only show skeletons when offers.length===0), pass result.message through getFriendlyError, and call load() after a successful accept.

findings.title: Wallet inventory is silently truncated at 100 NFTs (no pagination) across every trade/list surface
findings.evidence: fetchWalletNfts (api.js:598-614) requests `pageSize: "100"` and never follows a pageKey. TradeWindow.loadInventory (137-151), OpenTradeAccept (TradesPanel.jsx:75-91), MyCollection (98-108, while displaying full `totalCount` at line 209), and BidManager.fetchReceivedOffers (359) all consume it. A 150-NFT whale cannot offer/select/list 50 of their tokens and gets no notice.
findings.suggestion: Loop pageKey until exhausted (cap ~500 like MAX_MY_PAGES) or show 'showing first 100 of N' with a load-more control when totalCount > tokens.length.

findings.title: Pre-flight order validation is inconsistent: cart validates (3 layers), sweep and deals buys do not
findings.evidence: ShoppingCart runs validateOrderFillability on every item and auto-removes red ones before confirming (ShoppingCart.jsx:132-187). SweepCalculator.handleSweep (266-315) and Deals.handleBuy (640-674) call fulfill* directly with no Layer-1/2/3 checks — stale/cancelled listings reach the wallet and fail with a revert mid-sweep (SweepCalculator stops the whole sweep on first generic failure, line 304-307).
findings.suggestion: Run validateOrderQuick over the sweep list first (it's cheap and already written), drop reds with a toast, and in SweepCalculator continue past per-item failures the way ShoppingCart does instead of break-ing.

findings.title: 'Save 0.5% vs OpenSea' badge markets a fee discount built on an assumed ~0.5% royalty — contradicts the standing 'don't market a fee discount' decision
findings.evidence: OrderBookPanel.jsx:16 `const OPENSEA_FEE_PCT = 1.5; // OS 1% + ~0.5% avg creator royalty` and line 208 renders `Save {savingsPerEth}% vs OpenSea`. Project memory (2026-06-09 Tradermigos) records 'OpenSea fee is 1% now (don't market a fee discount)'. The comparison also omits that native fills pay NO creator royalty (createNativeListing consideration is seller+platform only, orderbook.js:281-298) — a material disclosure for royalty-respecting collections.
findings.suggestion: Reframe additively as 'flat 1% — fees fund the Tegridy treasury' (the framing orderbook.js:4-6 already prescribes) and disclose that creator royalties are not collected on native fills.

findings.title: Stale comment still claims 'vs OpenSea 2.5%'
findings.evidence: orderbook.js:227 `// List an NFT on our orderbook at 1% fee (vs OpenSea 2.5%)` — contradicts the corrected header at orderbook.js:4-6 ('OpenSea has charged ~1% since Sep 2025 — don't market this as a fee discount') and constants.js:143-144 (OPENSEA_FEE_BPS = 100).
findings.suggestion: Fix the comment so the next copy-paste doesn't resurrect the 2.5% claim in UI copy.

findings.title: Empty-state copy promises offers and bids, but only purchases are ever recorded
findings.evidence: TransactionHistory.jsx:103 'Purchases, offers, and bids you make for this collection will appear here.' — every recordTransaction caller uses type:"buy" only (Listings.jsx:324, Modal.jsx:435, OrderBookPanel.jsx:146, SweepCalculator.jsx:297, ShoppingCart.jsx:261, Deals.jsx:657). TYPE_LABELS for offer/bid/list/cancel (lines 38-42) are dead.
findings.suggestion: Record 'list' in createNativeListing/BulkListingWizard success, 'offer/bid' in MakeOfferModal success, 'cancel' in the cancel paths — or soften the copy to 'Purchases you make…'.

findings.title: Board tab's empty state shows inbox/outbox copy ('Trades you send will appear here…') instead of board copy
findings.evidence: TradesPanel.jsx:506-510: the empty-state ternary only branches on `direction === "incoming"`, so direction "board" falls into the outgoing text 'Trades you send will appear here. Start one with "New trade offer".' — wrong call-to-action for the public board (should point at '+ Post to board'). Also the status filter (line 490) lacks an 'expired' option though STATUS_COLOR styles it (line 198).
findings.suggestion: Add a board branch ('Open trades anyone can accept will appear here — post the first one') and an 'expired' filter option.

findings.title: Retry wrapper shares one 15s AbortController across attempts and clears the timeout after attempt 1 — later retries have no timeout (or get pre-aborted)
findings.evidence: orderbook.js:40-51: `const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 15000)` is created once outside withRetry; `clearTimeout(timeout)` runs inside the first attempt after fetch resolves (line 45) even when `!res.ok` throws to trigger a retry — retries 2-3 then run with no timeout, and if the first attempt itself hung >15s the shared controller aborts all subsequent retries immediately.
findings.suggestion: Create the controller+timeout inside the retried function (the pattern postOrderbook in trades.js:46-70 already gets right).

findings.title: My Bids fetch is unpaginated (default page size) while the overcommitment math elsewhere paginates — heavy bidders see a truncated list
findings.evidence: BidManager.jsx:336-341 calls openseaGet('orders/ethereum/seaport/offers', {maker, …}) once with no limit/cursor handling; api-offers.js fetchMyOffers (557-594) paginates up to 500 with `MAX_MY_PAGES`. A user with >20-50 open bids manages only the first page from the Bid Manager.
findings.suggestion: Reuse fetchMyOffers (it already normalizes + filters expiry) instead of the bespoke fetch in BidManager.

findings.title: Cancel All signs one backend message per listing after the single incrementCounter tx — N sequential wallet popups
findings.evidence: MyListings.jsx:430-451: after `seaport.incrementCounter()` the loop does `await signer.signMessage(cancelMessage)` + POST per listing. 15 listings = 15 surprise signature prompts; a rejection mid-loop leaves the DB half-synced (rows stay 'active' though on-chain dead).
findings.suggestion: One signed message covering all orderHashes (server verifies the list), or have the server watch the CounterIncremented event and bulk-expire rows without client signatures.

findings.title: Bulk listing = 2 wallet prompts per NFT with no upfront warning, and Escape closes the progress UI mid-flight
findings.evidence: Each createNativeListing performs an EIP-712 sign + an auth signMessage (orderbook.js:323, 351) — 10 NFTs ≈ 20+ prompts, never disclosed in the review step. The Escape handler (BulkListingWizard.jsx:538-539) calls onClose() without checking `submitting` (backdrop and ✕ button do check, lines 641/655), so Esc during submission hides the progress bar while the loop keeps firing toasts.
findings.suggestion: Add 'you will be asked to sign ~2N times' to StepReview, gate Escape on !submitting, and consider folding the auth message into the EIP-712 payload server-side to halve prompts.

findings.title: 'Counter' doesn't counter — it just opens the token detail modal
findings.evidence: BidManager.jsx:474-478 handleCounter: `const token = resolveToken(offer.tokenId); if (token && onPick) onPick(token);` — no prefilled counter-offer amount, no link to the received offer; if the token isn't in the loaded map it does nothing at all (silent no-op). TradesPanel has a real counter flow with prefilled sides (TradesPanel.jsx:430-435) — inconsistent affordance.
findings.suggestion: Open MakeOfferModal prefilled (or a relist-at-price dialog) and disable the button with a tooltip when resolveToken fails.

findings.title: The polished tx-progress overlay is wired into just 1 of 5 buy surfaces; speed-up failures are silent; approve step never activates
findings.evidence: Only Modal.jsx uses it (Modal.jsx:127, 652) — ShoppingCart/SweepCalculator/Deals/OrderBookPanel buys are toast-only. handleSpeedUp swallows errors with console.warn (TransactionProgress.jsx:623-625) so a wallet that refuses custom-nonce replacement gives zero feedback. The APPROVE step is marked COMPLETED whenever phase==='signing' (lines 734-737) — it never shows an active 'approving…' state even when approval is actually running inside onExecute. Note also fulfill* helpers internally `tx.wait()` before returning, so the overlay's 'Pending' phase starts after confirmation — PendingMonitor resolves instantly, making the stepper's pending estimate cosmetic.
findings.suggestion: Adopt the overlay for cart/sweep/deals/orderbook buys (it accepts an onExecute), toast on speed-up failure, and have onExecute resolve at broadcast (return the tx, let PendingMonitor own confirmation) so the pending phase is real.

findings.title: Fixed two-column grid has no mobile breakpoint
findings.evidence: CollectionOffersPanel.jsx:77 `display: "grid", gridTemplateColumns: "1fr 1fr"` with no media query or auto-fit — at iPhone widths each column is ~150px and trait rows ('Shirt/Jacket: Hoodie Orange … 3 offers … Ξ0.1234') wrap awkwardly. Project requirement: flawless on iPhone 14+ (project_responsive).
findings.suggestion: Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr))` so the columns stack on narrow viewports.

findings.title: Canvas/SVG market visualizations are mouse-only — no keyboard or screen-reader path to the data
findings.evidence: Deals.jsx ScatterPlot canvas (390-395) exposes points only via mousemove/click; DepthChart.jsx tooltip only via onMouseMove (263). Neither has role/aria-label/focusable fallbacks or a data-table alternative. (Contrast: TradeWindow tiles correctly use role=checkbox + tabIndex + keydown, TradeWindow.jsx:52-55 — the pattern exists in-repo.)
findings.suggestion: Add aria-label summaries (the DepthChart auto-summary text already exists — link it via aria-describedby) and a visually-hidden table of deal points.

findings.title: Floor-distance is printed twice per row in two formats
findings.evidence: MyListings.jsx:603-605 renders `+12.3% from floor` in cardMeta and lines 612-616 render `12% above floor` again in the row below, computed two different ways (toFixed(1) vs Math.round) — same fact, two numbers that can disagree after rounding.
findings.suggestion: Keep one (the health badge already encodes the same signal) and let the second row show something additive, e.g. expiry date.

findings.title: 'Click to refresh view' badge doesn't refresh anything — the table is already live
findings.evidence: Deals.jsx:800-806 onClick only does `setNewDealsCount(0); window.scrollTo(...)` — deals recompute reactively the moment listings change (useMemo at 527), so the copy promises an action that already happened.
findings.suggestion: Copy: 'N new deals — jump to top'. Consider holding new rows out of the table until clicked (true Dexscreener-style pause) if the intent was stability.

findings.title: var(--border) used as card BACKGROUND token
findings.evidence: BidManager.jsx styles.card `background: "var(--border)"` (line 55) and TransactionHistory.jsx:128 `background: "var(--border)", border: "1px solid var(--border)"` — border-color token doubling as surface fill; other panels use var(--surface-glass). Any theme that darkens borders silently changes these cards.
findings.suggestion: Switch to var(--surface-glass)/var(--card) for fills to match TradesPanel cards.

findings.title: Hover styling via onMouseEnter style mutation instead of CSS classes
findings.evidence: ShoppingCart.jsx:407-408, 518-527, 769-770, 789-796 mutate e.currentTarget.style on every hover; these bypass the app's CSS layer (no touch/focus-visible equivalents, no reduced-motion respect) and add re-entrant listeners on a hot list.
findings.suggestion: Move to the existing class-based hover patterns (listing-card-actions et al. in App.css) — also gives keyboard :focus-visible parity for free.

findings.page: ShoppingCart / OfferPanel / Deals / TradesPanel (all money surfaces)
findings.title: No USD values anywhere on the trading surface
findings.evidence: Every price render across the audited files is ETH-only (e.g. ShoppingCart total ShoppingCart.jsx:572-574, OfferPanel best offer 104-106, Deals table 929-937, TradeWindow balance meter 463-476). fetchOpenSeaListings even stubs `priceUsd: null` (api.js:649) and nothing fills it. Blur/OpenSea/Gem show fiat context on every order row.
findings.suggestion: One cached ETH/USD feed (Coingecko via proxy or Chainlink read through the existing Alchemy RPC route) + a small <Usd value={eth}/> helper used beside totals, offer amounts, and trade cash legs.

findings.title: No net-proceeds preview when accepting an offer
findings.evidence: handleAccept (OfferPanel.jsx:31-55, BidManager.jsx:453-472) jumps straight to approval+fulfillment with no 'You will receive X WETH after OpenSea 1% fee (+ royalty)' confirmation — the seller learns their net only from the wallet popup. MyListings/BulkListingWizard DO show revenue-after-fee for listings (MyListings.jsx:619-625), so the pattern exists.
findings.suggestion: Pre-compute net from the offer's consideration items (fees are explicit in protocol_data) and show a one-line confirm before the approval tx.

findings.title: Counterparty input lacks ENS resolution and identity preview — a classic trade-scam vector the rest of the app already has tools for
findings.evidence: TradeWindow.jsx:289-301 accepts only raw 0x addresses (validCounterparty regex line 113-114); hooks/useEns.jsx exists in the codebase but isn't used here. There's no avatar/ENS/holdings preview of who you're about to trade with beyond their NFT grid; lookalike-address scams rely on exactly this.
findings.suggestion: Resolve ENS names in the input (accept 'name.eth'), show reverse-ENS + first-seen/holdings summary chip once an address validates.

findings.title: No deep links, sharing, or export for scanner results
findings.evidence: Deals rows (Deals.jsx:909-1006) and sniper rows (RaritySniper.jsx:484-527) only call onPick(modal) — no per-token URL, no copy-link, no CSV export of the deals table (lib/csv.js exportCSV exists and is already used by MyCollection.jsx:72-84). Dexscreener-grade scanners make every row shareable.
findings.suggestion: Add ?token= deep links (the router exists) and an Export CSV button reusing lib/csv.js.

findings.title: Sweep progress is lost on reload — no pending-state persistence or resume
findings.evidence: Buying state lives only in component state (ShoppingCart.jsx:27-28, progress 237-277). Mid-sweep refresh forgets which items were bought (cart items removed only after each success) and any in-flight tx is orphaned — there's no localStorage pending-tx record despite recordTransaction/localStorage infra existing (lib/transactions.js).
findings.suggestion: Persist {orderHash, txHash, status} per attempt to localStorage and reconcile on mount (PendingMonitor logic in TransactionProgress.jsx:559-599 is reusable for this).

good: Three-layer order validation library (lib/orderValidator.js) — expiry/freshness, batched RPC status+ownership+approval checks, definitive fulfillOrder staticCall simulation with revert-reason parsing — and ShoppingCart actually uses it, auto-removing definitively-invalid items before checkout.

trades.js is the strongest file on the surface: acceptTrade/acceptOpenTrade run a full pre-flight battery (chain guard, Seaport getOrderStatus, LIVE ownerOf re-check of the maker's items — the classic trade-window scam defense), use EIP-5792 wallet_sendCalls atomic batching with correct capability detection, 4001 rethrow so the fallback doesn't re-prompt, and a sequential fallback path.
cancelTradeOnChain (trades.js:955-973) uses the CORRECT Seaport OrderComponents ABI with a live getCounter() read — it is the in-repo template for fixing the four broken cancel paths.

Chain-guarding is comprehensive: assertOnExpectedChain on every offer/cancel/accept entrypoint (api-offers.js M-8 fixes), fulfillSeaportOrder wrong-chain refusal (api.js:996-1007), and isWrongNetwork banners with switchChain CTAs in MakeOfferModal/MyListings/BidManager/BulkListingWizard.

Supply-chain defenses on fulfillment data: tx target pinned to known Seaport 1.5/1.6 addresses AND function-name allowlist (SEAPORT_FULFILLMENT_FUNCTIONS) before encoding calldata from any API response, with ABI-name-based argument mapping to avoid Object.values ordering dependence (api.js:1042-1080, api-offers.js:739-775).
EIP-6963 wallet discovery replacing the spoofable isMetaMask race, with rdns preference order and a non-trusting legacy fallback (api.js:887-940).
WETH hygiene: approval hard-capped at 100 WETH per call, positive-amount asserts, ETH-balance + gas-buffer check before wrap, BigInt-exact formatEth (lib/weth.js).

MakeOfferModal overcommitment warning — sums ALL active offers (paginated fetchMyOffers, up to 500) plus the new offer against WETH+ETH-minus-gas and warns about simultaneous-acceptance risk; balances and auto-wrap messaging are clear.

fulfillNativeOrder pre-flight: client-side expiry rejection plus a Seaport getOrderStatus read before broadcasting, explicitly covering the 'backend missed a fill' stale-row case (orderbook.js:83-113).

createNativeListing is carefully engineered: check-set-reverify approval pattern, canonical TypedDataEncoder struct-hash derivation for the order hash (with the signed-digest vs emitted-hash distinction documented), signature-bound auth message, and the FULL_RESTRICTED/zero-zone footgun fixed and documented (orderbook.js:299-306).

Dutch-leg trade support is correct end-to-end: builder commits max(start,end) funding, fulfillment pays max and relies on Seaport's refund of unused native value, display uses a pure linear-interpolation helper (currentLegAmounts) mirrored from Seaport semantics, with rising/decaying direction arrows in TradeChips.

TradeWindow's prior TDZ crash is fixed (validCounterparty declared at line 113 before its first use in the effect at 154-157); it also ships a lopsided-trade warning (LOPSIDED_RATIO 0.6), a single shared rarity-adjusted valuation formula (lib/valuation.js, capped at 5× floor), and proper modal a11y (focus trap, Escape stopImmediatePropagation, ref-counted scroll lock, role=checkbox tiles with keyboard handlers).

Retry/backoff infrastructure is consistent and abort-aware: ApiError with isRetryable + Retry-After honoring (lib/proxy.js), exponential backoff with jitter, signal-aware sleeps that cancel on unmount (api-offers.js withRetry), and permanent-4xx short-circuit in postOrderbook.
useBuyNft does optimistic cache removal with rollback on error and targeted invalidation via structured query keys; per-data-type cache configs (queryConfig.js) document rate-limit-driven staleTimes.

TransactionProgress is a genuinely polished tx UX component: vertical stepper with states, ref-based pending poller that doesn't restart on re-render, elapsed timer, 2-minute speed-up offer with EIP-1559 20% bump and nonce reuse, celebration tiering with canvas confetti, friendly-error mapping and retry.

ShoppingCart re-verifies price and existence per item immediately before each buy (skips with explicit '#name price changed (a → b)' toasts), branches native-vs-OpenSea fulfillment correctly, and stops the loop on user rejection.

Graceful degradation when sources die: fetchListings runs OpenSea and the native orderbook in parallel with independent .catch (one source failing never blanks the other), NativeListingsTable distinguishes 'orderbook not configured' from transient errors, and Deals shows a slow-upstream notice after 12s instead of an infinite spinner.
Transaction history records lowercase-normalized wallets, caps at 50 entries, validates tx-hash format before linking Etherscan, and refreshes on window focus.
missingVsBestInClass: True single-transaction sweep (Seaport fulfillAvailableAdvancedOrders or EIP-5792 batch) — Blur/Gem fill N items in one confirm; this app does N sequential wallet transactions in both ShoppingCart and SweepCalculator.
USD values beside every ETH amount (cart totals, offers, deals, trade cash legs) — priceUsd is stubbed null and never populated.
Net-proceeds preview when accepting an offer (price minus 1% OS fee/royalty) — sellers see net only in the wallet popup.
Floor-relative context on bids ('92% of floor') in offer panels and MakeOfferModal — standard on OpenSea/Blur offer tables.
Pending-transaction persistence/resume across reloads (Blur-style) — sweep and buy state is all in-memory.
Per-row deep links and share/export from Deals and RaritySniper scanners (CSV export helper exists but is only wired to MyCollection).
ENS support in the trade counterparty field plus counterparty identity preview (reverse ENS, holdings) — lookalike-address scam mitigation.
Incoming-trade notification badge in global nav (polling exists only inside the TradesPanel tab; Blur surfaces actionable counts globally).
Surfacing the existing tx-simulation capability as a visible 'Simulated ✓' pre-trade badge on single buys (the staticCall layer exists but is invisible outside the cart).
Royalty/fee transparency table on the native orderbook (explicitly stating creator royalties are not collected on native fills).
Collection-offer quantity display ('0.1 WETH ×10') — quantity is fetched but never shown.
Price-history sparkline / last-sale column in Deals and sniper tables (sales-history API already exists in api.js).

nakamigos/lib/transactions.js + weth.js + valuation.js + errorMessages.js + formatPrice.js + proxy.js + queryConfig.js
nakamigos/api.js (fulfillSeaportOrder, getProvider/EIP-6963, listings merge, retry layer)

components: TradesPanel, TradeWindow (TDZ re-verified), TradeChips, OfferPanel, MakeOfferModal, CollectionOffersPanel, TraitBidPanel, BidManager, ShoppingCart, SweepCalculator, OrderBookPanel, DepthChart, Deals, RaritySniper, BulkListingWizard, BundleListing, MyListings, MyCollection, TransactionProgress, TransactionHistory
