findings.title: Order book is nonsense: best bid 4.52 ETH vs best ask 0.1045, spread -4.4155 ETH (-4225.4%) labeled 'Healthy'
findings.evidence: Expanding ORDER BOOK & OFFERS shows BEST BID 4.5200 / BEST ASK 0.1045, 'Spread -4.4155 (-4225.4%)' with a green 'Healthy' dot and insight copy 'Price gap is narrow (-4225.4%), suggesting healthy trading.' Bid ladder rows are 4.4475/4.3025/4.1575/3.8675... — ~43x the 0.1045 floor. COLLECTION OFFERS panel repeats it: BEST COLLECTION OFFER 4.5200 with a ladder of 4.52/4.49/4.44/4.41 from two addresses. These are almost certainly multi-quantity collection-offer TOTALS not per-item prices (4.52/43 = 0.105 = the real per-item offer, which the cards correctly show as 'Best offer: 0.1020').
findings.suggestion: Normalize collection offers to per-item price (offer total / remaining quantity) before feeding the order book, best-bid card, and offers panel. Add a sanity invariant: if bestBid > bestAsk, treat the book as crossed/dirty and suppress the 'Healthy' verdict. Fix the spread insight logic so negative/absurd spreads never read 'narrow ... healthy trading'.

findings.page: token detail modal (deals + listings) and theater mode
findings.title: NFT image never loads in token detail modal or theater mode — fallback 'N #id' placeholder shown
findings.evidence: Opened #1170 (from deals) and #10219 (from listings): the left image pane stays blank with the small 'N #1170'/'N #10219' fallback card, while the SAME tokens' grid/table thumbnails load fine. Theater mode for #10219 displays a black void with the tiny 'N' fallback. Reproduced on two tokens minutes apart; localhost modal also blank (inconclusive there due to missing env keys — prod is the proof).
findings.suggestion: The modal/theater uses a different (full-res) image source than the grid thumbnails. Point it at the same proxied/cached image used by cards, with the full-res as progressive upgrade and the thumbnail as fallback — never an empty pane.

findings.title: Rarity Sniper is permanently empty: '0/0 opportunities — No Nakamigos listings available' while 786 listings exist; NOT fixed at HEAD
findings.evidence: Prod sniper shows 'No Nakamigos listings available. Waiting for Nakamigos listings to appear. Hit Refresh...'; clicking Refresh changes nothing after 8s+. Meanwhile /listings shows '786 Nakamigos currently listed' and Deals scans dozens of live listings. localhost:5173/nakamigos/nakamigos/sniper (HEAD) shows the identical 0/0 empty state — same bug at HEAD.
findings.suggestion: The sniper appears to only ingest NEW listing events after page load instead of seeding from the existing listing snapshot the Floor page already has. Seed it from the same active-listings store on mount, then stream updates.

findings.title: Connect Wallet modal lists WalletConnect three times and uses identical generic icons for Safe/Base/MetaMask
findings.evidence: Clicking Connect Wallet on /trade: list = Safe, WalletConnect ('QR code · Mobile wallets'), Base Account, MetaMask, WalletConnect, WalletConnect, Phantom — 3 duplicate WalletConnect rows; Safe, Base Account and MetaMask all show the same money-bag emoji icon instead of brand marks.
findings.suggestion: De-duplicate connectors by id when building the list (multiple WC-based connectors are collapsing into identical rows) and wire real wallet brand icons; duplicates plus generic icons read as a phishing red flag on the single most trust-sensitive surface.

findings.title: Trait/rarity analytics computed from only 40 of 20,000 tokens — 'Rarest Traits' is meaningless (every trait = 1, '2.5%*')
findings.evidence: Stat card 'LOADED 40'; Trait Distribution header '40 of 20,000 loaded'; Rarest Traits grid shows 16 traits ALL with count 1 and '2.5% *', footnote '* Percentages based on 40 loaded tokens'. The Deals page on the same visit progressively scanned 3,600+ tokens, so deeper data exists in-app.
findings.suggestion: Share the progressive token-scan cache the Deals page builds (or precompute trait counts server-side once — they are static for a fixed collection) and keep the honest footnote only while genuinely loading.

findings.title: 'Rarity vs Price' chart never renders: 'Need at least 3 listed items with rarity data' despite 786 active listings
findings.evidence: Panel body shows only the message 'Need at least 3 listed items with rarity data to render scatter plot. Load more tokens or wait for listing data.' while the Listing Velocity card on the same page shows ACTIVE LISTINGS 786.
findings.suggestion: Join the listings feed with the rarity ranks already computed for the Deals table (which shows ranks for the same listed tokens) — the data exists, the join is missing.

findings.title: Trend labels contradict their own numbers: 'Whales are ACCUMULATING' at Net +0; 'Accumulation phase' at 1.0:1 buyers/sellers
findings.evidence: Whales page: '↑ Whales are ACCUMULATING — 1 inflows · 1 outflows · Net +0' (green, up arrow). Analytics Buyer vs Seller (24h): '13 buyers vs 13 sellers / 1.0:1' labeled 'Accumulation phase ▲'.
findings.suggestion: Add a NEUTRAL state for net = 0 / ratio = 1 (e.g. 'Balanced flow') and only show ACCUMULATING/DISTRIBUTING beyond a +/- threshold. Right now the page invents a bullish signal from zero data, which undermines the whole intelligence surface.

findings.title: Outlier troll listings (up to ~1650 ETH) destroy every linear price axis: deals scatter, floor-depth histogram, ask ladder
findings.evidence: Deals RARITY vs PRICE Y-axis read 0.12 → 1650.00 ETH with every deal dot squashed onto the bottom line. Sweep panel FLOOR DEPTH axis: '0.10 ... 1500.00 ETH' with all bars crammed in the first ~10%. Order-book ask ladder buckets: '93.8480: 782 asks' then 281/468/656/.../1406.2565 — 782 of 786 asks land in bucket 1, so the ladder carries zero information.
findings.suggestion: Clamp chart domains at p95 of listings (or floor x3) with a '+N outliers' annotation, or use a log scale. One 1650 ETH listing currently blinds four separate visualizations.

findings.title: Stale fee claim 'Save 0.5% vs OpenSea / OpenSea: ~1.5%' — OpenSea fee is 1% now
findings.evidence: NATIVE LISTINGS card shows 'Direct Seaport orders · 1% fee', badge 'Save 0.5% vs OpenSea', comparison chips 'Native: 1% Platform fee only' vs 'OpenSea: ~1.5% Marketplace + royalty'. Project memory (2026-06-09 Tradermigos note) explicitly recorded OpenSea's fee is 1% now and 'don't market a fee discount'.
findings.suggestion: Update the comparison to '1% vs 1%' parity messaging or remove the savings badge; a checkably false fee claim is a trust liability on a trading product.

findings.title: Secondary 'Make Offer' button next to Buy is clipped to 'Mak'/'Ma' — present in prod AND at HEAD
findings.evidence: In the #1170 and #10219 modals, the button right of 'Connect Wallet to Buy' renders ~30px wide showing only 'Mak'. Same clipped 'Ma' next to 'Buy for 0.1045 ETH' on localhost:5173 (HEAD) — so not env-specific.
findings.suggestion: Fix the flex layout (min-width / flex-shrink) so the secondary CTA renders fully; it currently looks broken on the primary conversion surface. The separate '+ Make Offer' button further down works as a stopgap.

findings.title: Offers and Comparable Sales sections show skeleton rows that never resolve
findings.evidence: #1170 modal: OFFERS shows BEST OFFER 0.1580 followed by 3 grey skeleton bars; COMPARABLE SALES shows 3 skeleton bars. Both still skeletons after 60+ seconds and repeated scrolling. #10219 modal showed 3 offer skeletons with no best-offer card at all in prod.
findings.suggestion: Replace永-skeletons with real rows or an explicit empty state ('No other offers' / 'No comparable sales in 30d') once the fetch settles; skeletons that never resolve read as broken.

findings.title: Two contradictory fair-value/rank models for the same token on the same click path
findings.evidence: Deals table listed #1170 at fair value 0.3880→0.9000 ('32% below', rank ~#1103-#1782 refining); opening its modal shows 'Est. Fair Value 0.2502' with a 'FAIR' badge (i.e., NOT a deal) and 'RANK #3332'. A user clicks a '32% below' deal and the detail view tells them it's fairly priced at a different rank.
findings.suggestion: Use one fair-value and one rank source on both surfaces (or show both metrics labeled 'trait-floor value' vs 'sale-history value'); the contradiction kills confidence in the deals engine.

findings.title: Floor Depth 'Depth Chart' renders an essentially blank box; floor 24h delta shows ↓35.0% with empty 1h/7d deltas
findings.evidence: Depth Chart panel is an empty red-bordered rectangle with a single tiny line top-left (zoomed to verify). FLOOR PRICE health card shows '1h: %' and '7d: %' with no values and '24h: ↓35.0%' in red while the floor sat at ~0.1045-0.1048 throughout the session (sales 0.0967-0.85) — a -35% day is implausible.
findings.suggestion: Fix the depth chart rendering (likely the same outlier-domain problem) and hide delta rows when the baseline is missing instead of rendering bare '%' glyphs; verify the 24h floor baseline source.

findings.title: Documented 'c = add to cart' keyboard shortcut does nothing; Escape fails to close the Trait Offer popover (it persisted across Lite/Pro remount)
findings.evidence: KeyboardHelp lists 'c — Add to cart (focused card)'. Pressed j (card #11481 visibly focused with highlight) then c: no toast, no cart badge (bag icon zoomed — empty). Separately, the PICK A TRAIT popover from 'Trait Offer' stayed open after Escape, after clicking elsewhere, and was still in the DOM after toggling Lite mode.
findings.suggestion: Wire the c handler to the focused card's cart action and add Escape/outside-click dismissal to the trait-offer popover.

findings.title: Click-to-enter splash (~10-14s before CLICK TO ENTER appears) replays on EVERY full page load / deep link
findings.evidence: Hard navigations to /deals, /trade, /portfolio, /analytics and localhost each replayed the full TRADERMIGOS card animation; clicking before the animation finishes does nothing (had to wait ~12s then click on /portfolio and /analytics). No sessionStorage memory — a bookmarked deep link always pays the toll.
findings.suggestion: Keep the splash (it's great brand art) but remember entry per session, make it click-skippable from second 0, and auto-skip for deep links with a query param/referrer check. Do not remove the art — just gate the replay.

findings.title: Two near-identical connect-gated tabs ('Trade' and 'P2P Trades') with no preview of the trade flow
findings.evidence: /trade: 'Connect your wallet to swap Nakamigos directly with other holders through peer-to-peer trades.' /trades: 'Connect your wallet to send and receive NFT-for-NFT trade offers.' Both are bare gates; nothing shows what the trade builder looks like, what's offered, or recent public P2P trades.
findings.suggestion: Merge or clearly differentiate (builder vs inbox); show a read-only mock of the two-sided trade window with disabled controls and a feed of recent public trades behind the gate, like Trader.xyz/Sudoswap OTC do.

findings.title: No public collection bid book for logged-out users
findings.evidence: /bids is purely 'Connect your wallet to manage bids...'. The data to show a public bid wall exists in-app (listings page renders COLLECTION OFFERS (50) ladder).
findings.suggestion: Show the collection-wide bid ladder (Blur-style bid wall: price x quantity x bidders) on /bids for everyone, gating only the 'manage MY bids' half behind connect.

findings.title: Fair-value outliers produce unbelievable headline claims (95% off, 18 ETH fair value, 'TOTAL SAVINGS 20.13 ETH')
findings.evidence: Deal row #669: listed 0.9000, 'fair value' 18.0000, '95% below' (Crocodile trait floor inflated by one thin listing). Header stats reached 'TOTAL SAVINGS 20.13 ETH' on a 0.104-floor collection. BEST DEAL '91% off / 92% off' rotated through similar thin-trait tokens.
findings.suggestion: Cap trait-floor fair value (e.g., min(trait floor, k x collection floor) or require >=3 listings/sales per trait), and badge low-confidence estimates. One absurd row makes users discount the legitimate 20-50% finds.

findings.title: eth.llamarpc.com RPC returns 521 (origin down) on repeated OPTIONS preflights
findings.evidence: read_network_requests captured https://eth.llamarpc.com/ OPTIONS -> 521 on deals, sniper, whales and listings; it retries continuously in the background. App functions via other providers; /api/alchemy calls returned 200.
findings.suggestion: Drop or demote llamarpc in the fallback list (or health-check before use) to stop burning requests on a dead endpoint.

findings.title: LIVE sales ticker intermittently renders empty (dot with no text)
findings.evidence: After ~5 minutes on /listings the ticker pill showed only the green dot and '5m ago' with empty sale text (zoomed screenshot); it recovered on the next cycle.
findings.suggestion: Keep the last sale rendered until the next one is ready instead of clearing mid-cycle.

findings.title: Profile drawer is excellent but Escape doesn't close it; expanded holder grid lazy-loads with many blank cells initially
findings.evidence: Holder profile drawer (0x0220...60EE: 596 owned, est. value 62.282, WHALE + DIAMOND HANDS badges, View all 596) only closes via the X; Escape press did nothing. Holder #1 expanded '100 NAKAMIGOS HELD' grid showed ~half empty cells for several seconds before images arrived.
findings.suggestion: Add Escape/overlay-click to close, and a shimmer placeholder in grid cells while thumbnails lazy-load.

findings.title: Type filter offers only All/Sale and search ignores the selected timeframe; stats don't react to search
findings.evidence: Filter chips are 24h/7d/30d/All Time + All/Sale only (subtitle says 'Live on-chain transfers' but no Transfer/Mint/List types exist). With 24h selected, searching '2346' returned rows '1d ago' and '2d ago'; header still showed '17 SALES 2.5338 VOLUME' while 2 rows displayed.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the redundant All/Sale pair or add real event types (listings, transfers, mints like OpenSea); scope search to the active window or visibly switch to 'all time' when searching, and recompute the header stats.

findings.title: Top Holder Distribution histogram buckets are misleading (top-100 only, so 1/2-5/6-10/11-25 rows are always 0)
findings.evidence: Rows: '1 NFT: 0', '2-5: 0', '6-10: 0', '11-25: 0', '26-50: 58', '51-100: 28', '100+: 22' with footnote 'Showing top 100 holders of 5,212 total'. Four permanently-empty rows under a title implying full-collection distribution.
findings.suggestion: Either compute the real full-holder distribution (5,212 owners) or retitle to 'Top 100 holders by position size' and drop the empty buckets.

findings.title: Six connect-gates share the same visual with no 'demo/preview' affordance the app already has elsewhere
findings.evidence: All six gated tabs render the identical wallet-icon + copy + Connect Wallet block; the deals loading screen briefly flashed a 'DEMO' badge concept, but no gate offers demo data or a screenshot of the connected experience.
findings.suggestion: Additive: add a 'Preview with demo wallet' link rendering the real components with sample data — converts better than a wall and exercises the gated code paths in prod.

findings.title: Microcopy nits: 'Nakamigos - My-listings' title casing; '- 0xbluemoon.eth · Profile' stray leading hyphen; theater bottom bar repeats '#10219' twice
findings.evidence: document.title = 'Nakamigos - My-listings | Tradermigos'; modal owner row renders '- 0xbluemoon.eth · Profile'; theater bar shows 'Nakamigos #10219  #10219'.
findings.suggestion: Humanize route-derived titles ('My Listings'), drop the dangling separator when collection name is absent, and dedupe the theater label.

findings.title: Theme toggle (moon/sun) only swaps blue/gold accent colors — there is no light theme; header alternates 1-row/2-row layout on scroll causing nav targets to jump
findings.evidence: Clicking the moon icon re-tinted card borders/CTAs gold and swapped the icon, background stayed near-black (screenshots before/after). The nav row collapses from two rows to one as you scroll, moving Floor/More by hundreds of px — three of my clicks landed on the wrong control after a layout switch.
findings.suggestion: If light mode isn't planned, use a palette icon instead of moon/sun; consider pinning the header to one layout to keep click targets stable.

findings.title: No USD values or fee/gas breakdown in cart and offer modal; offer modal lacks floor/best-offer context
findings.evidence: Cart shows '2 ITEMS 0.2091' with no USD, no marketplace fee or royalty line (sweep panel DOES show EST. GAS ~0.0180 — inconsistent). MakeOffer modal has only a WETH input + expiration chips; no floor price, current best offer, or 'your offer is X% below floor' hint (OpenSea shows all three).
findings.suggestion: Add USD conversion + fee/royalty/gas line to the cart summary and floor/best-offer context inside the offer modal.

findings.title: No wash-trade/self-sale flagging anywhere on the trading surface
findings.evidence: Activity feed shows '#16971 0xf46a...6feb → 0xf46a...6feb 0.0967' (same address both sides) rendered as a normal sale; sales stats and price history include it.
findings.suggestion: Badge same-wallet and round-trip sales ('possible wash') and exclude them from avg-sale and price-history stats — table-stakes for a 'pro' trading tool.

findings.title: Rank values silently shift while the scan runs (#434 went #910→#982→#994) with no 'approximate' marker in the table
findings.evidence: Same row re-screenshotted ~30s apart showed three different ranks as 'Scanning: X / 20,000' progressed; only the page subtitle hints at refinement, the rank cells look authoritative.
findings.suggestion: Suffix ranks with '~' (the sniper already says 'ranks approximate') or freeze displayed ranks until the scan completes a checkpoint.

good: /trades prior 404 is FIXED in prod — loads with proper title 'Nakamigos - Trades | Tradermigos' and a sensible connect gate
/portfolio prior P&L TDZ crash: page loads cleanly with zero console errors (sub-tabs are behind the wallet gate, untestable logged-out)

Deals engine is genuinely live: progressive 'Scanning: X / 20,000' counter, stats refine in real time, '3 new deals found! Click to refresh view' banner works, filters (price min, min discount, trait select, rank) all filter the table instantly

Activity feed is real on-chain data refreshed ~12s: ENS-resolved addresses (gwizz.eth, even 🚮🚮🚮.eth), marketplace tag, time-ago, external links, timeframe chips recompute the SALES/VOLUME header, search works, Load More present

Whale Intelligence page has real substance: top-25 holders with holdings/%, expandable holding grids, holder concentration bars (Top10 16.6%, 4,989/20,000), live whale alerts, and a polished holder Profile drawer (owned count, est. value, WHALE/DIAMOND HANDS badges, View all N)

Sweep calculator is excellent: BY QTY / BY BUDGET modes, trait filter, max-price-per-item, correct math (0.5 ETH budget → 4 items, 0.4193 total verified by hand), floor impact estimate (+1.0%), est. gas, sweep queue with per-item source badges, correct disconnected CTA 'Connect & Sweep 4 Nakamigos'

Cart flow is fully local and safe: card checkboxes → '2 selected · 0.2091 total' bar → Add All to Cart toasts → badge → drawer with per-item remove, Clear Cart, and a friendly empty state — zero network mutations observed
KeyboardHelp (?) modal is complete and styled (j/k, Enter, Escape, g, 1-9, f, c, s//, m); j-focus visibly highlights cards
Per-page document.titles are correct everywhere ('Nakamigos - Deals | Tradermigos', etc.)

Token modal has real micro-content: price history sparkline with min/avg/last, ORDER WARNING for 50-day-old listings, trait story cards ('Frog — a nod to Pepe... 868 exist 4.34%'), honest '(based on 5,280/20,000 loaded)' annotations, OpenSea/Etherscan links
Connect gates use page-specific helpful copy (bids/history/my-listings each explain exactly what connecting unlocks)
Lite/Pro toggle meaningfully changes density (6-wide simple grid + slim header vs pro panels); notifications dropdown has clean tabbed empty state
Zero console errors recorded across all 12+ pages audited; /api/alchemy calls all 200
Splash art and falling-cards intro is genuinely beautiful brand work (keep it — just fix replay behavior)
live:naka-market.splashAndTransitions: The TRADERMIGOS click-to-enter splash is the dominant transition cost: ~10-14s of card animation before 'CLICK TO ENTER' becomes clickable (early clicks are ignored), and it replays on EVERY hard navigation/deep link — no session memory (verified on /deals, /trade, /portfolio, /analytics, and localhost). In-app tab switches are instant with no splash and feel good; data-heavy pages (deals, analytics) show their own progressive 'Scanning N/20,000' states which are honest and well done. Skeleton quality is mixed: deals/whales/listings skeletons resolve properly, but token-modal Offers/Comparable-Sales skeletons never resolve (stuck), reading as broken. Scroll position resets to top on tab switches (acceptable); one transient full-black repaint occurred during a fast scroll-to-top on deals but recovered in ~2s.
live:naka-market.consoleAndNetwork: Console: zero errors/exceptions captured across all audited tabs (checked+cleared after each page). Network: recurring https://eth.llamarpc.com/ OPTIONS preflight failing with 521 (origin down) on every page sampled — background RPC fallback burning requests; should be removed/health-checked. https://tegridyfarms.vercel.app/api/alchemy?endpoint=getNFTsForContract... returned 200; lazy-loaded chunks (MakeOfferModal, orderValidator, weth, useEns) all loaded normally. No 4xx/5xx from the app's own API observed, no 429s during ~50 minutes of continuous polling pages.
pagesCovered: /nakamigos/nakamigos/listings (Floor: cart, sweep, order book, theater, shortcuts)

findings.title: Immunefi bug-bounty program does not exist — 'Submit on Immunefi' links to a 404
findings.evidence: Page claims "We partner with Immunefi, the leading Web3 bug bounty platform" and the purple 'Submit on Immunefi' button links to https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/tegridyfarms/ which returns HTTP 404 (curl-verified). Same href present at localhost HEAD, so not fixed. This sits next to $10,000/$5,000/$1,000/$500 reward tiers, and directly contradicts the site's own FAQ honesty stance ("There is no paid third-party audit yet — we don't claim one").
findings.suggestion: Either stand up the actual Immunefi program, or change copy to 'Bug bounty paid case-by-case — report via Twitter DM / security email' until it exists. A fake partnership claim on the trust page is the single worst credibility hit on the site.

findings.title: Changelog is 5+ weeks stale and contradicts the Security page
findings.evidence: Latest entry is 'May 4, 2026 — Pass-7 Adversarial Multi-Agent Audit' (today is June 11, 2026). The June 2026 relaunch and mainnet MVP redeploy — which Tokenomics itself references ("rebuilt fresh at the June 2026 relaunch") — are absent. Worse, the April 14 entry says 'NFT Lending & AMM Deployment / Deployed TegridyNFTLending...' while /security lists TegridyLending, TegridyNFTLending, TegridyNFTPoolFactory as 'Not deployed — deferred from the relaunch'. Same content at localhost HEAD.
findings.suggestion: Add a June 2026 'Relaunch' entry (new addresses, what was deferred, why) at the top. Without it the page reads as abandoned and the deploy-history contradiction looks like dishonesty rather than staleness.

findings.title: First-load splash runs ~18-20 seconds with no visible skip affordance
findings.evidence: Cold navigation to /tokenomics played a multi-stage intro (dim art slideshow → RGB-glitch art → particle ring → glass-shatter) lasting ~18-20s before any content. A click mid-splash did not visibly skip (shatter stage continued). Only control shown is a mute toggle top-right. Splash is correctly session-scoped (no replay on later loads).
findings.suggestion: Keep the art (it's great) but add a visible 'Skip' / click-anywhere-to-skip and cap default duration to ~4-6s. 20s before first paint is bounce territory for first-time visitors clicking a tokenomics link.

findings.title: Page named 'leaderboard' contains no leaderboard, ranks, or my-rank affordance
findings.evidence: Content is 'Your Tegridy Score' + How Points Work (+10 swap/+25 stake/+50 LP), tiers, and badges. No table, no ranks, no top-wallets, no 'your rank' placeholder. Banner honestly says 'A cross-wallet ranking goes live when the Ponder indexer is publicly queryable.'
findings.suggestion: Additively: show a 'Top stakers (on-chain)' preview readable directly via RPC (staking contract events/balances) so the page has at least one real ranked list pre-indexer, plus a disabled 'Your rank — connect wallet' row as the my-rank affordance.

findings.title: Empty state asserts 'No participants yet' as fact while the data source isn't live
findings.evidence: Card reads 'No participants yet. Stake TOWELI to earn your first points!' — but the same page says cross-wallet data awaits the Ponder indexer, and staking has live stakers on-chain (staking contract is seeded and earning). Zero is being displayed where the truthful state is 'unknown/not indexed yet'. Same copy at localhost HEAD.
findings.suggestion: Change to 'Ranking goes live once the indexer is public — be early: stake now to start your streak.' Don't render an unverifiable zero; it advertises emptiness.

findings.title: Light/day mode renders 'Your Tegridy Score' heading dark-on-dark (unreadable)
findings.evidence: After toggling the sun icon, only the navbar switched to Kenny-orange; the page body stayed near-black but the H1 'Your Tegridy Score' switched to a dark navy color — virtually invisible in the screenshot. Day mode on Activity pages is effectively navbar-only.
findings.suggestion: Audit day-mode tokens on LearnPage/ActivityPage: headings must keep a light-on-dark pair while the art-panel backgrounds remain dark, or flip the panel scrims with the theme.

findings.title: 'All Badges' grid is borderline unreadable — dim locked-badge text over bright busy art
findings.evidence: Zoom-verified: badge titles ('First Swap', 'Farmer', 'Week Warrior') and descriptions are mid-gray on a translucent card over bright orange/purple character art; double-dimming (locked state + low scrim opacity) makes several badges illegible.
findings.suggestion: Additive fix: raise the card scrim opacity / add backdrop-blur behind the badge grid (keep the art behind it). Locked state can use a lock icon instead of further text dimming.

findings.title: Gold Card page has zero value proposition — entire content is a 3-line SOON banner
findings.evidence: Full page text: 'SOON / Gold Card isn't live yet / Premium memberships and revenue-share perks return once the PremiumAccess contract is deployed for the relaunch.' Nothing about what the Gold Card is, perks, pricing, or the JBAC free-access policy (those answers exist only in FAQ → PREMIUM). For the record, the prior art issue is gone: the page now renders a hand-drawn extreme close-up of an ape's eye with lens-flare sparkles, fully on-style.
findings.suggestion: Additively add: perks preview cards (revenue share, boosts), 'JBAC holders get free access' callout, link to the two FAQ premium answers, and a notify-me / follow-X CTA so the page captures demand instead of dead-ending.

findings.title: Logged-out History is a pure connect-gate — no protocol activity feed, no preview
findings.evidence: Page shows only 'Transaction History / Connect your wallet to view your history.' + Connect Wallet button over the (excellent) newspaper-ape art. None of the page objectives (feed realness, tx links, filtering, pagination) exist without a wallet.
findings.suggestion: Additively show a protocol-wide recent-activity feed (stakes, swaps, claims from the indexer or direct RPC logs) with Etherscan tx links below the connect CTA, plus a faded sample-row preview of what personal history looks like.

findings.title: Multisig/timelock claims have no on-chain proof links and no 'as of' state
findings.evidence: 'Protocol admin controlled by team multisig', 'All admin changes require 24-48h timelock', 'Multisig & Governance' section — none link to the Safe address or timelock contract on Etherscan (the three contract rows above do have links). Given ownership acceptance is still mid-rotation operationally, the claims are currently unverifiable from the page.
findings.suggestion: Add Etherscan links for the Safe + timelock (like the contract rows), and an 'as of <date>' stamp. Verify the multisig-control claim matches current on-chain owner before the acceptOwnership wave completes — until then a softer 'transitioning to multisig control' is more honest.

findings.title: FAQ search matches question titles only — terms inside answers return nothing
findings.evidence: Typing 'uniswap' returned zero results even though the 'How do I get TOWELI tokens?' answer says 'Buy TOWELI on Uniswap V2...'. Typing 'rug' correctly found 'Can the admin rug pull?'.
findings.suggestion: Index answer bodies in the filter, and highlight the matched term in results.

findings.title: 'No questions match your search' empty state is nearly invisible
findings.evidence: With query 'zzzqqq', the no-results message renders as small dark text directly over the bright pink watercolor art (and is partially overlapped by the character's head) — zoom needed to read it at all. No 'clear search' action in the empty state.
findings.suggestion: Put the message inside the same dark panel style as the accordions and add a 'Clear search' button.

findings.title: Emission numbers disagree on the same page and round away 6% of the seed
findings.evidence: 'Emissions End In ~89 days' (Emission Schedule card) vs 'ENDS IN 90 days' (Community Treasury strip). 'Funded (lifetime) 6M TOWELI' and 'REWARDS REMAINING 6M TOWELI' — actual seed is ~6.41M (71,219.52/day × 90d; rewardRate 0.8243/s), so the compact format truncates 410k tokens, and 'remaining' equals 'funded' (no decay shown).
findings.suggestion: Use one rounding source for both cards, display '6.4M', and compute Rewards Remaining from periodFinish-now × rate so it visibly ticks down.

findings.title: 'Live' vs 'Deployed' badge taxonomy unexplained
findings.evidence: Contracts list: most rows green 'Live', pending rows gray 'Pending / Not yet deployed', but POLAccumulator gets a unique orange 'Deployed' badge (0x2A5f65...ED11D2) with no tooltip explaining how Deployed differs from Live.
findings.suggestion: Add a tooltip or legend ('Deployed = on-chain, not yet activated'), or collapse to one term.

findings.title: eth.llamarpc.com is down and tried on every load
findings.evidence: Network log: OPTIONS https://eth.llamarpc.com/ → 521 and POST → 503 on multiple page loads; failover to rpc.ankr.com and ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (both 200) works with zero console errors.
findings.suggestion: Failover works, but deprioritize/health-check llamarpc to avoid the dead first hop latency on cold loads.

findings.title: Keyboard jump-scroll (End / Ctrl+Home) shows fully blank frames until a wheel scroll
findings.evidence: Pressing End and Ctrl+Home on /security both produced screenshots of a pure dark page (no navbar, no content) ~2s after the keypress; content reappeared immediately on the next mouse-wheel scroll. Reproduced twice; likely the scroll-reveal animation system not firing on instant jumps. Low confidence on root cause but the captures were real.
findings.suggestion: Check IntersectionObserver-driven reveal animations on programmatic/keyboard scroll; ensure sections default to visible after a timeout.

findings.title: Entries are raw audit jargon with no reader-level summary
findings.evidence: Bullets like '13 stateful invariants × 1.664M total calls, zero reverts' and 'V4 hook fee delta never settled — every V4 swap would have reverted CurrencyNotSettled'. Transparency is great; comprehension for a normal user is near zero.
findings.suggestion: Additively add a one-line plain-English TL;DR chip per entry ('What this means for you: ...') above the technical bullets.

findings.title: Mascot tooltip overstates security posture vs FAQ
findings.evidence: Mascot bubble on /security reads 'Audited and bug-bountied. Safer than my last job.' while the FAQ answer carefully says 'There is no paid third-party audit yet — we don't claim one' and the bounty link 404s.
findings.suggestion: Soften to 'Internally red-teamed to hell and back' — keeps the joke, drops the over-claim.

findings.title: Mascot bubble covers the 'Protocol Active' price ticker
findings.evidence: Bottom-right ticker ('● Protocol Active $0.0…132') is overlapped by the mascot avatar and its speech bubble whenever a tip shows (zoom-verified on /history and /premium).
findings.suggestion: Stack the ticker above the mascot or shift the bubble up so both are readable.

findings.title: Category labels low-contrast over bright art
findings.evidence: Section labels 'GETTING STARTED', 'REWARDS', 'NFT FINANCE', 'SECURITY' are small dark-purple caps directly on the bright pink/lavender watercolor background — readable only on the darker patches.
findings.suggestion: Give the labels the same translucent dark chip treatment as the accordion rows.

findings.title: Audit chip label dates drift from linked filenames
findings.evidence: 'Pass-7 audit + remediation (May 4)' links to PASS7_2026_05_03.md; 'Pass-6 fresh-eyes audit (May 3)' to PASS6_2026_05_03.md. One-day drift between label and artifact name on the page whose whole point is precision.
findings.suggestion: Make labels match the artifact dates exactly.

findings.title: No per-entry anchors or subscribe affordance
findings.evidence: Timeline entries have no anchor links (can't share '#may-4-2026'), and there's no RSS/notify option for protocol updates.
findings.suggestion: Add anchor ids per entry and a 'follow updates on X/Telegram' chip at top.

findings.title: No time-axis emission chart
findings.evidence: Emission data is presented as four static numbers (Rewards/Day, Rewards/Second, Funded, Ends In) — there is no chart showing the 90-day emission runway or what happens at the cliff, even though the page has chart real estate (the donut).
findings.suggestion: Additively add a small area chart 'emissions remaining over time' with the end-date marked — this also pre-answers the September cliff question.

good: Honesty discipline is genuinely best-in-class for this market: 'Not deployed — deferred from the relaunch' + SOON badges on Security contract rows, 'Gold Card isn't live yet' gating, FAQ openly stating 'There is no paid third-party audit yet — we don't claim one', NFT Lending FAQ answer admitting contracts are 'audited but not yet redeployed', and the Points page disclosing the streak counter is local. (The Immunefi claim is the one glaring exception.)

All 8 deep links select the correct tab; in-page tab switches update both URL and document.title ('Tokenomics | Tegridy Farms', 'Your Tegridy Score | Tegridy Farms', etc.) and reset scroll to top — clean SPA routing.
All six GitHub audit-artifact links on /security resolve HTTP 200 to real files in a public repo (PASS7/PASS6/post-remediation ledger/300-agent/Opus reviews) — receipts actually exist.

Contract addresses are full, copyable, Etherscan-linked, and match the deployed MVP record (TOWELI 0x420698...278F9D, TegridyStaking 0xcaDc93...5E046D, Router 0xE9F83A07...). Tokenomics figures are internally consistent (price × 1B supply = displayed FDV; donut sums to 100%).
Zero console errors across all 8 routes, and RPC provider failover works silently in production: eth.llamarpc.com down (521/503) → ankr + publicnode picked up with no user-visible impact.
Splash is correctly session-scoped — plays once, never again on subsequent navigations in the session.

Art direction is a real differentiator and is used additively: newspaper-reading ape behind History's empty state, the eye close-up on Premium, skull 'JB AC' on Security, watercolor on FAQ — with content kept on translucent dark panels (mostly readable).

The mascot assistant has per-page contextual copy ('Your tx receipts...', 'Climb the ranks. Earn points. Brag responsibly.', 'Randy's Gold Card. Bonus rewards for the loyal.') with 'Don't show again' — personality without blocking content (except the ticker overlap noted).

FAQ is well-built: 22 questions across 6 categories, smooth multi-open accordions, live search with clear button, and the 'Can the admin rug pull?' answer is an unusually honest, specific threat-model disclosure (bounded admin powers, what a compromised admin could and couldn't do).
RainbowKit connect modal opens and closes cleanly from History's Connect Wallet CTA (Phantom detected as installed, standard wallet list).
Ultrawide layout holds up: content column capped at 1200px and centered, flanks filled with full-bleed art rather than dead margins — no over-stretched line lengths anywhere on the 8 pages.
Footer carries consistent legal/disclaimer ('Experimental protocol. Use at your own risk. Not financial advice.') plus Risk Disclosure and Security links on every page.
live:learn-activity.splashAndTransitions: First visit: ~18-20s multi-stage splash (dim art slideshow → RGB glitch → particle ring → glass shatter) with a mute toggle but no visible skip; a mid-splash click did not clearly skip. Splash is session-scoped — no replay on any later full page load (verified on /history). In-page tab switches are instant, update URL/title, and reset scroll to top. Scroll-reveal fade-ins are used heavily; they look good on wheel scroll but keyboard jumps (End/Ctrl+Home on /security) twice produced fully blank rendered frames until the next wheel tick. No skeletons needed on these mostly-static pages — stat cards on Tokenomics rendered with real values immediately after splash. Day-mode toggle works but only reskins the navbar on these pages and creates a dark-on-dark heading on /leaderboard.
live:learn-activity.consoleAndNetwork: Zero console errors or exceptions across all 8 routes (tracked after first load; subsequent SPA navigations clean). Failed network calls: https://eth.llamarpc.com/ — OPTIONS 521 and POST 503, recurring on multiple page loads; failover requests to https://rpc.ankr.com/eth and https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com/ both 200, so no user-visible breakage. No /api/ calls observed on these 8 logged-out pages (they are static/RPC-driven). External-link audit via curl: all 6 GitHub audit links 200; https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/tegridyfarms/ 404 (also linked at localhost HEAD).

findings.title: Chat posting writes with the anon-key client that the JWT-gated RLS policy rejects — sending fails for everyone in live mode
findings.evidence: CommunityChat.jsx:516-522 calls sendMessage from lib/supabase.js, which does a DIRECT anon-client insert: supabase.js:216-218 `await supabase.from("messages").insert({ author, text, token_id: tokenId, slug })`. But migration 004_security_hardening.sql:97-98 re-creates `CREATE POLICY "Verified can insert" ON public.messages FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (author = lower(...request.jwt.claims...->>'wallet') ...)` — the anon key's JWT has no `wallet` claim, so the check is null → INSERT rejected → sendMessage returns null → user always sees "Failed to send message. Please check your connection and try again." (CommunityChat.jsx:531). The file's own header (supabase.js:90-94) says "All WRITE operations ... should go through the /api/supabase-proxy endpoint", and the proxy is ready for it: api/supabase-proxy.js:53 ALLOWED_TABLES includes "messages" and api/_lib/proxy-schemas.js:106-107,174 validates `author` against the JWT wallet. CommunityChat was never migrated to the proxy and has no SIWE sign-in affordance anywhere (it gates posting only on wallet+holderTier, App.jsx:655). Caveat: based on repo migrations as source of truth; only a divergent prod policy would change this.
findings.suggestion: Route sendMessage through /api/supabase-proxy (same proxyCall pattern as lib/dm.js), and add the DirectMessages-style "Sign in" gate to the room composer (useSiweAuth is already in the bundle). Surface 401 as needs-auth instead of a generic connection error.

findings.title: Like button is a silent no-op in live mode — toggle_like RPC requires a JWT wallet claim the anon client can never supply
findings.evidence: lib/supabase.js:255-257 calls `supabase.rpc("toggle_like", { msg_id, wallet })` with the anon key. Migration 006_audit_2026_05_26.sql:46-48: `jwt_wallet := lower(current_setting('request.jwt.claims'...)); IF jwt_wallet IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'Unauthorized: JWT missing wallet claim';` → RPC always errors → toggleLike returns null (supabase.js:259-265). CommunityChat.jsx:559-565 `const updated = await toggleLike(...); if (updated) {...}` — no else branch, no toast: the heart button visibly does nothing.
findings.suggestion: Route the like through the proxy (or add a toggle_like proxy RPC path) and show feedback on failure; until then at least toast 'Sign in to like' the way handleReaction toasts on failure.

findings.title: toggle_reaction RPC has no JWT ownership check — anyone with the public anon key can add/remove reactions as ANY wallet
findings.evidence: Migration 007_p2p_trades_and_chat.sql:119-149 defines toggle_reaction as SECURITY DEFINER validating only the emoji allowlist and `w !~ '^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$'` — unlike toggle_like (006:46-59) it never compares against request.jwt.claims. 008_grant_new_table_roles.sql:20 grants EXECUTE ON ALL ROUTINES to anon. So reactions are simultaneously (a) the only chat write that works from the current anon client and (b) spoofable: any visitor can call the RPC with any victim wallet and toggle their reactions. CommunityChat.jsx:437-446 passes the connected (unauthenticated) wallet.
findings.suggestion: Add the same jwt_wallet check to toggle_reaction (new migration) and call it through the proxy — matching the toggle_like pattern.

findings.title: Entire userdata cloud-sync layer is dead in production: all writes (and, since migration 004, favorites/watchlist reads) go through the anon client that RLS rejects — everything silently degrades to this-browser-only localStorage
findings.evidence: userdata.js writes use the bare anon client: saveProfile :161-169, syncFavorites push :197-199, addFavoriteRemote :211, removeFavoriteRemote :218, syncWatchlist push :255-266, addWatchlistRemote :278, removeWatchlistRemote :291, castVote :325-327. Migrations 001/004 make every one of these require `wallet = lower(jwt->>'wallet')` (e.g. 004:120-130 favorites, :132-142 watchlist, :144-155 votes), which the anon JWT cannot satisfy. Worse, 004:157-165 replaced the public SELECT with `CREATE POLICY "Owner reads favorites" ... FOR SELECT USING (wallet = ...jwt...)` — so syncFavorites' read (userdata.js:185-189) silently returns ZERO rows (RLS filters, no error) and sync becomes a no-op. The header comment (userdata.js:9-10, "persistence ... across devices") is false at runtime. The proxy already allowlists user_profiles/user_favorites/user_watchlist/votes (api/supabase-proxy.js:53) but userdata.js never uses it.
findings.suggestion: Port userdata.js writes to the supabase-proxy (proxyCall pattern from lib/dm.js) gated on SIWE, and either restore public reads for favorites/watchlist or read them through the proxy too. Until then, remove 'across devices' implications from UI copy.

findings.title: "Profile saved" success toast fires even when the cloud write was rejected — saveProfile's failure return is ignored
findings.evidence: EditProfile.jsx:92-97: `await saveProfile(wallet, {...}, slug); addToast?.("Profile saved", "success");` — saveProfile returns false on Supabase error (userdata.js:171-175 `return !error;` / `return false;`) and does NOT throw, so the catch at EditProfile.jsx:100 never runs. Combined with the RLS rejection above, every prod save shows a false success while only writing the local cache (userdata.js:154-156).
findings.suggestion: Check the boolean result: success toast only on true; on false show 'Saved locally — sign in to sync your profile'.

findings.title: NftCompare still uses the legacy userdata.createTradeOffer/updateTradeStatus path that migration 007 revoked — trades become localStorage ghosts the counterparty never sees
findings.evidence: NftCompare.jsx:8 imports `{ createTradeOffer, getIncomingTrades, updateTradeStatus } from "../lib/userdata"` and calls them (:424, :457). Migration 007:47-54 drops all client-side trade_offers write policies and replaces with `CREATE POLICY "Service role inserts trades" ... TO service_role` (writes only via /api/orderbook). userdata.js:436-461: when the insert errors it silently falls back to `loadTradesCache(...); trades.push(trade); saveTradesCache(...)` — a local-only "pending" trade. The correct Seaport-settled path exists in lib/trades.js (used by TradeWindow/TradesPanel).
findings.suggestion: Point NftCompare's trade flow at lib/trades.js createTradeOffer/fetchTrades/updateTradeStatus (the orderbook API path), and delete the dead trade functions from userdata.js.

findings.title: DM polling consumes 18 of the proxy's 20 req/min wallet budget; the first 429 is then misclassified as "DMs aren't enabled yet"
findings.evidence: With a thread open, every 15s tick (DirectMessages.jsx:220) runs loadThread → fetchThread (1 proxy call) + markThreadRead (1 PATCH, unconditional even when nothing is unread — dm.js:137-146) and loadConvos → fetchConversations = 2 SELECTs (dm.js:92-95). That's 4 calls/15s = 16/min, plus useDmUnread's fetchUnreadCount = 2 more calls/min (useDmUnread.js:4,32) = 18/min vs the proxy stage-2 limit `limit: 20, windowSec: 60` keyed per wallet (api/supabase-proxy.js:230-233). Two sends or reactions in a minute tip it over. When a 429 lands, classify() at DirectMessages.jsx:173 (`if (err?.status && err.status < 500) return "not-enabled"`) replaces the whole pane with "DMs aren't enabled yet — The messaging backend (migration 007) hasn't been switched on" (:352-360) — wrong message for rate limiting.
findings.suggestion: Handle 429 explicitly (transient/retry state), only PATCH read_at when the thread actually has unread, and merge the conversation-list poll into a single proxy call (or lengthen its cadence while a thread is open).

findings.title: Sign-in button produces an unhandled promise rejection when the user rejects the wallet signature
findings.evidence: DirectMessages.jsx:341-344: `onClick={async () => { const ok = await signIn(); if (ok) {...} }}` — no try/catch. useSiweAuth.signIn throws on rejection: useSiweAuth.js:122-126 `if (err.code === 4001 || err.code === "ACTION_REJECTED") { throw new Error("Sign-in cancelled"); } throw err;`. Rejecting the MetaMask prompt yields an unhandled rejection and zero UI feedback (button just un-busies).
findings.suggestion: Wrap in try/catch and toast the error message ('Sign-in cancelled' / server error).

findings.title: "Recent Sales" and "24H VOLUME" math counts live listing/bid prices as sales once the OpenSea stream connects
findings.evidence: The `activities` prop is mergedActivities (useCollection.js:29-31 flattens `openSea.listings, sales, bids, cancellations`; :94-113 prepends them to the sale-only polled feed). Analytics.jsx:131 `const prices = activities.filter(a => a.price > 0)` feeds AVG SALE / HIGHEST / LOWEST / SALES COUNT (:133-138) — listing and bid events all carry price>0 (eventFeed.js:85-92). CollectionHealth.jsx:199 `recentSales.day.reduce((s, a) => s + (a.price || 0), 0)` is labeled "24H VOLUME" but recentSales filters only by time (:156-162), so an above-floor listing inflates volume; floorMetrics (:165-188) has the same contamination.
findings.suggestion: Filter `a.type === "sale"` in Analytics.activityStats/priceDistribution and CollectionHealth.recentSales/floorMetrics (ActivityFeed already does this for its own stats at ActivityFeed.jsx:186-194).

findings.title: Feed is not chronologically ordered when live events are present (two merge points skip sorting)
findings.evidence: useCollection.js:112 `return [...newLive, ...activities].slice(0, 500)` — prepends without sorting. ActivityFeed.jsx:124-141 mergeBase() concatenates propActivities then fetchedActivities and only sorts when tradeEvents exist (:119-121 `if (tradeEvents.length === 0) return base;`). A 30-minute-old live transfer can sit above a 1-minute-old fetched sale.
findings.suggestion: Sort the merged list by time desc in mergeBase (or always take the tradeEvents path's sort).

findings.title: usePriceAlerts is instantiated twice (App level + inside the panel) — duplicate 30s stats pollers and duplicate alert toasts/notifications
findings.evidence: App.jsx:566 `usePriceAlerts(nfts.allTokens, addToast);` AND PriceAlerts.jsx:415 inside PriceAlertPanel (mounted at App.jsx:653). Each instance has its own fetchCollectionStats interval (PriceAlerts.jsx:58-71) and its own checkAlerts that fires `new Notification(...)` + addToast (:138-158) against the same localStorage alerts — when the alerts tab is open, a trigger fires twice. useSmartAlerts adds a third 30s fetchCollectionStats poller (useSmartAlerts.js:173).
findings.suggestion: Lift the hook into context (single engine) and have the panel consume it via props, mirroring how useSmartAlerts feeds NotificationCenter.

findings.title: "GAS SPENT" stat is a hardcoded 0.003 ETH-per-token fiction presented as data
findings.evidence: lib/portfolio.js:175 `const GAS_ESTIMATE = 0.003;` and :188 `totalGasSpent += GAS_ESTIMATE;` for every held token (including mints/airdrops); comment :91 admits "Estimate gas at ~0.003 ETH (typical NFT purchase gas cost)". Rendered as a primary red stat "GAS SPENT" (PortfolioTracker.jsx:336-340) with no estimate qualifier. At current sub-gwei gas an NFT purchase costs ~0.0001-0.0005 ETH, so this is ~10-30x off and stale.
findings.suggestion: Either fetch real gasUsed*effectiveGasPrice for the acquisition txs (Alchemy receipts) or label it 'est.' and derive from live gas price; don't charge gas for mints with no purchase record.

findings.title: Realized P&L FIFO matching can pair a sale with a buy that happened AFTER it; sells without a matched buy count full proceeds as profit
findings.evidence: lib/portfolio.js:216-229: for each sell, `sortedBuys.find(s => String(s.tokenId) === tid && !matchedBuyHashes.has(...))` — no constraint that buy.blockNumber < sale.blockNumber, so sell-then-rebuy of the same token uses the later rebuy as cost basis. When buy history (limit "100", :136) is truncated, `buyPrice = 0` → `realizedPnL += sellPrice - 0`. Also saleToEth (:47-53) assumes every fee amount is 18-decimals ETH — a USDC-denominated sale would be wildly wrong.
findings.suggestion: Constrain matching to buys with blockNumber < sale.blockNumber, mark unmatched sells as 'cost basis unknown' instead of zero, and check sale fee token symbol/decimals.

findings.title: API outage renders as "this wallet holds 0 NFTs" — fetchWalletNfts' error field is ignored by every caller
findings.evidence: api.js:610-613 catches and returns `{ tokens: [], totalCount: 0, error: "Could not load wallet NFTs..." }`. OnChainProfile.jsx:127-132 sets tokens/totalCount without reading `.error` → shows "This wallet does not hold any {collection.name} NFTs." + "Observer" badge (:566-571, :501-503); WhaleIntelligence toggleHolder :246-249 shows "No {collection.name} held by this wallet." (:812-822); PortfolioTracker :161-167 shows "No {collection.name} Found".
findings.suggestion: Check `data.error` in all three callers and render a retryable error state instead of a confident zero-holdings claim.

findings.title: 30s refresh re-resolves every no-ENS address against a hardcoded llamarpc endpoint, and the shared ens_cache uses a conflicting format that useEns prunes away
findings.evidence: WhaleIntelligence.jsx:363 `new ethers.JsonRpcProvider("https://eth.llamarpc.com")` (bypasses the app's provider failover; OnChainProfile.jsx:158 duplicates this). Only successful names are cached (:389-391 `if (r.status === "fulfilled" && r.value.name)`), so misses re-resolve on every 30s holders refresh (effect deps :409 `[holders, whaleTransactions]`, new arrays each poll) — up to ~45 lookups/cycle in batches of 3. Cache format clash: WhaleIntelligence writes plain strings into `ens_cache` while useEns writes `{name, ts}` and prunes entries whose `ts` fails `now - v.ts < CACHE_TTL` (useEns.jsx:28) — i.e., useEns wipes WhaleIntelligence's entries on startup.
findings.suggestion: Reuse resolveEns() from hooks/useEns.jsx (it dedups, caches misses, and shares format) and drop the hand-rolled resolver + hardcoded RPC in both components.

findings.title: Three always-on 30s pollers ignore document.hidden and duplicate the same stats fetch; WhaleIntelligence additionally re-pulls the full owner list every 30s
findings.evidence: useSmartAlerts.js:328-330 `setInterval(check, CHECK_INTERVAL)` (two fetches per tick) with no visibility check; PriceAlerts.jsx:69 same; WhaleIntelligence.jsx:225-228 polls fetchTopHolders+fetchActivity every 30s — fetchTopHolders calls getOwnersForContract withTokenBalances (api.js:562-565) which returns the ENTIRE owner set each time. Contrast: useActivityWebSocket.js:179 and useOpenSeaStream.js:239 both gate on `!document.hidden`, and useDmUnread.js:32 too.
findings.suggestion: Add the `!document.hidden` gate to all three, share one fetchCollectionStats poller, and lengthen the holders refresh (owner sets don't change at 30s granularity).

findings.title: Remote upsert fires on every keystroke of note/target inputs, and watched items not in the loaded token set vanish without explanation
findings.evidence: Watchlist.jsx:86-112 updateNote/updateTarget call `addWatchlistRemote(...)` inside onChange handlers (:199, :208) with no debounce. :114 `const watchedNfts = useMemo(() => tokens.filter((t) => watchedIds.has(t.id)) ...)` — a watched token outside the loaded gallery pages simply doesn't render; Favorites.jsx:70-74 has a "{n} favorited NFTs not yet loaded" hint, Watchlist has none.
findings.suggestion: Debounce remote writes (500ms) and add the same 'not yet loaded' counter Favorites has.

findings.title: "Reset Zoom" button visibility reads a ref during render — zooming doesn't re-render, so the button doesn't appear when you zoom
findings.evidence: RarityPriceScatter.jsx:746 `{zoomRef.current.scale > 1 && (<button ...>Reset Zoom</button>)}` while handleWheel (:574-589) mutates zoomRef and calls draw() without any setState — React never re-renders, so the reset affordance only shows after an unrelated state change (e.g. toggling a filter).
findings.suggestion: Mirror scale>1 into a small state flag (setIsZoomed) inside handleWheel.

findings.title: "Diamond Hands" claims are unsupported by data: badge is granted for whale-count alone; the health metric's "never sold" only looks at the last ~50 events
findings.evidence: OnChainProfile.jsx:496 `{isWhale && <Badge label="Diamond Hands" .../>}` — no hold-duration input at all. CollectionHealth.jsx:262-269 computes `sellers` from the merged activities feed (50-event window) yet renders "{count} never sold" (:493).
findings.suggestion: Gate the badge on actual hold time (acquisition timestamps already exist in lib/portfolio.js) or relabel to 'Whale'; relabel health copy to 'no sells in recent activity'.

findings.title: "Normal rate" alert setting is dead — the engine ignores config.listingRate.normalRate
findings.evidence: NotificationCenter.jsx:111 exposes `SettingInput label="Normal rate" ... onChange={v => handleField("listingRate", "normalRate", v)}`, but useSmartAlerts.js:293 computes `const normalRate = Math.max(1, Math.round((collection.supply || 10000) / 2500));` — the user-edited value is never read.
findings.suggestion: Use cfg.listingRate.normalRate when set, falling back to the supply heuristic.

findings.title: Top gainers and top losers overlap when fewer than ~6 tokens have cost basis — the same positive-P&L token can appear under "TOP LOSERS"
findings.evidence: PortfolioTracker.jsx:204-210: one sorted array, `topGainers: sorted.slice(0, 3), topLosers: sorted.slice(-3).reverse()` — with 1-3 priced tokens the slices overlap, and losers entries can render '+12.0%'-style positives under the red TOP LOSERS header (:558-569 renders pnlPercent unconditionally).
findings.suggestion: Filter gainers to pnlPercent>0 and losers to pnlPercent<0 before slicing.

findings.title: Refresh button is a no-op for up to 5 minutes — calculatePnL serves its localStorage cache, including a stale floor price
findings.evidence: lib/portfolio.js:122-124 `const cached = readCache(key); if (cached) return cached;` with CACHE_TTL = 5min (:11); the cached object bakes in floorPrice/currentValue. PortfolioTracker.jsx:299-309 'Refresh' calls loadPortfolio → calculatePnL → cache hit.
findings.suggestion: Add a forceRefresh flag that bypasses/invalidates the cache from the Refresh button.

findings.title: OpenSea stream events render uncolored lowercase raw type badges — EVENT_LABELS expects "ask" but the stream emits "listing"/"cancellation"
findings.evidence: eventFeed.js:61-66 and useOpenSeaStream.js:19-24 normalize to types "listing"/"bid"/"cancellation", but ActivityFeed.jsx:8-23 only maps sale/ask/bid/transfer/mint/trade — a live listing renders `{EVENT_LABELS[a.type] || a.type}` = grey 'listing' chip with fallback #666 color (:371-373) instead of the yellow 'Listed' style. Same gap in OnChainProfile.jsx:9-23 and WhaleIntelligence.jsx:1028-1032 (`tx.type === "ask"` never matches stream events).
findings.suggestion: Add listing/cancellation keys to the EVENT_LABELS/EVENT_COLORS maps (one-line additions in three files).

findings.title: Block cursor advances before the logs fetch succeeds — a failed eth_getLogs permanently skips that range's transfers
findings.evidence: useActivityWebSocket.js:126 `lastBlockRef.current = currentBlock;` executes BEFORE :128 `const logs = await fetchTransferLogs(...)`; if that throws, the next poll starts after currentBlock and the missed range is never re-fetched.
findings.suggestion: Move the cursor assignment after the successful fetch.

findings.title: Supabase votes are global across collections while the local fallback is slug-scoped (and writes are currently RLS-dead anyway)
findings.evidence: userdata.js:325-327 castVote upserts `{ wallet, token_id, week }` with no collection column (PK wallet,week per doc :73); getWeekVotes :352-355 selects by week only — voting in one collection overwrites/merges with another. The localStorage fallback paths are keyed `${slug}_votes` (:316-321).
findings.suggestion: Add a collection_slug column + composite PK in a migration and pass slug through, matching the local behavior.

findings.title: Profile drawer lacks the modal hygiene the rest of the app has: no Escape close, no focus trap, no scroll lock, raw unformatted price
findings.evidence: OnChainProfile.jsx renders a fixed overlay (250-280) with only click-outside close; EditProfile.jsx:30-53 has Escape + focus trap + lockScroll for comparison. Activity price renders `{a.price}` raw (:729) while every other surface uses formatPrice.
findings.suggestion: Add Escape/focus-trap/lockScroll (reuse EditProfile's pattern + lib/scrollLock) and formatPrice.

findings.title: New-DM input only accepts raw 0x addresses — no ENS name resolution despite useEns being loaded in the same component
findings.evidence: DirectMessages.jsx:389/398 gate on `/^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/.test(peerInput)`; typing 'vitalik.eth' can never open a thread, yet the component already imports useEns for display (:4, :160).
findings.suggestion: Resolve .eth input via the existing ENS infra before opening the thread.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback whale data shows with no 'example data' banner (ActivityFeed has one)
findings.evidence: api.js:584-593 returns FALLBACK_WHALES on API failure with fallback:true; WhaleIntelligence only drops the LIVE badge (holdersLive=false, :183) — the Top Holders list renders the canned wallets as if real. ActivityFeed.jsx:252-261 shows an explicit '⚠ Showing cached example data' banner for the same situation.
findings.suggestion: Add the same fallback banner when holdersLive/activityLive are false but data is present.

findings.title: No touch support for zoom/pan and 'scroll to zoom' microcopy on mobile; linear regression systematically flags rare items as 'underpriced'
findings.evidence: Only wheel/mouse handlers exist (RarityPriceScatter.jsx:574-657, wheel attached non-passive :679); project mandate is flawless iPhone/iPad. Trend math :250-262 fits price~rank linearly; NFT price-rank curves are convex, so top-rank items sit far above a straight line and everything near rank 1 reads 'overpriced' or the green zone hugs commons (DEAL_THRESHOLD :36).
findings.suggestion: Additively: pinch-zoom via pointer events + conditional microcopy; offer a log-price fit toggle for the trend line.

findings.title: isAuthenticated never flips when the token expires while the page stays open
findings.evidence: useSiweAuth.js:139-142 `useMemo(() => isSessionValid && !!authenticatedWallet && !isTokenExpired(), [isSessionValid, authenticatedWallet])` — isTokenExpired() reads localStorage but the memo only recomputes on state change, so a session that expires mid-visit still reads authenticated until the next remount/wallet change.
findings.suggestion: Add a timer that re-checks expiry (or recheck on visibilitychange).

findings.title: Quiet hours drop alerts entirely — they never reach the notification history either
findings.evidence: useSmartAlerts.js:129-130 `if (isInQuietHours(config.quietHours)) return;` exits before the history append (:145), so events during quiet hours are unrecoverable rather than just silenced.
findings.suggestion: Append to history (read:false) and skip only the toast/push during quiet hours.

findings.title: Browser notification uses bare `new Notification()` which throws on Android Chrome — the SW-based sendLocalNotification helper exists but isn't used here
findings.evidence: PriceAlerts.jsx:148 `new Notification(`${collection.name} Price Alert`, { body });` inside try/catch (silently dropped on mobile). lib/notifications.js:165-179 sendLocalNotification already does `registration.showNotification(...)` which works on Android.
findings.suggestion: Call sendLocalNotification here for cross-platform delivery.

findings.title: Row keys and stat-window labels: live rows keyed by array index; header stats reflect a 50-event window while the range selector implies 24h/7d/30d coverage
findings.evidence: ActivityFeed.jsx:368 `key={a.hash ? `${a.hash}-${i}` : i}` — index in the key defeats reconciliation as live rows prepend (re-mount + replayed entrance animations). Stats source is the 50-item page (api.js fetchActivity limit 50) labeled by the selected daysBack range (:186-194 vs :274-294).
findings.suggestion: Key by `${hash}-${token.id}` (the dedup key already used) and caption stats 'last N events'.

findings.title: UNIQUE HOLDERS sparkline is synthetic data (base += sales*0.1) presented as a trend
findings.evidence: CollectionHealth.jsx:282-292: `// Rough directional estimate only — not actual holder count changes` then `buckets.map(v => { base += v * 0.1; return Math.round(base); })`; rendered under the real holder count with only a hover tooltip 'Estimated trend based on sales activity' (:429-431).
findings.suggestion: Either store daily owner-count snapshots (like portfolio snapshots) for a real series, or visually mark the sparkline as an estimate inline.

findings.title: Stale doc-comment schemas: notifications.js header still shows the keys-jsonb/preferences schema replaced by migration 002; supabase.js/userdata.js headers carry superseded policy SQL
findings.evidence: notifications.js:15-25 documents `keys jsonb` + `preferences jsonb` + `"Anyone can manage own subs" ... USING (true)` while the code writes flat p256dh/auth via the proxy (:100-109) and 004:202 dropped that policy. supabase.js:77-79 still says 'Author identity is NOT cryptographically verified' below a header saying SIWE-verified.
findings.suggestion: Prune the dead SQL blocks; point at the migrations directory instead (these comments have already caused drift).

findings.title: Pending-message reconciliation matches on text+sender — sending the same text twice can drop one optimistic bubble; trade-attach banner reads a ref during render
findings.evidence: DirectMessages.jsx:194 `setPending((prev) => prev.filter((p) => !msgs.some((m) => m.text === p.text && m.sender... )))` — duplicate texts collapse. :602 `{pendingTradeRef.current && (...)}` renders from a ref; it only updates because handleSend's setText happens to re-render.
findings.suggestion: Reconcile by a client-generated id echoed through the proxy (or timestamp window), and mirror pendingTrade into state.

good: PortfolioTracker P&L crash IS fixed: PortfolioTracker.jsx:127 `const { ethUsd } = useTOWELIPriceOptional() ?? {};` with an explanatory comment referencing the 2026-06-11 prod bug — the tab no longer crashes outside PriceProvider.

Analytics wraps every lazy sub-panel (RarityPriceScatter, CollectionHealth, HolderAnalytics) in ErrorBoundary + Suspense with staggered skeleton fallbacks (Analytics.jsx:419-470), and is consistently honest about partial data ('X of Y loaded', asterisked percentages, 'Computed at runtime from N loaded').

lib/supabase.js fetchMessages distinguishes backend-unreachable (null) from genuinely-empty ([]) and CommunityChat renders distinct 'Chat Unreachable' vs 'be the first' empty states (supabase.js:174-181, CommunityChat.jsx:667-694).

DirectMessages is a strong messaging surface: optimistic sends with failed-state + retry, day separators, message grouping, read receipts, single-pane mobile nav via matchMedia, local block list, and an impersonation warning when a DM peer has no shared trade history (DirectMessages.jsx:490-499).

useEns is well-engineered: shared module-level memCache + pendingLookups dedup, caches misses (empty string) to avoid re-lookups, prunes by TTL and size cap, stale-guard in the effect (useEns.jsx:37-84).

Both stream hooks (useActivityWebSocket, useOpenSeaStream) are production-quality pollers: jittered intervals to de-sync rate-limit buckets, AbortController wiring, document.hidden pause + immediate poll on visibilitychange, TTL'd dedup maps, API keys kept server-side via proxies.
useHolderStatus uses a generation counter to discard stale async results across contract/wallet switches (useHolderStatus.jsx:56-103) — the correct pattern.

The supabase-proxy server layer is hardened well: JWT signature verification, jti revocation with fail-closed prod behavior, per-table body schema validation including author/wallet-must-match-JWT, bounded upstream reads, two-stage rate limiting, strict match-value charset (api/supabase-proxy.js throughout) — the fix path for the broken client writes already exists server-side.

RarityPriceScatter builds its tooltip with DOM APIs specifically to eliminate innerHTML XSS from NFT metadata (RarityPriceScatter.jsx:634-650), zooms toward cursor, is dpr-aware, and offers quartile averages + Pearson correlation + click-through to the NFT modal.

CommunityChat sanitizes input via DOMParser (tag-strip + entity decode) with regex fallback, has client-side spam patterns and a send cooldown, a reversible mute list with footer affordance, and a 200-message render cap with 'Showing the latest N' notice (CommunityChat.jsx:63-95, 492-496).
NotificationCenter: portal-rendered panel with outside-click + Escape close, role=switch toggles with aria-checked, aria-labeled bell with 99+ badge cap, per-category tabs.

ActivityFeed has honest data provenance: '⚠ Showing cached example data' fallback banner, three distinct empty states (apiEmpty vs apiFallback vs filtered), an OpenSea deep link when the indexer lacks history, chunked rendering behind Load More with an explicit mobile-perf rationale comment.
dm.js exports groupConversations as a pure function for unit tests, dedups by id belt-and-suspenders, and channel_key derivation matches the RLS CHECK exactly (sorted lowercase pair).
localStorage quota failures are guarded with try/catch essentially everywhere (chat, watchlist, alerts, ens cache, snapshots).

lib/notifications.js push flow was genuinely repaired (2026-06-11 comment): on-demand SW registration instead of hanging on .ready, writes through the SIWE proxy, passive isSubscribed check that doesn't force-register.
missingVsBestInClass: True background alert delivery: floor/whale/listing 'smart alerts' only fire while the tab is open (client-side 30s polling). The push_subscriptions + VAPID infra exists but only trade alerts use it — a Blur/OpenSea-Pro-grade product delivers floor and outbid pushes server-side.

Watchlist target prices don't actually alert: copy says 'set price alerts' but the target only paints a badge while the Watchlist tab is open — no wiring into usePriceAlerts, notification history, or push.
Chat history pagination: fetchMessages caps at 100 with no 'load older' affordance; DMs poll at 15s with no realtime channel, no typing indicator, no delivery state beyond a single read receipt.

No USD values in P&L per-token rows or analytics panels (only the two hero stats); no cost-basis method choice (FIFO/specific-ID), no P&L CSV export (Analytics has CSV export, portfolio doesn't), no per-token price-history chart despite fetchTokenSalesHistory existing in api.js.

No deep links/shareability for the analytics surfaces: profile drawer, alerts, and notification items aren't URL-addressable, and notification items aren't clickable through to the token/event they describe.

No real historical series: holder-count trend is synthetic, floor change uses sale-price proxies from a 50-event window — a Dexscreener-grade page persists periodic snapshots (the portfolio snapshot pattern already in the codebase) or pulls an indexer/Dune feed.
ENS-name input resolution (DM compose, watchlist/alert search) and ENS avatars in chat — the resolution infra exists but is display-only.
Canvas charts have no accessible alternative (no aria-label summaries or data-table fallback) and no pinch-zoom on touch, against the stated iPhone/iPad-flawless mandate.

No tx-simulation/preview or price-impact-style guardrails on the DM inline trade accept (it signs and executes after one confirm click; best-in-class shows a balance/approval preview first — TradesPanel may have more, but the DM card path is thinner).
